Elevation, transfer, split, merge, proxy grant, revocation and retirement require explicit authority decisions with identifiable basis; a step-produced authority decision cannot be re-acquired as though newly supplied. Direct/proxied decisions preserve source, subject, basis, acting identity/mode, scope, change class, disposition and supersession. Recording cannot widen a ruling. Proxy authority neither makes implementer self-review independent nor grants unrelated runtime/domain authority.
semantic.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS owns the complete authority-carrier and proxy-prohibition law; only supplied instances and table consequences are retained.

grounds.heading: IDENTITY/7. Default formats and overrides/Derived domain overrides

conditions: A bound runtime publishes identity defaults or a derived domain overrides them.
semantic.statement: Runtime defaults are lawful only while derived domains may override them. An override is lawful only if it preserves scoped uniqueness, explicit kind distinction, deterministic parsing/reading, family/member non-aliasing and stable downstream traceability. It is published in domain authority, not only hidden as implementation regex assumptions.

grounds.heading: IDENTITY/7. Default formats and overrides/Override publication surface
IDENTITY/7. Default formats and overrides/Override publication surface

conditions: A domain overrides defaults of its bound runtime realisation.
semantic.statement: The override is published on a lawful domain-authority surface, visible, auditable and recoverable without reverse-engineering implementation regexes. At minimum the domain should publish scoped kinds, their serialisation/readable form, uniqueness scope/hierarchy and grouping versus concrete executable/traceable identity distinctions.

exceptions: A family marker, display alias or prose heading may be first-class only when governing identity law declares it an identity of its own kind.
semantic.statement: Parsers distinguish concrete identity kinds from grouping labels. They do not promote family markers, display aliases or prose headings into executable/traceable identities merely from matching shape. Acceptance criteria, tests and similar subordinate identities do not collapse into requirement identity because their readable form derives from a requirement token. A domain needing family identities should explicitly publish requirement_family identities.
Object identity, release identity, publication/revision coordinates and mutable discovery selectors may relate but are not interchangeable; none grants another's authority.
semantic.uncertainty: RELEASE owns the detailed release identity forms.

conditions: Defining or auditing an identity surface.
semantic.statement: Ask all seven identity-surface questions: owner; kind; uniqueness scope; lifecycle stability; readability convenience versus over-trust; unambiguous family/member/alias/revision parsing; runtime/domain/release category. If they cannot be answered, the surface is under-defined.

Implementations should prefer typed readers, explicit kind distinctions and source-of-authority parsing contracts, and should avoid regex mining as the real model, silent family/concrete coercion and engine-grammar leakage into domain semantics. For a project relying on those patterns, the first lawful repair contains the immediate bug; the enduring repair publishes identity law and moves implementations onto it. This is the member's implementation policy, applied under project design authority.

conditions: A product is claimed to be built using ODD.
semantic.statement: Using ODD means building a GTL/ABG domain product with typed assets/nodes, named published graph functions bound into a GTL module, ABG-owned traversal governance/runtime facts/provenance/continuation/re-entry, bounded cooperative commands/services returning evidence and control, and visible state projected over constructive history. Documents, graph sketches or helper scripts alone do not satisfy that meaning; a hidden imperative constructive carrier leaves it not yet built with the profile. Automation must remain within lawful manual traversal of the same graph.

SPEC_METHOD supplies general constitutional goals/intent/product/requirements/design/re-entry law. ODD supplies graph-native structure and product shape, not domain semantics or the current local line. Domain methods supply semantic law; local INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md, requirements and design supply the ratified local line, with GTL surfaces included for graph-native software development. When WORLD_MODEL is also adopted, it governs world-model semantics, publication and composition. A source-described builder must acquire the product-specific method and local authority surfaces to build correctly; ODD alone is insufficient.
semantic.uncertainty: The referenced general/domain methods and actual product surfaces are not supplied.

conditions: A consumer selects an installed STDO distribution.
exceptions: A project-local copy is optional, not the default.
semantic.statement: Consumers select one complete immutable release, addressed by exact logical release URI and installed-manifest digest independently of machine-local store path. Mutable source governs no consumer before publication and explicit selection. Installed bytes must match the selected immutable RC; mutable source and moving selectors cannot silently repair, replace or outrank it. A mismatch is an adoption defect repaired by selecting/installing one complete released cut, never by mixing source and installed members; the selected release wins disagreement.
semantic.uncertainty: No installation or consumer basis has been inspected or qualified.

conditions: Work occurs within one declared ODD vector or edge traversal.
semantic.statement: The vector declares admissible external space; unconstrained internal solution path remains worker HOW. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify, but neither it nor the framework thereby executes or owns the domain's internal strategy. Worker output remains a candidate until evaluated and a report remains observation: the worker cannot close an edge, emit runtime events, mutate ledgers or decide re-entry. Neither worker nor human receives ambient authority from F_P/F_H classification.

conditions: A graph function refines a published outer vector into an inner workflow.
semantic.statement: Inner steps conserve the outer callable contract and every applicable invariant; each input satisfies its declared domain and preconditions. Earlier outputs are read only through the declared adapter/environment contract, and each published inner boundary is governed by the loop as the outer boundary is. Retained functions should declare requires/provides/carries. Changes to ACTIVATION §4, §11.8, the outer vector or any function environment declaration invalidate the binding until re-evaluated.
semantic.uncertainty: The full AC-016 and §11.8 laws are not supplied.

semantic.statement: Installed builder and target project remain distinct. The installed product must not assume prior knowledge of the target domain. A source-defined clean install proceeds from installing the ODD product to authoring target intent, definition, requirements and realisation root, then traversing its graph to produce target-domain outputs. This sequence is represented, not performed.

conditions: The installed released product helps build a subsequent version of itself.
semantic.statement: Self-hosting is lawful only while released installed builder and in-development product remain distinct, with distinct territories, authority surfaces, runtime state and project-owned specification/build-tenant surfaces. Automation, runtime resolution or qualification that silently merges them violates the profile.

grounds.heading: ODD/8. Responsibility layers and local binding

conditions: A capability layer is active in a concrete product.
semantic.statement: Each active layer should explicitly bind local typed assets/nodes, public graph-function carriers, required carried environment, proof/closure surfaces and projection/query surfaces; audits should distinguish shared law from local semantics. Copying another product's asset names without semantic need is accidental doctrine transfer, not method reuse. A prose-only capability lacking typed assets, graph functions and proof lanes is under-built.

conditions: A product is governed under ODD.
semantic.statement: Products should be audited against the profile. At minimum the audit should identify capability layer, local typed bindings, public constructive functions, proof/closure lane, projected/query state preserving ABG truth, any tenant orchestration replacing ABG continuation, and whether the execution-authority audit establishes ABG ownership of loops, invocation, supervision, retry, continuation, events and closure.

exceptions: Product-local work may remain local when it changes no shared structural law.
semantic.statement: Approved changes or clarifications of reusable structural law must update the profile. Uncovered moves must be evaluated as compliant, non-compliant or valid/worth incorporating. Incorporation is not fully approved until the profile is updated; non-compliance should be repriced, repaired or rejected. Grey work cannot silently enter the line. Usage, repetition and drift confer no shared approval; shared law is ratified in the profile and local law in product authority surfaces.

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is

exceptions: Existing projects and other ODD product types may use different layouts preserving the authority split.
semantic.statement: Read ownership strictly: one WHAT surface, one HOW relation, ABG runtime ownership and product domain-meaning ownership; stdo_<label>.json binds actual locations. reference_frame_bases carries evaluation-frame meaning. ABG Frame/attention/zoom/overlay frames remain runtime contracts and are not enrolled as evaluation frames by name. An evaluation frame may inspect a runtime frame as exact subject or coordinate without collapsing their identities.
semantic.uncertainty: REFERENCE_FRAME's full evaluation-frame definition is not supplied.

conditions: Assessing whether an ODD product is built correctly.
semantic.statement: Built-correctly status requires every §11 clause to hold. A failing or unestablished clause prevents that positive conclusion; unestablished is not thereby equated with falsified.
semantic.uncertainty: The supplied §11 text stops at §11.5C; no whole-profile conformance judgment is possible from this excerpt.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.1 Typed assets and nodes are explicit

semantic.statement: The product operates on explicit typed assets/nodes, not a hidden blob, giant mutable workspace object or undocumented service payload. Concrete assets must explicitly bind typed domain boundaries. Every actual produced/consumed boundary declares asset_surface.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.2 Graph functions are the primary constructive carrier

semantic.statement: Every operative constructive step has one named GraphFunction or one lawful graph-function composition. Its real carrier cannot remain hidden in orchestration loops, bespoke pipeline runners, controller scripts or service methods merely calling GTL-adjacent helpers.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.2A Outcome-first realisation order

conditions: Building operative ODD framework behaviour.
semantic.statement: Use edge traversal to build operative framework behaviour, in order: declare outcome traversal over typed assets; publish declarative GTL/ABG carriers; implement only remaining necessary minimal imperative adapters. Before implementation declare source/target types, edge/function name, closure/evaluation, lineage, ambiguity/gap obligations and allowed F_D/F_P/F_H bindings. Declarative structure comprises graph functions, typed nodes/vectors, operator/evaluator bindings, carrier schemas, policy/projection declarations and lineage ledgers. Imperative-first behaviour later described in GTL is ODD-shaped but not yet ODD-built.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.3 The function catalogue is published
ODD/11. Core law/11.4 The GTL module is the operative publication surface

semantic.statement: The live line must publish a machine-readable function catalogue; each retained function should expose at least name, inputs, outputs, intent and public/helper role. Prose/prompt-only callable surfaces leave the product under-built. Publish public carriers, traversed graphs, typed node/vector surfaces and bound semantic jobs/equivalent outer contracts. Publish live refined inner boundaries explicitly through lawful GTL surfaces; callers always bind the outer public contract, never hidden inner vectors.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5A ABG owns continuation and re-entry

conditions: An application operates over GTL/ABG.
semantic.statement: The application is cooperative, not a replacement runtime. ABG owns continuation, publish-boundary re-entry, graph-call lifecycle and graph step selection. Product code must not hold hidden continuation loops, multi-step controller memory across publish boundaries, locally infer later steps instead of ABG re-entry, make public next and graph-function continuation rival authorities, or otherwise replace ABG orchestration. Replacing ABG continuation with tenant-local flow leaves the application outside ODD-over-GTL/ABG behaviour.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5B Execution authority audit

conditions: An ODD product changes runtime, start/iterate, worker transport, actor invocation, process supervision, plugin dispatch, event projection, closure, assurance, retry or continuation semantics.
exceptions: A different runtime realisation is lawful only under an explicitly ratified, non-overlapping runtime scope.
semantic.statement: Before activation and closure, include an execution-authority audit proving exactly one authority for the affected traversal: the consumer-bound ABG realisation, including when that realisation itself is changing.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5B Execution authority audit

conditions: Conducting an execution-authority audit.
semantic.statement: Inventory at least all five authority surfaces. ABG owns selection/advance; invocation/supervision; retry/correction/continuation/re-entry; runtime events/append/replay/projection; and closure/assurance, with product policy/gain inputs. Product/plugin roles are declarations and policy inputs, actor bindings/prompts/payload/evidence adapters, bounded outputs and control return, admitted evidence payload mapping, and domain interpretation/evaluators/gap reasons/weights. Forbidden local substitutes include next-step runners; spawn/spawnSync/exec/timeout/kill/stdout-stderr supervision outside the ABG seam; retries/controller memory/hidden next; direct event append/side-ledger mutation/bypassing reconstruction; self-report or postflight closure. Include language/tenant-appropriate code, call-graph or static-surface review and name evidence ruling out hidden execution authority; artifact review alone is insufficient.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5B Execution authority audit

conditions: An audited surface admits a consequential entity transformation.
semantic.statement: ABG admission authority is then the graph-native specialisation of transformation admission completeness owned by ACTIVATION §4 and applied by DESIGN_MODULE. Broader ABG execution, supervision, retry and projection authority still derives from ODD and is not reclassified as admission authority. F_P/F_H remain the declared ODD projections of candidate-production/human-adjudication roles.
semantic.uncertainty: The complete enclosing-relation admission semantics are referenced but not supplied.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5B Execution authority audit

conditions: Any listed closure-preventing condition is present.
semantic.statement: Each condition independently prevents closure and leaves the product not currently ODD-correct over GTL/ABG: downstream start/iterate loop for ABG traversal; process supervision outside the ABG seam; retry/continuation/re-entry state outside ABG; runtime event/ledger mutation without admission; plugin output carrying next-vector/closure/invocation/process/event authority instead of evidence/policy; or two controllers able to claim one traversal. Utility does not remove this boundary.

Projections cannot redefine ABG facts or reconstruct alternate authority. Catalogue views reconcile to admitted module/public carrier; ownership/start-target views derive from or structurally compare against their admitted carrier; runtime views derive from ABG facts/events/replay/projection truth. Domain overlays fail closed on missing, stale or structurally divergent carriers. Same names with different inputs, outputs, vectors, declarations, ownership or closure law denote different truth surfaces until reconciled. Projection negative proof must include structural drift as well as missing truth.

conditions: Applying the source-described ODD constructive evaluation loop.
semantic.statement: Artifacts, reports, process success and liveness alone close no edge. Closure folds admitted evidence; workspace counts only through the ledger, and evaluation attends only to admitted ledger rows reachable through declared lineage. Every closure-relevant callout is admitted to immutable ledger/event log. Corrections append or supersede without rewriting and preserve corrected identity. Every closure decision and next-action selection is replay-reproducible from carriers naming causal predecessors. Model synthesis, gap discovery, next-action selection and action evaluation retain separate authorities; each design, ticket, module or proof names the function it implements or consumes.
semantic.uncertainty: Ledger fields, replay inputs and detailed A0–A16 contracts are absent.

conditions: Selected-outcome-bounded work is evaluated for continuation or closure.
semantic.statement: Each action binds current gap to exact target assets/obligations before invocation; only published lawful actions are ranked. The selected outcome bounds the loop. After a terminal condition, no further material work is selected without another admitted basis. Reprice requests constitutional re-entry and selects nothing. Lawful but undecided work yields control without failure classification, preserving the same edge and replay-visible resume basis; yield differs from retry, block and timeout. Edge closure is evidence toward Product acceptance, not acceptance.
semantic.uncertainty: The supplied table does not enumerate terminal conditions, full yield protocol or all repricing relations.

semantic.statement: Closure decisions form a closed sum type and evaluate_next is total. Every closure decision and audit outcome maps to exactly one core value for a named predicate, including cause when cause decides the value. Closure concerns an edge predicate; ACTIVATION disposition concerns acceptance; neither counts toward the other. Selection data has no core value because it decides no predicate. Typed no-action decides that no published lawful action can be selected and maps by cause; any preceding closure decision retains its own edge-predicate value. Product owns priority policy.
semantic.uncertainty: Seven closure decisions and the two no-action causes are referenced but not enumerated; no mappings beyond supplied audit mappings are invented.

conditions: Applying the foundation table's manual, negative-proof, installed-development or refinement-convergence rules.
exceptions: Dogfooding applies only to a product providing this profile's framework behaviour; installed-development decisive proof applies where an installable development form exists.
semantic.statement: Every automated move must be possible for an actor holding only declared surfaces; agentic artifacts take effect only through admission against deterministic criteria, and conformance evidence is not ratification. Negative evidence invalidates the real authority-bearing input on the supported path and demonstrates refusal before prohibited effect; manufactured refusal/event/gap/verdict proves nothing about that path, and source/package/install/runtime absence are distinct claims. Decisive proof uses an installable development form where one exists; isolation/proving-lane provisions remain recommendations. Refined inner chains close enclosing carriers only if outer contract survives fold-back and zoomed/unzoomed views agree. A live requirement without a proof witness keeps the enclosing carrier open until realised or owner-deferred/repriced out of the active branch. Scenario bundles should clarify boundary, assets, vectors, paths and closure evidence; products choose scenarios and appropriate witnesses.
semantic.uncertainty: Full manual sequence, negative-test mechanism, installed-development rule and zoom/scenario clauses are outside the supplied excerpt.

conditions: An actor enters ODD product construction.
exceptions: A product-specific domain method is acquired where one exists.
semantic.statement: The source-defined construction order acquires general method, applicable domain method and local authority surfaces before action; then declares graph carrier and loop; code comes last. The table attributes a fourteen-step sequence and two reading orders to the profile and retains 'usually' for consequences of skipping that order. This is interpreted workflow data, not an instruction executed here.
semantic.uncertainty: The fourteen steps and two reading orders are not supplied in full.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

exceptions: Further material work requires another admitted basis after a terminal or exhausted basis.
semantic.statement: Material work must remain within the selected outcome or an admitted bounded prerequisite/experiment. No further material selection occurs after outcome acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment decision resolution, another admitted terminal condition, or exhaustion/rejection/withdrawal/supersession/repricing-away/falsification of its basis or bound without another admitted basis. Reprice requests constitutional re-entry; it performs neither repricing nor successor-outcome selection. Graph/edge closure is evidence toward Product acceptance, never Product or release acceptance.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.statement: Every GTL/ABG ODD product must preserve one authoritative traversal-consequence surface: IntentLineage → ProductAssetModel → ObservationSnapshot → GapPressureRow → TargetObligationBinding → PriorityProjection → ConstructionIntent → AdmittedEvidence → EdgeFulfillmentLedger → EdgeClosureDecision → NextActionProjection, with selected outcome/admitted bounded-basis refs also feeding TargetObligationBinding. No CLI branch, prompt, postflight string, gap-dossier list, query, service or operator summary may rival it. Carrier renaming cannot alter this authority shape.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

exceptions: Libraries may be shared; authority may not.
semantic.statement: synthesize_model may update desired/known typed asset truth only from event-backed lineage, prior model and admitted product truth; it cannot observe worksite, admit intent, invoke, close or select work. eval_gap only observes and emits gap pressure; it cannot admit intent, invoke, close or choose work. evaluate_action only folds admitted action evidence into ledger and closure decision; it cannot select the next graph action. evaluate_next may bind obligations, rank lawful published actions and publish next-action projection, but cannot admit intent or decide prior-action closure/yield/failure/repair except by consuming admitted EdgeClosureDecision. Designs, tickets, modules and proofs must identify the specific implemented/consumed function rather than merely say evaluator.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop
ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

conditions: Before every constructive action invocation.
exceptions: The admitted prerequisite/experiment reference is optional when the selected outcome alone is the basis.
semantic.statement: Bind current gap, exact target assets, obligations, required roles and evidence refs to the exact selected outcome and any admitted prerequisite/experiment before invocation. A broad edge satisfies a specific gap only if the binding proves its lawfulness for those assets. External/bootstrap intent seeds the model but cannot invent unpublished actions. After evaluate_next selects an already-published function/vector, a distinct admission step admits construction intent synthesized against model and gap, citing lineage, selected action and preserving target-binding authority refs. An unpublished desired action yields typed no-action, never a broad-graph/script fallback.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.statement: Filesystem/process output, screen logs, worker artifacts and product files are observations, gaining authority only through typed evidence admission and folding into ledger/decision truth. W may change without being true; L may be true without containing all W. Closure and evaluation judge W only through L, and evaluator outputs affect traversal only after their own L/E admission. Every closure-relevant F_P callout needs admission; corrections append/supersede rather than rewrite history. Evaluators may attend only to admitted rows reachable through declared lineage, predecessor refs, target binding, policy and relevant event cursor; outside workspace facts, prose, archives, summaries and controller memory are excluded. Closure cannot follow raw artifact presence, worker report, process success or CLI summary. The fulfillment ledger records counts, obligation rows, materialization/liveness/admission refs and edge_converged; it never selects the next action.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

exceptions: Unresolved post_reprice must return no_action(undeclared) pending separately admitted constitutional re-entry.
semantic.statement: evaluate_next must be total. initial_selection uses current model/gap/binding/catalogue/policy. post_yield_resume resumes or yields the same lawful edge from replay-visible resume truth without failure classification. post_close_graph_continuation may choose the next edge or empty selection when complete. For post_retry/post_repair/post_reenter/post_block, select a higher-priority lawful action if one exists; otherwise follow the current edge if lawful; otherwise if authority is missing return a reprice-or-block typed no-action; otherwise block with typed no-action. These are selection outcomes, not evaluate_action closure decisions. Default following still passes through evaluate_next. Post-reprice work can be evaluated again only after separately admitted exact outcome/bounded basis enters new initial_selection or basis-bearing resume.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

exceptions: An earlier result stands for no-action only if it decided the same selection predicate on the current basis.
semantic.statement: Selected next action is invocational data, not a core result. Each typed no-action independently answers whether a lawful published action can be selected for this gap on this exact basis, retaining its domain outcome beside its core value. no_action(undeclared) maps to out_of_frame when catalogue lacks the action or no admitted basis declares a needed relation/capability/authority; it names the missing item and owner. no_action(basis) maps to invalid_basis when the current outcome/catalogue/policy cannot support the gap. On unresolved post_reprice, no_action(undeclared) names the undeclared outcome/bound and declaring re-entry. Prior closure results are selection evidence only and neither predicate's value counts toward the other. A next-action projection establishes availability only. Empty selection after a closed, complete graph is neither refusal nor selection determination.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop
ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

conditions: Closure results use admitted evidence and exact edge basis.
exceptions: For re-enter or block with both undeclared and basis causes, record both and take the basis value.
semantic.statement: Every closure decision is replay-visible with sufficient basis/reason refs. close→satisfied when admitted ledger evidence fulfills exact-basis obligations. yield→indeterminate when the edge stays lawful and admitted progress/waiting does not decide, with resume basis naming what would decide. retry(defeated)→falsified only when admissible evidence defeats this attempt while the action stays lawful; all other retry is retry(undecided)→indeterminate, naming the deciding re-attempt. Repair requires coherent governing relation/basis/binding and a local defect permitting repair of the same edge: repair(implementation)→falsified for admitted implementation failure with failing obligation counterexample; every other repair is repair(proof)→indeterminate with repaired proof needed to decide. re-enter requires upstream asset/governing-relation change: undeclared needed relation/capability/authority→out_of_frame, naming it and its owner; otherwise unsupporting/stale/substituted/unrepairable basis→invalid_basis. reprice→out_of_frame for an undeclared selected outcome/bound, naming it, owner and requested constitutional re-entry. block(undeclared)→out_of_frame and block(basis)→invalid_basis when the action leaves the edge unable to proceed for the respective cause. Cause comes from reproducible basis/reason refs and adds no decision or core value.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.statement: Do not combine candidate availability, edge fulfillment, next-action selectability or candidate acceptance as each other's results. Closure repair is not ACTIVATION local_repair, and re-enter is not re_enter: proof repair is indeterminate versus local_repair falsified; undeclared re-entry is out_of_frame versus re_enter invalid_basis. In ODD §§11.5D, 16 and 19, disposition denotes a closure decision or, for typed no-action disposition, evaluate_next selection, never ACTIVATION §3 disposition. RELEASE §9 owns successor-claim dispositions. Repair/re-entry realization is a published graph action chosen by evaluate_next from admitted closure truth; evaluate_action's conceptual disposition does not itself invoke it.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.statement: Yield requires the same edge/attempt to remain lawful, admitted progress/waiting, replay-visible resume basis and control return without failure classification. It preserves the current edge for long-running, bounded or partially productive work and is not retry, block, timeout or a local CLI loop. Liveness alone cannot establish semantic failure, closure, requirement non-satisfaction or retry(defeated). It can support yield or interruption.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

conditions: For every closure decision, next-action selection and governing admitted/replay-derived carrier or projection.
semantic.statement: Reproduction must use RuntimeEventLog, execution basis, event-backed IntentLineage, ProductAssetModel publication basis/event refs, selected outcome identity/admitted bounded refs, GapPressureRow, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog, admitted evidence, ledger, closure decision, NextActionBasis and visible policy refs. Inability to reproduce signals hidden state. Each governing carrier must carry causal predecessor refs: outcome/bounded refs→binding; lineage→model→gap→binding→priority→selected-action projection→construction intent→evidence→ledger→closure decision→next-action basis→post-action projection. Both projection occurrences must be predecessor-reachable; the latter also uses fresh eval_gap. Construction intent preserves authority refs. Reproduction must be reachable without external joins; a broken chain fails replayability.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

exceptions: Intentionally opaque internals remain one bounded action and may compute an internal result with local control flow.
semantic.statement: Each published inner-vector boundary must obey all four functions with its own visible model, gap, binding, action, evidence, ledger, closure and next-action projection. Opaque internals may not publish, dispatch, retry, repair, re-enter or close graph work as a hidden traversal controller. ABG owns runtime truth/replay, graph-call lifecycle, actor/process supervision, continuation and re-entry mechanics. Product owns domain asset/catalogue meaning, gap interpretation and priority policy. DESIGN_MODULE tier 3 governs realization modules inside this split and may not fragment eval_gap/evaluate_next/evaluate_action into module-local authorities.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

conditions: For any ticket, design, code module or proof touching the four functions, traversal, gap evaluation, selection, intent, worker invocation, evidence admission, fulfillment, liveness, closure, re-entry, public query or live proof.
exceptions: Unchanged accepted relations cite their accepted basis and are not proved again.
semantic.statement: Causally applicable axioms and the constitutional equation control acceptance for the selected outcome and affected published boundary; they authorize no horizontal realization growth, new Product work or outcome widening. Local checklists, test names, source-grep checks, CLI summaries and implementation notes cannot weaken them. A locally complete ticket leaving a rival traversal-consequence path requires lawful re-entry, keeping the gap as blocker, or separately bounded paydown under an independently selected outcome/prerequisite. Correctness requires the next-work decision to derive only from the equation, with U=(selected outcome, optional admitted bounded basis) causally reachable through binding and intent. The equation projects lineage, synthesizes model, observes gap, binds U, evaluates initial selection, distinctly admits intent, invokes and admits evidence, evaluates action, refreshes model/gap/binding, derives post-action basis and evaluates next; unresolved post_reprice returns typed no-action.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.statement: Gap dossiers, postflight/assurance reports, materialization manifests, liveness projections, run summaries, worker prose, screen/PTY transcripts, prompt packages, harness target arguments, source-grep tests, CLI output/branches, queries/gaps views and service outputs provide only evidence, diagnostics or read-model context; none independently closes an edge, selects work or routes retry/repair/re-entry. The admitted ledger/decision/projection chain prevails over conflicts; without it there is no constitutional edge closure or next-action selection. Public query may render read-only eval_gap/evaluate_action/evaluate_next outputs but cannot append events, invoke workers, admit intent, run evaluate_action or choose traversal itself.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7 Manual walkthrough must still be lawful

semantic.statement: Automation must stay true to the manual process, which an operator using only declared surfaces should be able to follow. It cannot skip undeclared nodes, fabricate authority, collapse multiple constitutional transitions into an opaque step without declared refinement, depend on implementation-carrier knowledge the installed product should lack, or merge installed-builder and development-product authority during self-host work. Inability to explain manual traversal means automation is not yet method-safe.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7A Conforming agentic development
ODD/11. Core law/11.7A Conforming agentic development

semantic.statement: Agents work from the smallest sufficient declared packet with source refs, not stale memory or wholesale hidden context. Compression is prompt input, never deciding authority; generic derived frames may orient precedence/re-entry/traceability but product behavior must come from current Product authority. Produced work must have correct change class, traceability and admission. Tickets, change classifications, design derivations and execution contracts must pass existing SPEC_METHOD/TICKETS admission: deterministic, fail-closed and naming violated rules, never treating a drafted classification as automatic truth. F_P reasons/drafts/proposes; F_D decides artifact conformance. A passed admission and completed walkthrough are conformance evidence, not ratification; repeated use cannot amend shared method or constitutionalize grey work.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7A Conforming agentic development

semantic.statement: A walkthrough stopping point is a method defect only when a competent, correctly configured agent using declared authority still cannot decide because an owning surface has ambiguity, a missing step, contradictory authority or undecidable change class; reprice that defect into its owner. Ignored authority, stale memory or bad reasoning is agent error instead; malformed artifacts are rejected either way. Process-followability proof is independent of automated runtime: external API overload or transport failure cannot prove process soundness, because runtime availability and process validity differ.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7B Real authority-path negative proof (STDO-UP-010)

conditions: The specified identities apply to the boundary.
semantic.statement: Negative proof must not manufacture the refusal, blocked event, gap or verdict being tested. The supported path is public entry → admitted GTL composition owning topology → named GraphFunction callable contract → implementation/plugin limited to admitted seam → ABG traversal/event/continuation/replay truth → replay projection → typed Product outcome/continuation. CLI, SDK, service, adapter, plugin, fixture, query and projection cannot become rival controllers. The consumer chooses the concrete test/evidence mechanism; the section fixes the property it must prove.

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.8 Cumulative environment law is mandatory
ODD/11. Core law/11.9 Global convergence must be stable under zoom

exceptions: A live requirement without an executable witness stops holding the enclosing carrier open when realized, explicitly deferred or explicitly repriced out of the active branch.
semantic.statement: Published graph functions must obey cumulative-environment law rather than last-output-to-next-input wiring; explicit requires/provides/carries declarations remain a should. Local green arcs alone do not establish global closure: refined chains must lawfully close, preserve coarse contracts and agree across zoom. Live current requirements lacking appropriate executable proof keep the enclosing carrier open subject only to realization, explicit deferral or explicit repricing out of the active branch.

conditions: Installed proof applies where an installable development form exists; mandatory graph-function construction applies where the product provides ODD framework behavior.
semantic.statement: Direct source checks do not replace decisive isolated installed-dev proof. Developing the product through its own graph-native method is recommended generally. Building provided ODD framework behavior through ODD graph functions is mandatory; publishing ODD-shaped artifacts after imperative execution decided the work is prohibited.

conditions: Any listed failure is sufficient for violation of this profile.
semantic.statement: Violations are: a claimed step lacking node/vector; function lacking clear outer contract; automation not describable as manual traversal; installed-product dependence on authoring-carrier knowledge absent from clean targets; scenarios unable to name significant proving paths; closure without target-relative evidence; wiring bypassing cumulative environment; zoom disagreement; service-owned operative transition lacking published function outcome contract; workspace-first framework orchestration labeled GTL afterward; imperative closure/continuation/semantic-target movement/lineage truth outside declared graph-function, ABG or Product carriers; hidden execution authority in product/plugin for traversal, actor invocation, process supervision, retry, continuation, runtime events, projection or closure folds; flattening lawful yield into retry/block/timeout/local waiting/hidden CLI loop; query/postflight/service/operator decisions outside the constructive loop; or inability to follow the constitutional process end-to-end from declared authority, or acceptance of a constitutional artifact without deterministic admission.
semantic.uncertainty: The agentic inability condition is read with §11.7A's explicit distinction between qualified method defects and agent error.

semantic.statement: Outcome traversals precede declarative GTL/ABG structure, which precedes minimal imperative adapter code. The invocation sequence cannot be replaced by imperative scripts later relabeled GTL, graph functions used as documentation wrappers or service code acting as hidden carrier. The canonical compression owns no determination; a differing source section decides.

conditions: An LLM is ramping into an ODD product.
semantic.statement: The LLM should quickly recover: semantic source-to-outcome chain; typed domain assets/nodes; public functions; catalogue and GTL locations; ABG/Product ownership split; projection/query lane; each projection's admitted source and structural-drift fail-closed behavior; proof execution authority has not escaped ABG; constructive loop; closure vocabulary and replay-visible yield; capability-closing proof surfaces; outer carrier kept open by live unproved requirements despite inner green lanes; and whether an agent can follow declared authority alone with deterministic artifact admission. If these cannot be answered quickly, the product is not yet sufficiently ODD-shaped.

Posts carry provisional, investigative, comparative, argumentative or unratified content. Live requirements, live design decisions and active process law belong in applicable bound WHAT or ratified design surfaces and must not be carried as posts. Location, visibility and Closed state cannot confer ticket, Product, requirement or design authority.

Each post uses one listed category and the base template, with a MATRIX decision table replacing central free prose. It must identify current reality, target direction or both; separate findings from recommendations; support claims with exact file/requirement refs; avoid presenting itself as ratified; preserve closed history against stealth rewriting; and concern one bounded subject. Its subject should be short, specific and stable enough for later scanning. Default file carriers use the prescribed timestamp/category/subject filename; non-file carriers must retain equivalent identity/history fields. Status explicitly records discussion state.

Post content becomes consequential only through explicit adoption into bound WHAT, ratified design or accepted implementation. Closing a discussion is not adoption. Carrying incident/review evidence or proposing reusable method change does not adopt it; STDO-UP-012 propagation remains governed by SPEC_METHOD §6.

exceptions: A directory may contain multiple definitions only when it contains multiple distinct product WHATs.
semantic.statement: Publish exactly one JSON definition per distinct current WHAT; additional tenants of the same WHAT are entries, never additional definitions. A definition identity may persist across successive releases; forks, replacements or independently governed WHATs require another definition_id. Immutable Product/release identities remain separate. Product-definition, immutable Product, bounded-context and tenant identity URIs remain subject to IDENTITY and owning authority; URI, filename, path, label or proximity creates/widens no identity or authority. Relative refs resolve from retrieval URI, not assumed source-project proximity. Overlay/schema/template own only locator/relation shape, never referenced content.

conditions: For every Product Definition.
exceptions: product.bounded_context is null if no separate enclosing context is claimed; sprint bindings are optional.
semantic.statement: Each definition contains product identity/display name/source locator/explicit enclosing context or null; constitution.stdo source repository, mutable discovery selector and exact installed basis/deterministic manifest digest; every non-STDO set in additional_authorities; basis-qualified entrypoints; agent_bootstrap entrypoint and marker-managed targets; local axioms/overrides/disambiguations with owner/target/basis/scope and applicable context resolution; one or more accepted reference_frame_bases with authorities/scopes; current what Intent/Product/specification bindings; how shared surfaces and one or more independent tenants; ticketing Goals/tickets/comments/optional sprints; explicit composition; $schema and kind=stdo.product-definition. Repeating source truth in JSON is non-conformant rival authority. product.bounded_context identifies only enclosing WHAT context, not an exhaustive registry or flattened subordinate/peer/composed/tenant/user/runtime namespace; local disambiguations name their exact contexts.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/1. Overlay and layout independence/Foundation to law: binding a project to the method

conditions: The family consequences use the declared instance premises, not foundational commitments alone.
semantic.statement: F12 consequences preserve project-owned WHAT and layout without becoming part of the method; one locating definition per WHAT without repeated content; separate definition/Product/release/tenant/project identities and explicit verified composition; exactly one applicable discovered definition or fail closed; complete constitutional sufficiency without entrypoint replacement or design-invented Product meaning; one exact complete immutable release verified before use, owner acceptance of exact change plans, and fail-closed unverifiable state with prior state kept/recovered; exactly one context-qualified material meaning after authorized resolution; imports preserving owner meaning and authority, with changed applicability rebound and missing meaning/adoption/authority reported before reliance; Product-admitted frame engagement with availability/adoption/activation and frame/actor/lineage identities distinct; one tenant registry and separate Goals/ticket/comment authorities; one owner per law, members governing together as one release, source-condition/digest-preserving derived surfaces stale on source change, digest equality proving identity not fidelity; and bootstrap from the selected release template into existing surfaces without a rival local method root, with initial requirements from any legitimate constitutional input. Each consumer applies only its owner's rule. Widening Product scope to executable tool/runtime/realization requires separate explicit human authorization.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed foundational standing, referenced rule implementations and external consumer loci are not supplied.

semantic.statement: The complete governing set must collectively recover all five dimensions for its scope. constitution.stdo.basis locates one complete immutable RC cut and exact installed manifest, never a selected subset; additional_authorities locates every additional set/source. Each entrypoint names its resolving basis and cannot narrow/replace the set. Product-meaning ontology belongs in or is cited by bound WHAT. Accepted realization design ontology has semantic-design authority only for its boundary, derives from WHAT and applicable methods, and cannot invent missing Product meaning.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager
PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

semantic.statement: Canonical plan hashing uses UTF-8 JSON, recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF endings and one final LF. Basis-only Adoption Plans exclude machine-local installation paths/status; fleet plans order by deterministic discovery path. Complete update uses the same serialization but additionally binds physical destinations/preimages and selected cohort/routes/source observations. Already-installed status changes neither its digest nor authority. Digest possession alone never grants operation authority; mutation requires explicit acceptance and exact re-derivation.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

semantic.statement: Only constitution.stdo.basis.uri and manifest_sha256 author STDO selection; transport repository and mutable channel selector do not. Every manager-owned component from configured store root downward must be a physical directory or regular file of declared type. Symlinks, junctions, reparse points, devices, sockets, other redirections/special entries fail closed. Verification inventories all entry types including directories, rejects entries not derived from exact manifest file paths and never follows unmanifested aliases. No cache, registry, checkout, alias, schema or agent file may silently replace the selected basis. Every case-insensitively parsed stdo: schema locator must name that same immutable cut before schema loading.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

semantic.statement: install admits one explicitly named immutable RC without changing definitions. sync installs/verifies only the selected exact basis and never consults selector. adopt --dry-run resolves annotated selector/immutable RC and presents cut/tag/commit/tree/manifest/current-definition-byte/plan digests without mutation. Mutating adopt requires exact prior plan acceptance, re-derives before installation, installs only bound target, rechecks definition bytes and atomically changes only basis and basis-relative schema; drift refuses. status/verify/list/manifest/resolve are definition-read-only. Fleet adoption requires accepted aggregate digest over every per-definition plan and whole-selection authorization for all writes; nesting implies neither composition nor inheritance. Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag/commit or manifest mismatches, missing/extra/changed members, ambiguous discovery, unaccepted/stale plans, URI escape, redirected store, undeclared entry types or malformed markers fail closed.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

semantic.statement: agent_bootstrap embeds no other constitution; it names one basis-qualified entrypoint and marker-managed discovery blocks in local instruction files. Targets are portable relative paths resolved against product.source_project; absolute paths, parent traversal, redirection and escape fail closed. Fleet source projects stay within the explicitly authorized fleet root and every target is preflighted before first write. Replace exactly one correctly ordered marker span, preserving all outside bytes including trailing whitespace; append preserves old bytes as exact prefix. Bootstrap only routes to definition/exact basis/owners. Recursive discovery prunes exact names .git, .hg, .svn, .bzr, .venv, venv, node_modules, vendor, site-packages, build, dist, out, target, .gradle, .tox, .nox, .cache, .ruff_cache, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, __pycache__, .genesis and .stdo. A discovered definition cannot itself be a symlink. Pruning is not proof that excluded trees lack independently governed Products.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

exceptions: Newly staged immutable installs may remain unused after refusal/failure.
semantic.statement: cohort-update first presents the complete plan without consumer effects; exact accepted plan is re-derived before mutation. Verify selected cohort dependency closure and each companion definition/release record/admitted members before reliance. Stage absent immutable installs, verify existing ones without in-place repair and preflight every consumer target. Changes are restricted to selected basis/schema, existing composition locators/contracts and selected native/install links; historical installs and unrelated content remain unchanged/available. No consumer-local checker, Product meaning change or local semantic-map change is created. adopt/sync/fleet keep their narrower contracts. Caller explicitly selects every native route and derived context; empty selection means selected none, not semantic absence.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

semantic.statement: For every selected derived context, missing/ambiguous/changed/unavailable program, map or source evidence holds the whole update before consumer effects. Only the source owner performs semantic re-entry; the manager cannot relabel old maps current. Source freshness proves integrity, not semantic conformance/verdict. After staging, recheck consumer preimages and source evidence; report completion only after verifying every selected resulting binding/companion. Pre-effect refusal retains prior state; caught application failure restores affected preimages and reports no completion. Application requires exclusive consumer write scope. No cross-path crash atomicity is claimed; process/host loss or unavailable rollback requires preimage recovery before claiming the complete relation.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

conditions: For operations with an intended external write effect, including install, sync, mutating adopt, fleet adoption and complete update.
semantic.statement: For 'intended effect occurred', completed→satisfied requires evidence of the entire effect. Refusal before any effect with retained prior-state evidence is not_effected→falsified and ended. Caught application failure is also not_effected→falsified: the complete update fell short and no later part is applied, regardless of rollback verification. Verified restoration establishes the effect's end; unverified restoration or unavailable rollback leaves the end unestablished, recorded as a residual naming needed verification without changing falsified. Name unused newly staged installs as the part that did occur. Abrupt process/host loss without a caught failure establishing shortfall yields completion_unknown→indeterminate, never completed or not_effected. Reconcile unknown completion or unestablished end from presented preimages before repetition or complete-relation claims.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

semantic.statement: Refusal also answers whether the operation may apply its effect on its exact subject/basis. Before commencement this is admission/activation; afterward it is construction availability. Missing exact-plan acceptance or fleet whole-selection authorization is missing operation authority: admission_refused(authority)→out_of_frame, naming required acceptance/authorization and owner. Every other refusal listed by the source has a basis cause, including byte/preimage drift, stale plan, ambiguous discovery/no exact subject, integrity failures, path/locator/marker boundary failure and deficient derived evidence: admission_refused(basis) before beginning or re_entry_requested(basis) after, both invalid_basis, naming failed coordinates and applicable source owner. Commands without intended external effect have no Effects result; refusals still map by cause. A verify finding of a missing/extra/changed member is falsified for its own predicate, not a refusal. Refused/failed/unknown operations must not be combined as completed; known caught failure with unverified restoration must not be called undecided; missing acceptance must not be called defective basis.

conditions: For every material term occurrence.
exceptions: An owning document/section/schema field/operation may explicitly declare a context for subordinate occurrences, avoiding repeated qualifiers when resolution is unique.
semantic.statement: A context exists only through owning-authority declaration of stable identity, owner, selected basis and semantic scope; a consumer defines inside it only through explicit owner relation. Resolve by scope/nearest explicit context, then exact basis/applicable authorities, then admitted local definitions/imported refs, then all applicable authorized overrides/disambiguations, admitting only one remaining concept. Equal spelling/capitalization/shape/location/nesting/actor/implementation establishes no equal meaning, identity, equivalence, inheritance or authority; differing spelling proves no difference. Filename, heading, index, glossary, schema value, URI, repository, prompt, actor or proximity cannot accidentally declare context. Relations require the semantic address or explicit authorized relation.

conditions: Zero or multiple applicable concepts remain at a material boundary.
exceptions: A dependent evaluation returns indeterminate where admissible evidence also cannot decide the claim and supplies that ground; otherwise the undeclared selecting relation grounds out_of_frame.
semantic.statement: Zero concepts is unresolved meaning; multiple concepts is ambiguous meaning. Both fail closed for agents, designs, schemas, implementations, tests, translations and reviewers; none may choose by familiarity, frequency, recency, nominal match or context-free glossary fallback. Dependent evaluation names the missing definition/import/disambiguation relation and owner and returns the grounded out_of_frame or indeterminate outcome, not false. Glossary is only a locator to exact context-declaring/concept-owning clauses; it defines neither, repairs no declaration and supplies no shared default. Its indexed concept applies only through the selected semantic address or explicit target import.

conditions: For every cross-context relation.
semantic.statement: Require explicit owner authorization and a carrier naming exact source/target concept refs and context identities; kind; direction and material lawful inverse; preserved/changed meaning, loss/refusal conditions; both semantic owners without authority transfer; both selected bases; scope/provenance; lifecycle/invalidation. The owner is distinct from the owning clause resolved by a concept reference. Meaning change/narrowing/loss cannot be called import. Equivalence needs governing-authority equality, not spelling or opposite translations. Disambiguation neither equates concepts nor imports by itself. No kind widens authority. Specialisation additionally specifies exact target, preserved/narrowed meaning, excluded source instances and absent/lawful inverse; its label alone establishes nothing. The source relates these kinds to AC-012 without making that reference an executed calculus operation.

Each local axiom/override/disambiguation must name decision URI, existing lawful authority, applicable overridden clause/resolved ambiguity and exact scope; file category or overlay listing grants no authority. Disambiguations additionally require exact lexical term, context identity, complete material candidate refs, resolves_to as one of those candidates, every selected semantic basis, and uri/authority/applies_to. Cross-context candidates require the resolution-owning carrier's complete import/translation/equivalence relation. Empty arrays explicitly bind no entries of that kind; omission is not equivalent.

reference_frame_bases is nonempty; every entry locates an accepted declaration, all lawful admitting authorities and exact governed Product/context/tenant/outcome/other scope. The referenced declaration, not JSON entry, owns frames, method/profile basis, outcome, binding rules, envelopes, grants, triggers, coverage, results and invalidation; the entry adopts no profile and creates no authority. Availability comes from cut inclusion, adoption only from Product authority and activation only from exact authorized actor/subject work instruction. Activation mutates no overlay; no agent registry, permanent frame assignment or temporary active configuration is persisted there. Frames and actors remain distinct, with no grant arising from actor name or broad frame beyond cited owners/exact activation. A domain/runtime carrier called Frame enters the collective set only through explicit declaration with required evaluation/authority relations.

conditions: The governed outcome crosses a chain of Products.
semantic.statement: The frame basis records a Product-role map distinguishing mutable source projects, definitions, candidate checkpoints, cuts, released Products, installs, artifacts and dependent Products; each development-product role binds an exact install identity. Each directed composition edge names source/target roles, authority/contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and invalidation. Common actors/repos/files/implementations/outputs/tools create no composition or identity. The starter templates/PROJECT_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS_TEMPLATE.md is non-authoritative; adopting it requires replacing every placeholder with exact identities, owners, scopes, sources, grants, results and invalidation conditions and admitting the completed declaration under existing authority.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/8. WHAT, HOW and work carriers

exceptions: Specification may cite multiple surfaces; sprints are optional.
semantic.statement: Intent and Product each have one canonical WHAT entrypoint; specification may locate multiple requirement/specification surfaces. Canonical how.build_tenants entries carry stable identities and root/design/implementation locations; an optional TENANT_REGISTRY.md is only companion/projection, never another identity/location authority. Common realization law requires explicit adoption across more than one tenant. Ticket lanes minimally include backlog, active and completed. Goals own work-wave truth, tickets own ticket state and comments remain commentary. This member binds locations, while SPEC_METHOD §4/TICKETS select the carrier for a particular work item.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

conditions: A Product scope is requested.
semantic.statement: Select exactly one applicable definition. Zero applicable definitions or several unresolved definitions fail closed; refuse a symlinked definition.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

semantic.statement: Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition or constitutional override; parent and child definitions remain independent until explicitly composed. Resolution verifies locator and expected target identity. Movement requires a locator update without identity change; replacement by a different identity at the same locator fails closed. Edges binding exact immutable Product or release versions also carry and verify those identities in their relation and contracts; a mutable definition identity cannot substitute.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

conditions: A discovered set claims conformance.
semantic.statement: Every definition validates against its selected released schema; every required URI/fragment resolves within declared workspace/resolver boundaries; every product.definition_id is unique; every build-tenant identity is unique within its overlay; every governed scope has a resolvable applicable frame basis and overlapping bindings are reconciled by cited authority. Every local disambiguation binds one exact term, target context, complete material candidate set, selected concept, authority, basis and scope; resolves_to belongs to disambiguates and the referenced resolution carrier is congruent. Every material cross-context term seam uses explicit import, disambiguation, translation or equivalence, not nominal matching. Every composition target is another definition with the expected ID, and every relation and non-empty contract set resolves. No two carriers claim authority for the same Product, tenant, ticket state or constitutional relation.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

exceptions: Schema uri and uri-reference formats assert syntax only when the declared validator implements format assertion.
semantic.statement: Conformance explicitly checks RFC 3986 URI and URI-reference syntax using an assertion-capable validator, then separately checks resolution, fragments, selected-release identity, cross-file uniqueness, constitutional sufficiency, semantic resolution, cross-context-relation completeness and authority congruence. Structural validation is not semantic conformance.

conditions: No explicit cross-context relation is supplied.
semantic.statement: Frame: evaluation frame and consumer runtime carrier remain distinct; spelling cannot enrol the latter. Owner: specialist evaluation family and semantic/decision owner remain distinct without authority transfer. Product: immutable release and mutable definition remain distinct and selection uses the occurrence's declared context. Tenant: build realisation supplies no default for hosted/customer/account/runtime/data tenancy. User: Product role, person, principal, account, actor, operator and data subject remain unresolved until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates applicable meanings.
semantic.uncertainty: User is expressly unresolved, not false or interchangeable.

semantic.statement: A positive local case declares one context and resolves exactly one concept; a positive cross-context case supplies the complete authorised relation. Negative cases include zero candidates, remaining multiplicity after disambiguation, selection outside candidates, context-free glossary fallback, incomplete coordinates, authority/basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidation. Correct downstream behaviour based on guessed meaning does not pass. CONFORMANCE may index but cannot redefine these cases.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

semantic.statement: Derived surfaces cannot become selectable partial constitutions or reinterpret owners. Within scope they preserve applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision owners and invalidators, including a prohibition's condition and lawful alternative even with correct digests. Compression cannot strengthen or weaken a relation. References must resolve within declared actor access; otherwise supply required meaning directly.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

conditions: A released cut or installation carries a derived surface.
semantic.statement: Each carried derived surface records paths/digests for every deciding source and watched index. Any such digest change makes it stale; installation may treat it as current only after regeneration or explicit re-acceptance. Raw owning members of the same selected cut decide questions a stale or insufficient carrier cannot decide. Matching digests alone do not establish semantic preservation.
semantic.uncertainty: ACTIVATION §2 owns the general staleness and standalone-scope laws; EVALUATION §7 supplies additional digest/qualification context not supplied here.

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

exceptions: A concrete form is method law when explicitly accepted by the method as an interoperability boundary, as claimed for the definition schema and template in §1.
Separate explicit human authorisation can authorise executable or consumer Product scope.
semantic.statement: Maintain method/consumer ownership separation. A shared-method amendment alone cannot establish an executable tool, workflow engine, runtime, assurance system or consumer realisation as STDO Product scope. Recording a ruling cannot widen its subject, implication, authority or change class. Mutable source may author a future cut but cannot silently govern consumers; publication authority belongs only to a released version.

exceptions: An explicitly bound and verified project-local exact copy is lawful, but is not the default and cannot be selected by proximity.
semantic.statement: Mutable methodology authoring resides in its own source workspace and governs a future candidate only. Released authority is the exact consumer-selected immutable version; installed distribution defaults to the manager's shared store and matches basis URI/manifest digest. Project constitutional authority is at what bindings; realisation/work at how and ticketing. Create no competing local methodology root and do not bind mutable or partial source as the immutable release. The resolved installed basis remains operative until explicit consumer adoption of another cut.

conditions: Following the source-described bootstrap sequence.
exceptions: Local axiom, override and disambiguation collections may be explicitly empty.
The sprint root is optional.
semantic.statement: The ordered sequence is: (1) install manager once, resolve one version-line selector and explicitly select one immutable RC; (2) install the complete cut and retain deterministic manifest digest; (3) copy its exact template to the named/default definition; (4) assign stable mutable-WHAT definition ID, source-project locator and bounded context, distinct from every immutable Product/release ID; (5) bind constitution.stdo.source, non-operative selector, exact basis URI/digest, additional authorities and basis-qualified entrypoints, confirming collective axioms/ontology/epistemology/taxonomy/semantics; (6) bind bootstrap entrypoint and portable targets relative to resolved product.source_project, preflight every target and install/refresh only marker-bounded discovery blocks; (7) bind or explicitly empty local axiom/override/disambiguation collections; (8) bind at least one accepted collective frame basis, admitting authorities and exact scope; (9) confirm/write Goals, run goals→intent→product and bind Intent/Product; (10) gather/derive/classify/bind live requirements without a co-equal rival; (11) bind at least one tenant with root/design/implementation and any shared realisation law; (12) bind Goals, ticket lanes, comments and optional sprint root; (13) explicitly bind every known composition edge with target ID, relation authority and non-empty contracts; (14) validate shape, assert URI syntax, synchronise/verify basis, resolve every URI and perform identity/composition/sufficiency/congruence checks.
semantic.uncertainty: This records the sequence as data; referenced §§3–8 and manager procedures are not fully supplied.

conditions: A bound requirement set has become the live constitutional surface.
semantic.statement: No rival monolithic requirements document should remain co-equal authority with the live bound set; this recommends clear, derivable, non-monolithic truth without prescribing a folder.
semantic.uncertainty: The concluding source uses 'should'; the bootstrap sequence separately says to bind without creating a co-equal rival.

exceptions: Core traversal records/F_D/F_P/F_H and generic ASSURANCE module are not restricted by this boundary.
semantic.statement: Profile/realisation-owned graph, edge, vector, ledger, event log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, IACS and Prime do not enter tiers 1–2. A profile may bind core mechanisms to them through its declared binding. Worked applications, hello worlds and data mappers remain external test subjects; their particulars cannot become generic functionality by precedent.

conditions: A profile uses generic core concepts/families or refines another profile.
semantic.statement: Import every used tier-1/2 concept under FOUNDATIONS §2 and every generic family on which profile rules rest; restate none of the owner's rules. The FOUNDATIONS §3 family-table premise column names each imported family ID and its table section; profile rules rest on its consequences with their stated standing. Imported rules/choices retain owners. A refining profile declares refinement in its lead and owns only additions; added choices must not be presented as foundational consequences.
semantic.uncertainty: Exact import and family-table laws are referenced rather than supplied in full.

exceptions: Tier-3 profiles are constitutional method members when a project selects them.
semantic.statement: Tiers 1–2 constitute method members, with selected tier-3 profiles. Each clause identifies foundational commitments. Owners state the method in full; guides/excerpts create no additional authority. Task frames copy owner sections byte for byte, record source digests and own no determination; digest mismatch makes them stale. ACTIVATION §2 owns when to read a frame or its owner sections.

exceptions: An explicitly bound and verified project-local copy remains possible, but is not the default.
semantic.statement: The manager installs each complete immutable cut once in a shared versioned store and resolves logical release URIs. Definitions name basis by logical URI and manifest digest, not machine-local path. Installed-byte authority depends on exact cut, basis URI, digest and member inventory. Neither mutable head nor moving selector silently replaces consumer basis. Included calculus theory remains separate from subject models/encodings; the optional occurrence profile neither changes calculus nor selects a consumer; GLOSSARY never defines a shared default.

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit

conditions: Within the reference-frame-evaluation context under its exact publication basis.
exceptions: Other members/products may import or specialise relations under their own authority, without entering or amending this member.
semantic.statement: This member governs finite actors' bounded reasoning/execution contexts over changing work only. It defines no application profile, role mapping, Product frame-basis binding, domain product, specification taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption relation or assurance implementation. Same-spelled profile/product/role/runtime carriers are not imported by proximity or nominal match.

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit/Imports into this context

semantic.statement: Each declared import runs from its named source member to the frame context with no loss, ownership transfer or authority grant. Imported concepts are not defined a second time; local refinements name and map back to their owners. Profile/Product frame specialisations retain those owners and are not thereby imports into this member.

No finite actor is presumed to hold the whole workspace actively. Useful frames are finite and sufficient for their declared family; evaluation determines attention. Human authority may select practical sets without a unique mechanical partition. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate or succeed; hierarchy is optional, and joint use need not compose coordinates. Coverage is relative to declared workspace/outcome/inventory/basis/time. Breadth, usefulness, actor or technology grants no semantic/operation/decision authority. A second independently released project requires qualification before either next cut.
