semantic.uncertainty: The exact-shape requirement is read together with the expressly conditional alternative-spelling provision in Naming.

conditions: An immutable cut is published in a shared release source.
exceptions: The canonical root locator is . alone; at repository root the project-subtree tree equals the repository-root tree.
semantic.statement: Bind namespace/owning Product authority, exact qualified ref/annotated tag object, peeled commit/repository-root tree, normalised repository-relative subtree root and its exact Git tree, declared member inventory/release claim bytes, and §9 predecessor/successor dispositions. Subtree root is a locator within exact commit, not Product identity: slash-separated exact tree-entry bytes with no leading/trailing slash, empty component, . component or .. component, except . alone for root. Moving source changes locator and cut identity without namespace reassignment. Commit tags confer no sibling membership; inventory/digest alone without qualified ref, commit, subtree root/tree is not complete reacquirable identity.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/2. Release identities/Historical ref and public-URI conservation

conditions: Project qualification or namespace transition.
exceptions: An additional archival ref may preserve reachability of the same historical tag object.
semantic.statement: Qualification is prospective: preserve historical unqualified ref names, objects, peels and public links; never recreate/reannotate/move/replace historical tag objects. Product-local names and stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/ remain unchanged; project-qualified transport refs do not enter the logical URI. Resolution binds exact historical/qualified ref and fails closed if one project-local coordinate names distinct tag objects. Latest spans greatest positive ordinal over that project's historical and qualified cuts. First qualified publication creates qualified selector; old unqualified selector remains at its object, stops being current for shared source, and is not force-moved to imitate the namespace.

Three phases: mutable candidate construction; immutable RC publication with monotonic selector advancement; exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption. Publication immediately advertises highest ordinal; acceptance is a verdict on that RC, not a second final cut/carrier. Any byte capable of affecting Product or release-scoped claim requires publication and review of a higher immutable RC.

conditions: Candidate construction precedes RC publication.
semantic.statement: Mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers. Before publication make intended Product boundary, release claims, excluded source state and qualification basis explicit. Reprice material scope change rather than silently absorbing it.

conditions: Publishing an immutable RC cut.
exceptions: Atomic push is conditioned here on transport support; coordinated cohorts impose mandatory atomicity separately.
The release branch is optional.
semantic.statement: In order: confirm triaged scope/lawful constitutional re-entry; declare exact Product subject/claim set; reconcile release-facing assets; run proportionate pre-RC qualification/operator checks; commit exact carrier; resolve/record namespace/subtree root/tree; in shared source create annotated immutable cut and annotated selector over same commit; atomically push carrier, RC branch, cut, selector and optional release branch where supported; remotely verify cut/selector/release branch resolve to highest published RC commit; record ref/subtree/identity/inventory evidence for reacquisition without mutable checkout. Tags never move. Increment RC ordinal on same line when applicable; bounded repair alone need not increment minor version. A higher published RC without matching selector advancement is invalid/fail-closed and cannot justify older-cut latest resolution.

conditions: Qualifying or accepting an RC.
exceptions: Artifact presence can establish presence when presence is the exact claim.
semantic.statement: Bind namespace, qualified immutable ref, annotated tag object, peeled commit, repository tree, subtree root/tree, member set, claim bytes, Product/release basis, each property/observation boundary, evidence subjects, owner verdicts/gaps and complete predecessor-successor relation. Evidence must match claim: source success proves neither packaged nor installed behaviour; packaging equivalence proves no semantic behaviour; artifact presence proves no usability except exact presence claims. Acceptance requires completed required exact-cut review/operator checks and human acceptance of exact subject. A qualifying-byte change leaves verdict on old RC and requires higher cut. Acceptance neither moves/rewrites selector nor creates final carrier.

conditions: Advancing a version-line selector for one namespace.
exceptions: Release branch updates apply only when that optional carrier is used.
Atomic transport push is conditioned here on transport support.
semantic.statement: Identify exact new cut/tag/ordinal/peel; confirm no higher ordinal; confirm selector absent or at lower ordinal on same project line; atomically create/force-update annotated selector to highest commit; align optional release branch; push complete carriers/refs atomically where supported; remotely verify highest peel and matching annotated immutable tag. Refuse missing matching annotated cut, existing higher ordinal, backward move or selector/release-branch misalignment. Forward movement is strictly ordinal-monotonic; repair defects with higher immutable RC, never moving old cut or rolling selector back. Selector means rc.latest; concrete RCs remain addressable.

conditions: Resolving a channel or adopting its selected cut.
exceptions: A consumer may explicitly retain an older exact URI/digest using exact-basis operations such as sync, not a latest channel.
semantic.statement: Selector answers only highest published cut, never consumer governing basis. Require annotated selector and distinct peeled commit; missing peeled ref fails closed, not lightweight fallback. Enumerate namespace RC tags including preserved historical ones; select greatest positive ordinal; require cut and selector annotated and peeling to same commit; fail closed for lag or other target. Refuse same-line channel target below current exact basis. Separate read-only presentation from mutation: bind current definition bytes/basis to exact target/tag object/peel/tree/manifest digest, emit deterministic plan digest, require operator acceptance of that exact digest, and rederive before any definition change. Selector/target/manifest/definition drift invalidates acceptance. Fleet acceptance binds aggregate digest over exact per-definition plans. Planning within mutation cannot self-authorise.
semantic.uncertainty: PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns unavailable hashing details and command boundaries.

conditions: Naming refs in a shared release source.
exceptions: Unqualified naming only under single-project or historical-conservation conditions.
Alternative spelling requires the expressly qualifying ref policy.
semantic.statement: Short shapes are rc/<project>/<version>, <project>/v<version>-rc.<n>, optional release/<project>/<version>, and <project>/v<version>. The example project/3.0.0 names illustrate successive rc.1/rc.2 with one latest selector; they do not allocate a namespace or identify actual releases.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject/Release-scoped assets

conditions: An RC uses release-scoped surfaces.
semantic.statement: Possible surfaces include release notes, release/installed-distribution manifests, dependency declarations, package/installed-carrier metadata, qualification receipts and branch/tag identity declarations. Reconcile every used surface to exact RC before publication. Any post-publication change to those bytes creates another candidate requiring higher RC. Selector adds no Product bytes and has no reconciliation phase. Exact version/RC identities belong in release carriers and consumer basis bindings; live constitutional version-label usage is governed by SPEC_METHOD's surface rule.
semantic.uncertainty: The complete external specification-surface rule is not supplied.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/6. Release-scoped assets and the Product subject/Product subject and repository carrier

conditions: Before qualification and after immutable publication.
semantic.statement: Before qualification declare namespace/exact subtree root, exact Product member set or artifact, release claim surfaces, and co-located mutable source fields excluded from both. Commit co-location confers no Product membership; subtree tree and inventory delimit subject. Published RC admits no post-review carrier delta. Publication-caused tickets/source bookkeeping go afterward on continuing source branch and cannot move the cut.

conditions: A cohort is explicitly declared.
exceptions: A stale derived index may remain immutable history, but not accompany changed source as current cohort.
semantic.statement: Every required member uses exact <version>-rc.<n> suffix: cut/ref rendering adds v, embedded asset version does not. Qualification normalises only this leading marker and requires exact suffix equality. Equality establishes matching only, never Product/member/tag/acceptance/authority identity. Missing, stale, differently versioned, other-source-cut or nonreproducible source-member/digest closure makes cohort incomplete. Any covered source-member change invalidates old derived candidate for successor; regenerate, mechanically validate, independently qualify where required and release index under same new cut name.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/7. Coordinated release-matched asset cohorts/Two-commit construction and one publication transaction

conditions: Constructing and publishing a coordinated STDO cohort.
semantic.statement: Avoid tag-identity/derived-byte self-reference with ordered construction: A freezes corpus/plugin/release record/qualification bytes; create annotated STDO cut locally over A without push; install/verify exact local cut to obtain manifest identity for every derived Product/index; B freezes Axiom Indexer, STDO Representation, semantic index and cohort record; qualify B against exact local STDO tag before child tags; prepare annotated child cuts and all Product RC/selectors/optional release branches; mandatory post-tag/pre-push qualification checks every local tag object/peel, selector, RC/release branch, normalised version mapping, target commit and closed ref set, fetching/binding expected remote OID or absence for every destination; one atomic transaction publishes only qualified carrier branch and complete Product refs.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/7. Coordinated release-matched asset cohorts/Two-commit construction and one publication transaction

conditions: Publishing or remotely verifying a coordinated cohort.
exceptions: Later bookkeeping commits are allowed without moving immutable cohort tags.
semantic.statement: Refuse remote lacking atomic publication; no sequential fallback. Immutable tags are create-only with bound remote absence. Every mutable carrier/RC/selector/release ref uses explicit per-ref compare-and-swap lease in same atomic transaction. Missing expected ref, unexpected tag or changed OID stops publication; refetch and repeat full content/local-ref-graph qualification before another push. Never substitute unguarded force, partial push or in-place expectation update. Remote verification fails closed for any required ref absent, lightweight, differently versioned, wrong Product commit or selector/release-branch mismatch.

grounds.heading: RELEASE/7. Coordinated release-matched asset cohorts/Qualification and recovery

conditions: Cohort qualification, recovery or change to cohort law.
exceptions: Historical same-version backfill only under separately authorised recovery law naming that exception.
semantic.statement: Content qualification binds exact A tag/manifest, B source tree, all Product target refs/version markers/inventories/index bytes/full source digest closure, establishing tagging requires no qualifying-byte change. After refs exist, local-ref qualification binds annotated objects, peels, targets, exact push set and all remote expectations/absences to unchanged content result. Post-publication verifies same relation remotely and refuses partial cohort. Authorised backfill must retain exact historical cut/name and complete remote set; it cannot move tag, add Product bytes or claim original atomic existence. Normal successors use atomic process. Adding/changing cohort law changes qualifying bytes and governs only a higher RC containing them, never retroactively an earlier cut.
semantic.uncertainty: No separate recovery law is supplied.

conditions: An RC is considered for acceptance.
exceptions: Independent exact-cut review applies where required.
Release-blocking gaps may be addressed by explicit claim-scope narrowing.
Retained evidence satisfies a gate only under the external validity conditions.
semantic.statement: Acceptance may occur when pre-RC qualification passed for declared subject; required independent exact-cut review passed; required operator review completed; intended scope/successor relation stable; release assets accurately describe cut; every release-blocking gap, including EVALUATION §5 promotion blockers, closed or scope explicitly narrowed; and human Product authority accepted exact immutable RC. Each is mandatory regardless of selected post-change checks. Acceptance binds immutable identity and neither advances nor rolls back selector. Consumer adoption separately evaluates channel's exact latest target and mutates only after digest-bound plan acceptance.
semantic.uncertainty: External promotion-blocker and retained-evidence validity criteria are not supplied.

conditions: A release claim depends on an external backend, transport or operator-facing service.
exceptions: The claim may be narrowed before acceptance instead of qualified against a healthy dependency.
semantic.statement: A dependency may remain outside Product for carrier/migration classification and still block dependent claim. A clean skip due to unhealthy dependency is unperformed evaluation with no result; correct classification does not establish capability passed. Qualify with healthy dependency or narrow claim before acceptance.

conditions: A successor evolves predecessor semantic claims.
exceptions: Earlier conserved evidence may be reused when owning text and carrying consumer bindings are unchanged or the change demonstrably does not affect the claim.
semantic.statement: Identify exact immutable predecessor; origin remains fixed for candidate. Every potentially affecting predecessor claim receives one semantic disposition. Retain/reassess evidence under change-impact law. Conservation compares same material case, scope and authority, must/may/prohibited outcomes, absent triggers/exceptions/prerequisites, owning text and consumer bindings, with discriminating counterexamples. Patch absence is not loss if successor-native behaviour is preserved; naming/code similarity is not conservation evidence. Indicative wording can bind; replacing must/shall alone neither conserves nor supersedes. Preserve obligation/preference force and every exception/scope condition. Package-wide equivalence proves no individual claim. Earlier conserved records predating this test must be reevaluated before qualification, remaining unresolved until then. Unresolved disposition blocks affected-claim qualification as a planned assessment without closed result; qualification records core value with each asserted disposition predicate, never treats disposition label as result.

conditions: A maintenance or support line may affect retained claims.
semantic.statement: Release basis names watched source, observation boundary, inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive semantic disposition at material integration and exact-cut qualification. Consumer owns record, branch strategy, comparison and proof mechanism. EVALUATION §5 owns acceptance requirements on the record and applies this section rather than becoming part of it.

Treat specification as constitutional source, enabling re-derivation, audit and correction under explicit authority. Declarative bias is a should: primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence surfaces for lawful derivation/realisation. Imperative procedure remains subordinate to declared authority. Constitutional examples use neutral capability/authority identities to demonstrate capabilities; consumer particulars are not precedent that becomes method law.
semantic.uncertainty: PROFILES §1's complete boundary is external.

semantic.statement: Method owns process constitution; goals current overriding work concerns; intent domain direction; product-definition current mutable source-project definition; requirements live obligations derived from it; shared/tenant-local design concrete mechanisms. Product definition binds actual authority locations and tenant registry realisations under shared specification. Bound WHAT alone defines WHAT; design/realisation define HOW. Tenants, design, code, definition overlays and derived surfaces never become co-equal with WHAT. Conventional GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md and specification/requirements/ require no relocation/duplication. Structured requirement families are preferred to an imperative monolithic catch-all; location itself is not constitutional.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed binding and registry laws are external.

semantic.statement: Four named areas do not make their owning members independently selectable or reduce the released Product to four members. Consumer authority remains one complete immutable released cut with exact member inventory.

exceptions: Ambiguity blocking/escalation is policy under declared risk appetite except hard-stop prerequisite failures.
semantic.statement: The canonical statement routes each clause to its owner and decides nothing independently. Every Product publishes a layout-neutral routing definition locating constitution/local decisions/collective frame bases/WHAT/independent tenant HOW/work/composition, not rival truth. Material terms resolve under bounded context, owner, selected basis and scope; spelling creates no cross-context meaning/authority; explicit imports/translations/equivalences/disambiguations govern seams; zero or multiple applicable meanings fail closed. Requirements cover capabilities, guarantees, governance and verification; design records structural HOW. Major boundaries reduce lawful interpretations and explicitly detect ambiguity. Implementations never replace constitution. Scenarios supply end-to-end proof where capability claims need it. Design derives from requirements, requirements from goals/intent/product, code from requirements/design. Iteration cumulatively reprices; events/projection/delta reveal drift. Every live requirement family has design ownership, classification and downstream closure or explicit deferment; every design record grounds in requirements; shipping behaviour traces authority. Live surfaces change through supersession/withdrawal, never silent mutation. New intent follows real cases and gap analysis. Sprints price proof cost and force close review; they are no authority layer or concealment of drift.
semantic.uncertainty: Several owning sections and hard-stop definitions are not supplied.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Foundation to law: chain, outcome and build-tenant binding

conditions: Applying F10's owned-layer, layered-surface and realisation premises.
exceptions: Explicit deferment may substitute for downstream closure.
Multiple conformant realisations may satisfy a layer.
Explicit version labels may identify immutable release facts, selectors or clearly historical/superseded material.
semantic.statement: Declared specification governs; realisations/overlays/views realise, locate or project without co-equal authority. Each live requirement needs owning design decision and downstream closure or explicit deferment; behaviour traces authorising requirements/design and broken trace is drift. A layer is sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer; derivation failure is an upper-layer defect. Unconstrained realisation choice belongs to design. Live constitutional surfaces are versioned history changed through supersession/withdrawal, never in place; current truth uses present tense, not version labels denoting recency. Use-exposed inexpressible constitutional conditions reprice the deficient surface or remain recorded governed debt; unanswered lifecycle phases remain recorded gaps. F10 identifies requirement categories/statuses, ADR fields/lifecycle/storage, Gap:/Unanswered: markers and conventional chain layout as domain choices, not consequences supplied by commitments alone.
semantic.uncertainty: Exact category/status values and detailed ADR/lifecycle rules are outside this excerpt.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Foundation to law: chain, outcome and build-tenant binding

conditions: Evaluating progress, closure, lineage or realisation shape under F10.
exceptions: Negative proof is needed where drift is plausible.
Realisation-shape recommendations are scoped to boundaries governed by the design profile.
semantic.statement: Progress is judged against one selected directly verifiable outcome per work wave; evidence evaluates but cannot select/enlarge/replace outcome. Growth requires admitted basis and ends with it; regression/unresolved gap blocks promotion only on affected path. Closure evidence includes authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift plausible, and remaining open pressure, under external TICKETS/EVALUATION/ASSURANCE laws. Lineage objects remain distinct and consumers select one complete release; reusable method change retains one authority relation from evidence to realising consumer. Method terms resolve in declared bounded context. Under governing design profile, semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth with explicit edge effects; higher-order/effectful boundaries require explicit composition/effect algebra without mandatory vocabulary. Admission carriers, evidence categories, eight-step adoption chain and mechanics are expressly allocated policy/domain choices.
semantic.uncertainty: Full progress categories, growth admission, adoption chain and design-profile rules are external.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Foundation to law: chain, outcome and build-tenant binding

conditions: A build tenant binds obligations to a realisation.
exceptions: Only an obligation's owner can weaken it by changing WHAT at its owning layer.
semantic.statement: Different means may realise the same obligations; obligations decide fitness. Executor kind neither accepts nor rejects a realisation, human performance is not adjudication, convenient stack weakens nothing, and structural representation validation does not prove correct execution. Binding divides requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment, chosen as tenant design. Identify operations, outcome values mapped to core, resource measures/units/boundaries and obligation-required limits so finite actors can evaluate them. Calculus may serve wherever its laws hold regardless of executor. Multi-tenant development mechanics belong to project law. Construction steps, data meaning and execution remain three separate accounts; mappings state and discharge preservation under ACTIVATION Refinement and AC-013 when recorded in a_c, with joined accounts and environmental evidence owned by tenant binding.
semantic.uncertainty: Full §11, resource-limit law and three-account definitions are not supplied.

exceptions: Projection need not replay a complete event stream if retained record is sufficient for Product obligations.
Design chooses where/how required surfaces are realised unless the path itself is constitutional.
semantic.statement: Every chain link is owned and load-bearing; absent repricing path, unowned requirement, ungrounded design or code without design decision creates accidental law. ADR is a durable design record, not another constitutional layer. Code/Events/Projection are binding-selected responsibilities across software/human/mixed realisations, not universal codebase/event-store requirements. Goals keep temporary work focus out of deeper layers until intentional repricing. Present-tense Product Definition bridges direction to requirements, naming source-project terms/boundaries; it is neither immutable cut nor installed Product. Requirements state mandatory truth including capabilities/invariants/constraints/governance/verification, not merely visible features. Design chooses mechanisms, interfaces/topology/placement/carriers/entry-control/runtime wiring/lawful tenant boundaries; requirements may mandate delivered surfaces without deciding placement unless path is constitutional. Constitutional insufficiency re-enters at change-class-named layer.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed change classes and §11 binding rules are only referenced.

exceptions: Transitional paths may remain as explicitly retained compatibility features.
semantic.statement: The method requires full constitutional requirements, code derivable from requirements/design, narrowing at major gates, evidence through scenarios/tests/events/projection/delta, and specification repricing when reality exposes a constitutional gap. Authority stays directional during iteration. Current operative truth is present-tense; obsolete transitions are erased subject to the compatibility exception. Derived artifacts, indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views are read models, never constitutional truth. Failure of these commitments excludes the spec-driven designation. Declarative truth/boundaries over imperative procedure remains a preference.

conditions: Any listed failure holds.
semantic.statement: Work is not spec-driven if a competent team cannot derive conformant intent from goals, product definition from intent, requirements from product, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; if any live requirement lacks explicit status, category, owning design decision, or both downstream realisation and explicit deferment; if code lacks requirement/design authority; if a live constitutional domain artifact is rewritten in place; if a capability lacks operational evidence; if triage attributes discovered drift to constitutional source that is not repriced; if major boundary ambiguity is neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or if a material product/module/function/application/runtime surface/capability has neither declared lifecycle signal nor recorded gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement questions.
semantic.uncertainty: These are exclusion conditions, not an independently sufficient acceptance test.

semantic.statement: Specification-drivenness requires ordered reconstructability. Boundary failure is an upper-layer defect: goals unclear/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for the bounded wave; intent vague/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for realisation; product underspecified/contradictory/insufficiently decomposable; requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by accidental implementation detail; or design incomplete/ambiguous/insufficiently operational for code. ADRs/design documents are load-bearing. Sufficiency depends on ambiguity governance; accepted relations may be reused only on exact basis after applicability/invalidation checks. A local selected function's span excludes rebuilding the whole product. The litmus neither waives the design profile's material-change gate nor requires recreation of unchanged accepted views.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed sufficiency, reconstruction-span and design-profile rules are externally owned.

conditions: A real use case, including scenario, deployment or external review, pressures the current model.
semantic.statement: Explicit gap analysis identifies what the constitution cannot express. A constitutional gap, distinguished from missing implementation, re-enters at its change class's layer and flows forward through that class's layers. New goals/intent arise only where work-wave focus, direction or scope changes; intent emerges from concrete, repeated real-use pressure, not abstract speculation or ad hoc coding pressure. Requirements/design refine cumulatively, code is repeatedly re-derived, and implementation/testing/replay/scenario gaps feed repricing without reversing authority.

exceptions: Optional realisation detail may appear in intent when itself constitutional.
Explicit version labels are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings, or clearly historical/superseded material.
semantic.statement: Preserve each layer's role: goals do not replace requirements, intent excludes optional nonconstitutional implementation detail, product is not release notes, requirements carry explicit acceptance and material lifecycle obligations/gaps, and ADRs are not a second requirements surface. Live constitutional wording is present-tense current truth at its declared affected boundary; dead law is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary, even during migration. Recency alone does not justify version branding. Before treating a downstream artifact as complete, check the whole affected span for clear class, lawful re-entry, layer derivability and agreement among active intent/product/requirements/design/qualification; otherwise the gate stays open.

exceptions: Upstream constitutional constraints bind choices; constitutional necessity may require specific filenames, placement, paths or packaging.
semantic.statement: Requirements specify required control/delivery surfaces; design chooses mechanisms, including stack/carrier/runtime and tenant execution binding unless upstream already constrains them. Agent-facing requirements may require authoritative bootstrap/control surfaces carrying bare axioms and routing to the canonical method; design chooses entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or other lawful topology. Hardcoding filenames/placement without constitutional necessity absorbs design detail and impairs re-derivation.

conditions: The design profile governs the realisation boundary.
semantic.statement: Semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth, with explicit effects pushed to the edge. Meaning requiring inspection of orchestration, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults indicates excessive imperative coupling. Readability, modularity and honesty about meaning/effects are required. A boundary composing higher-order functions or effectful computation requires explicit composition/effect algebra with applicable identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws.
semantic.uncertainty: The applicable algebra and profile-adoption rule are referenced but not fully supplied.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Requirement categories and classification

semantic.statement: Every live requirement family has explicit header Status and Category; either missing makes it incomplete. All four categories remain constitutional, not priority or user-facing labels. Scenarios validate capability meaning; not every requirement should become a marketed feature. Requirements should avoid premature concrete realisation choices; nonconstitutional path/filename/packaging choices belong to design. Every inherited/legacy requirement is classified: Deferred remains explicitly not-yet-operative/realised with honest deferment and no current-closure claim; Superseded transfers ownership and requires Implements/Supersedes in its governing design record; Active requires an owning design decision to be written/updated; Orphaned is removed or explicitly superseded. Nothing live remains unclassified.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Requirement categories and classification

semantic.statement: Requirement lifecycle/category/legacy classifications, evidence kinds, migration old-path classes, inherited-material classes, carry_across/redundant/rewrite, ADR statuses and change classes are declared states with no core-value mapping. They are never combined as evaluation results; evaluations return their own predicate-specific core value. Active/material advance does not mean satisfied; Deferred/Orphaned does not mean falsified.
semantic.uncertainty: The complete core-result algebra is outside the supplied source.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Requirement categories and classification

conditions: The project evolves a released predecessor as a successor release.
semantic.statement: Each predecessor claim requires its own RELEASE §9 disposition by that owner's predicates. Project lifecycle, legacy and migration-adoption classifications cannot supply or replace it. Active may coexist with successor superseded if meaning changed; Superseded establishes no accepted successor relation; Orphaned is not intentional removal.
semantic.uncertainty: RELEASE §9 predicates and disposition domain are not supplied.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Trace closure and anti-drift

exceptions: A live requirement may have an explicit honest deferment surface instead of realised design/code/tests.
semantic.statement: Every live requirement family has one or more owning design decisions; every ADR/design record explicitly grounds requirements through Implements:. Live requirements close through design/code/tests or explicit honest deferment. All shipping code/tests trace to live requirements and authorising design; working untraced behaviour is still accidental law. Unowned requirements, ungrounded design, unrecorded deferment and ownerless code are drift; implementation-habit tests lock it in. Persistent event/projection delta is diagnosed by intake among code, requirement/design stack, predictive model or observation. Capability without a scenario has unverified operational meaning. Treating guarantees/governance/verification as features misclassifies them; in-place live-constitution correction corrupts history. A real-use gap inexpressible in requirements re-enters at Requirements or upstream according to class, not by a code hack.

exceptions: Mutable implementation surfaces may be aggressively refactored while they retain that status.
Retained superseded responsibility must satisfy the migration retention relation.
semantic.statement: Published live constitutional domain artifacts cannot be silently mutated in place. An incorrect artifact is superseded by a new version or withdrawn/deleted from the live surface. Superseded transitions, scaffolds and fallbacks retire unless retention is justified; they have no permanent authority and compatibility shims need not ship forever. History is preserved by version control, operational events where present and superseded artifacts.

conditions: Lifecycle aspects materially affect product meaning or an obligation.
exceptions: No implementation mechanism for every phase and no release plan for every requirement is demanded.
semantic.statement: Product names boundary, intended use, release/install, live-use, observability and retirement/supersession posture where material. Requirements state invariant build/assurance/release/deployment/use/telemetry/retirement/ownership/source-truth/authority/interpretation obligations. Product/requirements provide enough signal for design or explicitly record ambiguity. Deferral names both deferment and later resolution owner surface. Each phase is answered, reasoned not-applicable, or named unknown; silence is invalid. Missing signal requires constitutional repricing or explicit governed debt, never invention from convention, precedent, prompts or fixtures. These phase answers are declared states, map to no core value and cannot substitute for satisfied; consuming evaluation has its own predicate/result.
semantic.uncertainty: ASSURANCE §16 application and the full result calculus are not supplied.

exceptions: An explicitly product-defined assurance capability may itself constitute product delivery; its evidence still does not author the claim.
semantic.statement: Judge progress and supported-path promotion against the same selected outcome. Only accepted material advance projects product progress; prerequisite readiness names its enabled obligation and remains bounded; preservation/repeated proof and regression are not new progress. Owner acceptance exhausts only the exact instance/interval, not enduring guarantees, recurrence or a broader family; witnesses persist for regression/preservation. Later work is preservation, a bounded prerequisite for another admitted outcome, or lawfully repriced change. Selecting an already-defined unresolved outcome is goals/sequencing; changed meaning/scope or a new outcome re-enters Product. Evidence completion cannot select, enlarge or replace the outcome. One artifact may be output for one claim and evidence for another only with separately declared roles.

Prerequisite/experiment authority is only its provisional bound and grants no enlarged outcome, downstream work, promotion, closure or waiver of applicable design/safety/authority/release law. Admission/renewal belongs to the work-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and is recorded in existing durable goals/ticket authority with bound and exhaustion/falsification condition. Experiment observation satisfaction or decision resolution, prerequisite discharge, outcome acceptance, another admitted terminal condition, rejection, withdrawal, supersession, repricing-away or evidential falsification ends the basis. Ticket/contract drafting or validation, active status, repair, continuation, evidence, run state and prior admission cannot create, extend or renew it; further material work needs new owner/proxy admission.

exceptions: Independent work may proceed under its own admitted basis.
Affected-path promotion may resume when regression/gap is repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority.
semantic.statement: Retention as supported behaviour, evidence, regression protection or bounded donor material grants no growth. Consumers own deletion/archive/quarantine/salvage mechanics; salvage inherits only explicitly re-adopted semantics, not enclosing authority, dependencies, completion or further-work selection. Regression or unresolved gap blocks the affected promotion path, without globally serialising independent authorised work or allowing its progress to be attributed to the governed outcome. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not complete product/release closure.

conditions: A substantive change begins.
semantic.statement: Every substantive change begins with intake triage, explicit declared change intent and lawful constitutional re-entry; the family table traces this route and creates no second decision path.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Foundation to law: change management and ambiguity

semantic.statement: F11 attributes ten consequences to premises: owning-layer re-entry rather than report labels; evidence-tested frames rather than names and diagnosis without repair authority; recorded exact-basis classification with distinct fact/judgment/ruling; unknowns withholding only dependent reliance and no assumption of no effect; obligation-conjunction closure rather than events/status; local visible bounded repayable proof deferral without sprint admission authority; recorded ambiguity with risk-policy blocking subject to hard stops; singular acceptance-path authority and downstream projections; shared-contract closure proof with persistent negative break evidence and owned retention; and no inherited authority absent explicit re-adoption. Domain/policy choices remain owned as stated: this member's six classes/four procedures/C-J-O order/material inputs, sprint requirements/triggers, ambiguity distinctions/narrowing, two migration strategies/presumption/old-path classes, inside-out order and implementation classes; project's declared risk policy; adopting profile's escrow suitability; and affected-product human authority's re-adoption selection. semantic.statement: Bug, feature, issue, regression, operator finding, release blocker and scenario failure enter the same triage; no label selects class or bypasses triage for code/tests/release. Triangulate the same subject/basis through the smallest sufficient applicable frame configuration, testing each diagnosis against its variables, relations and evidence. Preserve alternatives/uncertainty and identify the smallest lawful repair scope. Failure-exposing frame need not own the cause; renamed duplicate analysis adds no evidence. Conjunction preserves each predicate and any counterexample; unapplied planned frames leave diagnoses open. Required localisation/independence persists without prescribed reviewer count or new round. Diagnosis grants no effects and need not imply changed governing law.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/6. Lineage and release/Shared method adoption and propagation (STDO-UP-012)

conditions: A core interface changes.
exceptions: Bounded product-slice proof remains subject to the path-relative promotion rule.
semantic.statement: Change the authoritative contract first, prohibit authoritative bridge code for its family, audit and migrate every producer/consumer, and chase every downstream effect until no superseded closure law remains. Complete migration-closure proof comes after the completed migration wave. Split producer contracts, inconsistent runtime/reporting/topology carriers, authoritative aliases or second-truth projections cannot be declared complete despite green tests.

conditions: Selecting a strategy for core-interface or major implementation replacement.
exceptions: The presumption does not require an unsafe or constitutionally inadmissible predecessor path, nor retention of internal/public mechanisms explicitly superseded by product authority.
semantic.statement: Prefer bounded evolution rebuttably only when both strategies are lawful/feasible and a working predecessor reaches the admitted outcome without competing/ambiguous authority. Core-interface evolution uses inside-out hard-break. Fundamental re-adoption requires explicit affected-product human-owner selection comparing product value, feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics, with bounded abort/re-entry condition. Scale or architectural preference alone cannot select it.

exceptions: Residual superseded material outside the promoted path may be deferred only under all stated conditions.
semantic.statement: Both strategies prohibit proxy partial interfaces standing for the new contract in any acceptance path and silently authoritative bridges/fallbacks. Promotion requires singular authority over the full causal closure, not one successful trace; old/new admissibility for the same request/fact/identity/state/projection is competing authority and blocks it. Outside-path residuals may be deferred only when explicitly non-authoritative for the outcome or governing explicitly specified disjoint product/compatibility scope with deterministic routing, unable to falsify current/retained claims, and carrying bounded migration/qualification/release disposition. Tests detect leaks/prove, not plan migration. An intermediate slice can promote only with singular path authority and compliant residuals, leaving migration visibly open and retirement criteria intact. Slice identity/criteria include product plus every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design and retained predecessor claim; ticket/review wording cannot narrow them. Active migration does not renew accepted-slice growth; already-admitted removal/demotion/closure proof may continue within its bound without new progress claims, while producer/consumer growth requires another live admitted basis.

conditions: Every core-interface migration.
semantic.statement: Declare exact affected scope; every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope with deterministic routing; new authoritative and superseded contracts/surfaces; new closure law; full old/new producer and consumer sets; and every derived projection/report/status/proof surface. Classify every old path remove, replace, re-authorize or temporary scaffolding. Temporary scaffolding is lawful only when explicitly non-authoritative and scheduled for removal before closure.

conditions: A core-interface migration.

semantic.statement: No authoritative compatibility alias, silent fallback identity law, bridge acceptance as new contract, old authoritative reader/writer for a newly governed promoted outcome, or proxy/partial interface pretending completion is lawful, subject only to the explicit compatibility-feature exception.

Migration remains incomplete if runtime/reporting/topology/proof can disagree because of different carriers or closure laws, if a projection independently closes while its authoritative carrier is open, or if the carrier closes while a projection still depends on older law. Projections must not become second closure authority.

conditions: Inside-out hard-break migration.

Authoritative producers and source carrier precede downstream consumer/projection/prompt/dossier/report/review hardening. A projection ticket cannot close before its depended-on source-carrier ticket; explicit dependency direction exposes source-to-read-model order.

conditions: Each break in an inside-out interface-family migration.

Newly discovered affected interfaces leave the same wave only through explicit upward repricing.
semantic.statement: The wave is an ordered set of hard breaks, not permission for competing dual truth over the same request/fact/identity/state/projection. For each break publish or admit the deepest new carrier, sever and keep broken an old authoritative seam, repair outward through consumers, projections, prompts/reports and proof surfaces, then negatively prove rejection rather than mere nonuse. Tests may find interfaces but cannot replace the inventory. Re-enabling the seam via wrappers, fallback, projection or prompts is a defect.

exceptions: Bounded slice proof may establish only the exact intermediate outcome allowed by path-relative promotion.
semantic.statement: Complete migration proof is invalid while producers/consumers remain split across contracts; bridge-dependent passing tests and green local tests cannot establish closure. Slice proof is not migration proof. Per-break rejection/fail-closed evidence must precede counting downstream hardening as progress.

conditions: Claiming completion across the declared affected scope.
exceptions: A superseded mechanism may remain for a distinct supported responsibility satisfying the retention burden.
semantic.statement: Completion requires every authoritative producer/consumer on the new contract, superseded paths retired or justified for distinct supported responsibility, projections downstream of the same truth, one runtime/reporting/topology/proof closure law, and no acceptance-path temporary scaffolding. Otherwise the wave stays active. Every retained mechanism identifies current obligation, owner, purpose, execution scope and material cost. Temporary compatibility/comparison needs expiry/removal trigger; tests, oracle labels or nominal demotion do not justify duplicate production responsibility. Enduring required cold reconstruction or independent oracle needs no invented expiry. Identify surviving obligation owners; with no governing basis no replacement guard is required. Retirement within a closed affected cone need not await unrelated whole-product closure. Accepted slices name their exact closure and keep enclosing migration visibly open, never projecting migration/qualification/release closure.

exceptions: Inherited surfaces may be zeroed and rebuilt on the migration line.
Prior implementation may be moved sideways as reference material.

Explicitly re-adopt every retained statement/requirement/design/guide rule, intentionally locating it in the correct layer as recommended; old code/design are reference only unless re-derived/re-adopted. Absence means not-yet-adopted, without authority. Before reuse classify every inherited module/interface/carrier/projection/proof surface: carry_across is materially unchanged and intentionally adopted, redundant no longer needed, rewrite needed but rebuilt; unclassified implementation is a defect. Declare new line, establish fresh method/goals/intent/product/requirements/design, remove ambient old-line authority, classify constitutional material adopted/superseded/deferred/orphaned, copy only intentionally retained material, and re-derive from new truth. Direct runtime/projection/prompt/proof/review dependency on sideways implementation is bridge debt; partial proxies depending on it are not closure. The new surface is lawful supersession, not silent in-place mutation.

On landing, only new current operative truth remains in the affected scope; erase prior operative paths and retain the route only in version control/events/superseded records. Mixed operative models are not a stable endpoint; absent the explicit compatibility exception, delete rather than passively preserve.

semantic.statement: Deferral requires a named proof/cleanup class, debt local to admitted sprint surface, expected correction cost below per-change proof cost, a short enough sprint for reviewability, and close review that classifies and pays down debt. Escrow is explicit and satisfies no method/release/product closure until paid down, accepted or repriced. When governing method permits, eligible classes may include screenshots/walkthrough capture, visual review, accessibility cleanup, UI interaction replay proof, design wording, trace and local realisation cleanup. Escrow must not hide new product truth, changed/new data contracts, runtime/governance/closure/provenance/evidence semantics, missing constructive carriers, changed public published-function/carrier contracts, or law changes requiring goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe. Such findings are recorded and exit through a standalone ticket, repricing action or sprint supersession.
semantic.uncertainty: The governing method's specific escrow permissions are not supplied.

conditions: Sprint close review begins or closed status is proposed.
exceptions: Explicit local paydown debt may survive close only when governing method permits follow-up.
semantic.statement: Close begins with status closing and freezes new iteration. Every included ticket/iteration is reviewed against the manifest; evidence durability is checked; changed surfaces are walked against cited authority; deferred compliance is classified; debt surviving review gets paydown tickets. Every item receives accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice or remove. Closure requires classification of every item and debt entry and durable resulting paydown/repricing work, not satisfied results for all. Hidden authority drift cannot be accepted.

Classification must be against cited sprint authority and consume, while remaining separate from, the item's core review results. Local debt is the counterexample for local_paydown; its governing relation stays coherent, otherwise repricing is required. Repricing invalidates the cited authority's ability to support acceptance; its named layer is a declared re-entry fact accompanying the core value, not another result. Removal's reason is its counterexample and requires neither violated governing relation nor competing truth path; it therefore has no matching ACTIVATION disposition. Item/debt mappings add no core value or disposition and never turn debt, repricing or removal into compliance.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/One durable record per ticket

semantic.statement: Every ticket has one durable authoritative record. Repository/external-tracker carriers are lawful only if they preserve the required contract, history, state transition, stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal local copy. Local filenames should carry stable id and short slug; T-001-add-product-layer.md, B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md, S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md and C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md are recommended examples.

conditions: The same admitted work genuinely has multiple tenant execution lines.
Applies to backlog and active tickets.
exceptions: Completed tickets are not affected retroactively unless reopened or explicitly repriced.
Upstream-only and single-tenant cases require no sibling duplicate.
semantic.statement: Keep the upstream authority ticket separate and create one tenant-local ticket per build tenant, appending a tenant mnemonic to base id and filename. Each tenant independently owns status, proof, closure, repricing and reopening; another tenant's green status cannot hide blockers or false closure. Duplicates should record source_ticket and build_tenant. build_tenant identifies the product's how.build_tenants entry; path/display/tracker aliases substitute only when product definition binds them as identity. The unsuffixed base may remain upstream authority, while backlog/active multi-tenant execution and closure live on suffixed tickets. B-030 with B-030-T1 and B-030-T2 is illustrative.
semantic.uncertainty: Tenant identity and realisation semantics are imported from PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8.

semantic.statement: Every ticket records at least id, title, type, ticket_category, status, goal, change_intent, change_class, re_entry_point, triaged_at, created_at and updated_at. Recommended additional fields: priority, dependencies, links, intake_source, affected_boundary, source_ticket for duplication/derivation and build_tenant for tenant-local work. Migration tickets additionally carry migration_strategy and library_usage; consume/extend requires governing_library, none requires library_rationale. Tenant-local migration requires build_tenant and source_ticket when derived/duplicated upstream. For admission a runtime-drafted contract should also carry at least target_truth, superseded_truth when relevant, closure_law, evaluation_criteria, non_closure_conditions and proof_surface.
semantic.uncertainty: Recommended contract fields retain their 'should' modality.

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration.
exceptions: Downstream exploratory work may occur while the source ticket is active, but is non-closure evidence until the source carrier is admitted and authoritative.
semantic.statement: Tickets publishing/admitting the authoritative source carrier are upstream. Tickets hardening prompts, projections, reports, dossiers, review surfaces and other consumers depend on them. A downstream ticket cannot close while its upstream source-carrier ticket remains open.

Tickets record intake's declared class using SPEC_METHOD §4 classes. Type, category and class are independent dimensions: bug + implementation_migration + design_reframe is consistent. A spike should terminate in a more specific downstream ticket or an explicit decision that no further substantive change is required; exploratory status does not eliminate its current triage class.
semantic.uncertainty: The external class definitions are only partially described by the supplied text.

conditions: A bug's lawful re-entry class is being determined.
semantic.statement: Before realization_refactor, establish that current requirement and accepted realising design govern the affected behaviour and suffice for the authorized outcome; mere presence proves no coverage. Missing/ambiguous evidence leaves treatment unknown, not the layer absent. Candidate public violation does not select a new contract; governing-owner re-entry requires explicitly changed desired outcome or established insufficiency. Walk upward from realisation, checking each layer and stopping at the highest found missing/insufficient: requirement missing/insufficient → requirement_reprice and requirement owner; sufficient requirement but missing/insufficient design → design_reframe and Design; actual Goal/Intent/Product change → corresponding owner/class; sufficient requirement/design with implementation deviation → realization_refactor, repair or reject candidate. Unresolved meaning remains J and reserved choice remains O.
semantic.uncertainty: Full computed-classification algorithm and C/J/O annotation definitions are external.

conditions: Ticket concerns substantive work.
semantic.statement: The ticket carries declared change_intent, lawful change_class, lawful re_entry_point and triaged_at; these are the values intake triage declared, not a later role's replacement classification.

Ticket statuses including local additions, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and recorded change_class are declared carrier states and map to no core value. Sprint-close classifications and debt outcomes are results mapped at close review. Evaluating a state produces a separate predicate-bearing core result; states must never be combined as evaluation results.

Backlog tickets use ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, default .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/; active tickets use .active, default .ai-workspace/tickets/active/; completed tickets move to .completed, default .ai-workspace/tickets/completed/. Lanes keep the live set small and searchable without moving deferred work into comments or goals.

conditions: A derived surface or projected frame is insufficient.
semantic.statement: The described actor reads this member only for the named unresolved lifecycle/proof question and cites used clauses. Deciding routes are Carrier selection for record/lifetime, Execution contract admission for execution, Recorded judgment and owner-ruling continuity for reusable judgments/repricing, and Condition-based closure and reuse for completion. The derivation table is traceability, not an alternative decision owner.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Foundation to law: work carriers

semantic.statement: F13's eleven consequence groups concern lifetime-matched carriers, admitted execution basis, one authority chain, sprint escrow/close outcomes, recorded triage/upward re-entry, tenant-local lifecycles, migration proof/recurrence, independent verification and durable rulings, condition-based closure/test authority, semantic term resolution, and flexible carrier shape/bounded reading. Obligations surviving a run must be recorded before return; comment content is provisional until adopted into its owning surface and has its own discussion state. Member choices include carrier kinds/selection table, minimum fields/types/categories/statuses/lanes, offering sprints, escrow lists/result mappings, tenant suffixes, migration declarations/checklists/strategy/library values/thresholds/review questions/break order, four repricing states/predicate, five-step test reconciliation, recommended shapes/search defaults and bounded reading policy. Product definition owns carrier locations/rebinding and tenant registry; governing method owns whether debt may survive; POSTING_GUIDE owns post categories/structure/states. Admission step law, migration law, independent assessment/reuse, result conjunction/general test law and semantic resolution remain owned by the cited external sections. Consumers add no deciding authority. A credible recurrence requires review, not automatic commonisation or identity merging.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Carrier selection

conditions: An execution is governed by the described method.
semantic.statement: Every execution uses one run contract. Establish upstream work authority, then choose the first matching row, with local boundary equal to an admitted sprint when inside it, otherwise current run: (1) no authority → no admitted contract, no substitute-authority ticket, stop/re-enter; (2) exact admitted ticket → derive and reuse, no duplicate; (3) authority but no exact ticket and independent state/open obligation beyond local boundary → durable ticket plus contract, create/update only under ticket-state authority; (4) authority, no exact ticket, entirely inside admitted sprint with no post-close state → manifest plus local iteration, no durable ticket; (5) authority, no exact ticket or sprint and current-run completion without surviving independent state → intake-drafted contract, no durable ticket. Ticket-shaped fields create neither durable ticket identity nor lane state.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Carrier selection

semantic.statement: An exact product-authorized instruction may supply one-run upstream authority; generic requests and model-widened scope cannot. Durable creation/update requires selected surviving state and ticket-state authority. An explicit durable-record instruction from that authority selects durability but neither admits execution nor widens upstream authority. Admission mechanism/result-evidence surface are product-bound; admitted result coordinates are recorded on ticket/manifest when selected. Presence, lane, active status and admission prose without coordinates are not admission evidence; the contract remains drafted or rejected. Absent/rejected admission returns missing authority without execution. Before return, surviving obligations become sprint-local entries if their lifetime fits; otherwise durable tickets only under ticket-state authority. Without that authority, retain them in the named durable result/evidence surface or already-authorized enclosing carrier, mark closure withheld on ticket-state authority and return re-entry. No available durable result/evidence surface invokes referenced admission refusal. Execution and closure share categorization, criteria, proof and non-closure conditions; proof/gap analysis/repricing continue.
semantic.uncertainty: Exact admission coordinates and refusal procedure are defined by unsupplied ACTIVATION §1.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Execution contract admission

exceptions: A human or mixed binding may select another durable carrier; a binding requiring an event log still requires that log.
semantic.statement: Runtime flow should treat ticket/sprint entry/draft as admission candidate, never automatic truth; contracts carry at least drafted/admitted/rejected/superseded states. An admitted contract should be durably recorded for applicable prompt assembly and later closure on the same basis, with required event logs. Self-certification refusal belongs to ACTIVATION §1. Contract admission validates against the cited product outcome, prerequisite or experiment; it does not admit/renew that basis. Basis admission/renewal belongs to the selected goals-work-wave owner or explicitly bounded proxy and stays durably legible in existing goals/ticket authority. Active status, lane and admitted/retained contract never admit a growth basis.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Evaluation criteria and non-closure conditions

exceptions: Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by itself a non-closure condition.
semantic.statement: A contract should expose progress/completion criteria and failures despite local green proof, minimally visible evaluation_criteria and non_closure_conditions as its local gain function. Typical migration failures are old authoritative normal execution in affected scope, accepted mixed old/new proof, proxy/partial acceptance implementation, reachable competing/ambiguous executable authority on the claimed acceptance path, or unreconciled ticket/product/proof wording. These are material execution conditions. Outside-path debt may be deferred only under SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules.
semantic.uncertainty: The exact external debt-deferral rule is not supplied; migration compatibility exceptions are retained separately.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/5. From carrier to execution/Bounded-context term binding

exceptions: An unqualified term is permitted when cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning.
semantic.statement: Ticket/work-instruction terms follow PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. Cross-context or materially competing meanings require citation of applicable product disambiguation or owner-authorized import/translation/equivalence/disambiguation carrier; referencing the relation may replace duplication. Prose, familiarity, matching glossary headings, tenant placement and comment context cannot select meaning or transfer authority. Unresolved/multiply resolved material terms block affected admission and closure. Opening/updating a ticket records pressure without curing it; resolution re-enters the owner of the missing context/relation.

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration.
exceptions: No excluded/disjoint scope is satisfied by explicit declaration of absence, never silence.

Declaration names strategy, exact affected scope, every excluded/disjoint product or compatibility scope with deterministic routing, old/superseded and new/authoritative contracts, old/new producer and consumer sets, every derived projection/report/status/proof surface and closure law. Minimum checklist covers named scope/exclusions/routing/old/new paths/new producers/new consumers/projections; old authority removal or explicit demotion in scope; rejection of mixed-state closure evidence; removal/repricing of mixed-behaviour tests; recurrence review against libraries/commonisation; library usage with governing surface/rationale; one tenant lifecycle per backlog/active ticket with suffixed sibling work; and reconciled ticket/product/proof wording before closure. migration_strategy is inside_out_hard_break or fundamental_re_adoption; library_usage is none/consume/extend. consume/extend names governing_library; none explains in library_rationale that no reusable surface applies, the pattern remains boundary-specific, or no lawful recurrence/commonisation candidate yet exists.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/6. Implementation migration/Closure of a migration ticket

exceptions: An old path explicitly declared and justified in the ticket as retained compatibility may remain in affected scope.
Deterministically routed non-overlapping scope outside affected scope retains its own current authority.
semantic.statement: Old authoritative normal execution inside affected scope blocks closure unless the retained-compatibility exception applies. No silently authoritative old path, mixed green tests, proxy or partial implementation establishes completion; compatibility is named as such rather than native truth and cannot be inferred from surviving code. A completed ticket whose checked items are false on the current tree must reopen or have an explicitly linked successor. Intermediate product-slice acceptance may occur under SPEC_METHOD §7 path-relative promotion, whose identity/criteria ticket wording cannot narrow. The migration ticket stays active until its checklist and final closure law hold. Active status renews no exhausted slice growth authority; bounded removal/demotion/closure-proof work may continue, but further material producer/consumer growth requires another basis admitted under SPEC_METHOD §3.

semantic.statement: inside_out_hard_break requires a full best-guess interface inventory, deepest-source-outward break sequence, old seam intentionally severed by each break and expected negative proof per break. fundamental_re_adoption requires explicit human product-authority selection; comparison with bounded evolution across product value, feedback latency, authority risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics; bounded abort/re-entry; sideways reference/prior implementation boundary as source material; module/interface adjudication surface; and carry_across, redundant or rewrite classification of every inherited module/interface/carrier/projection/proof surface. Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/6. Implementation migration/Recurring realisation and library declaration

conditions: Applies to every implementation migration ticket, irrespective of adopted profiles.
exceptions: A third local rebuild may proceed with consume, extend, or a linked explicit do-not-commonise design decision in library_rationale.

Outside recurrence rules and current-claim hard stops, a discovered pattern is repricing input and blocks no bounded claim or requires no follow-up ticket unless its owning authority admits the follow-up.
semantic.statement: Second credible recurrence forces explicit library/commonisation review. If review establishes the same realisation pattern in two module boundaries or tickets, a third local rebuild blocks implementation absent a stated exception. Preferred order is boundary-local cleanup, then tenant-local reusable surface, then shared/common propagation only through separate design re-entry. DESIGN_MODULE adopters additionally apply §10's design-review/candidate refinement without a rival threshold. Patterns discovered during active work remain subject to these thresholds.

conditions: The same work item is processed across several tenants; backlog and active tickets are reviewed.
exceptions: Tenant-local reopening/repricing/successor work may require upstream change when the upstream source/product/design ticket itself must change.
semantic.statement: Review checks a separate suffixed ticket and named build_tenant for every tenant, separate proof surface/closure law, no substitution of one tenant's green proof for another's closure, and tenant-local reopening, repricing and successor work subject to the upstream-change exception.

conditions: Core-interface or carrier migration for the recommended Functional Review Criteria section.
semantic.statement: Migration must be concrete enough that rename/adapter/wrapper/happy-path proof cannot claim source-truth replacement. A core-interface/carrier ticket should include ticket-specific Functional Review Criteria enabling review of: control-flow meaning replaced by admitted carrier/algebra/event truth; semantic centre actually reduced/removed rather than relocated; typed/closed carrier/contract/transition rather than open dict/string/config protocol; main step as pure admitted-truth transform rather than procedural law; effects at the edge; consumers directly reading admitted carrier rather than reconstructing from payloads/.get/defaults/text/legacy files; projections derived without independent closure authority; deterministic gates, if present, informing state without structurally blocking lawful constructive/probabilistic paths; and explicit reuse/extension where the pattern exists elsewhere. Tests alone do not suffice. Preserved semantic centres behind wrappers, adapter policy, old lists alongside algebra, fallback configuration or rehydrated dictionaries fail review despite green public behaviour.
semantic.uncertainty: Review questions retain their recommended framing and do not establish answers for any implementation.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/6. Implementation migration/Impacted interface review checklist

conditions: Core-interface, carrier or authoritative-contract migration.
exceptions: A deferred interface names its successor ticket or stays unchecked.
Compatibility shims qualify only if explicitly justified as retained compatibility.
semantic.statement: The checklist must exist before tests serve as closure evidence and name every relevant live interface. It should enumerate where present source-carrier builders; closure/register/projection builders; deepest semantic kernel/adapters; wrappers and bootstrap/replay/ingest/resume/query entrypoints; prompt/report/projection/read models; constructor/materialisation paths; proof lanes and negative fixtures. Each item states interface-specific closure, such as consuming admitted projection without helper authority, exposing read models without rebuilding missing publication, or avoiding independent closure from open payload aggregation. A false checked item makes the ticket not closure-ready. Hard-break checklists describe seam inventory before test closure evidence; re-adoption checklists explicitly cover inherited carried/dropped/rewritten modules/interfaces, never implicit carry-forward.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/6. Implementation migration/Break order and break-to-closure map

conditions: Migration touches a core interface; a closure map additionally applies when several old interfaces exist.
semantic.statement: The ticket includes the source-outward ordered execution section and, for several old interfaces, the break-to-closure map. Explicit defects include typed wrappers retaining old semantic authority; a new carrier beside an old authoritative read model; proxies/partial implementations retaining old interfaces under new names; constructor/replay/ingest/resume/bootstrap/public-wrapper admission bypass; projections/tests passing without the new carrier; fallback invention of policy/identity/target/closure truth; and downstream proof passing while upstream source-carrier work remains open.

exceptions: Explicitly specified retained compatibility permits an old path.
Deterministically routed non-overlapping scope outside affected scope does not block migration merely because its path works.
semantic.statement: Positive behaviour proof alone is insufficient. The proof surface should include at least one negative/structural proof that the old path cannot satisfy closure. Examples include rejecting a severed seam before downstream repair counts as progress; fail-closed advancement/closure/prompts/projection without new carrier; rejecting legacy payloads instead of rehydrating truth; deliberate old/new disagreement resolved to new truth or fail-closed; rejecting same-name but structurally different carrier/function/route/policy/projection; and closure proof independent of undeclared fixtures or mutable sibling workspaces. Old normal execution in affected scope or reachability on claimed acceptance path keeps the ticket open absent the compatibility exception. With an interface checklist, negative proof exercises named public consumers material to closure; bypassing one shim is insufficient when live authority already bypasses it through helpers/loaders/rebuild paths.
semantic.uncertainty: The 'should include' proof-count recommendation is not strengthened into a universal numerical obligation.

grounds.heading: TICKETS/7. Authority, judgment, closure and state

semantic.statement: The source assigns generic independent assessment to tier-1 EVALUATION §3, acceptance as decision-owner disposition and condition-based rather than reviewer-approved closure to EVALUATION §5, and closed-result reuse to ACTIVATION §7. Constructor self-review is construction output; this member states work-carrier consequences without taking ownership of those generic laws.
