Their member schemas embed neither instance nor instance digest, preventing self-dependent digest preimages.

Profile is neither a change to pure a_c/reference-frame law nor mandatory for all symbolic models; neither concrete subject/workspace ontology nor process/traversal/retry/continuation/closure engine; neither event store/log schema/projection implementation/state carrier nor mutation/admission/evaluation/decision authority; neither prospective-frame nor sensor-population profile. It guarantees neither occurrence ownership of every event nor acyclicity of every typed-lineage graph.

conditions: For review and qualification of an adoption/implementation.
semantic.statement: Review covers at least: exact a_c basis/eight RecordKind_ac populations/closed domains without shadowing; inherited families/direct coordinates/disjoint local-external identities; complete seeds/congruent mirrors/no future results/events; first event without fictional predecessor; distinct candidate/judgment/event/relation/cut/cut-judgment ids with unchanged subject digest; idempotent or refused duplicates; cycles in each identity/causal subgraph; lawful opposing support/correction; closed event kinds/payload/digest/scope/bindings without fabricated event_for; separated functor/traversal/operation-kind/instance/executor/actor/grant/invocation/target/territory; missing/stale/mismatched/out-of-territory grants; all four effect cases; mutable reality carrier; fresh reapplication identities; component/aggregate identities; refusal on stale pre-observation and grant currentness; incomplete cut refusal including missing/non-admitted cut judgment or unequal source frontiers; frontier completeness/staleness/correction selection; no cause from timestamp/ordinal/adjacency/containment/correlation; absent adoption and incomplete-mapping refusal; exact JCS/kind/schema/URI/digest/calculus-address/publication-membership reconstruction. Examples/checkers establish only evaluated claims and acquire no engine or semantic authority.
semantic.uncertainty: The conformance list uses 'refusal' for stale readiness while the detailed law distinguishes stale, hold and stale_currentness.

conditions: For UX work governed by this profile.
exceptions: The narrowly conditioned view-local ephemera allowance is stated separately.
semantic.statement: View is a pure projection of typed State; transitions are pure reductions over typed Msg; effects are reducer-described values interpreted at a declared membrane; runtime owns lifecycle and continuation. Stateful mutation in views, two-way binding without action emission and effect handlers acting as controllers violate the profile despite ecosystem convention.

conditions: Product authority adopts the profile for a UX surface and records adoption in product definition, ticket, design module or review.
semantic.statement: Adopted profile is the surface's sole UX realization authority. Project ADRs may choose stack but cannot weaken process model. Existing code, library convention, screenshots, comments, design history, prototypes and generated artifacts are evidence only. Concrete ambiguity fails closed: satisfy stricter interpretation→resolved; reprice through governing constitutional method to governing-surface owner→escalated; record scoped design-module exemption before implementation→carried with exemption residual. Until an exit is taken, ambiguity is blocked and implementation cannot proceed.
semantic.uncertainty: Referenced §15 gives further result definitions outside the supplied sections.

conditions: Instance premises hold where a UX surface is realized under this adopted profile.
semantic.statement: F20 imports F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work-state/resumption/reuse, F11 change/ambiguity and F13 carriers, and refines F17 software design. Adopted instance premises, not foundational deductions, are: I1 people/systems observe admitted truth and request changes through surfaces; I2 external Product design declares truth/carriers; I3 stacks differ and tolerate view state/continuation/effects; I4 uncontrolled data seams; I5 short iterations can make per-change proof cost exceed correction. Ten authored consequence rows preserve ownership: (1) P6/P1+F2/F11+I1/I2 require admitted carriers and blocking absent carriers; profile owns five carrier kinds/binding requirements, Product design actual contracts. (2) P0/P1/P4a+F2+I3 support typed transitions; choosing TEA and ephemera test is profile policy. (3) P0/P5+F2 require declared effects; profile owns membrane/handler rules refining DESIGN_MODULE, project interpreter. (4) P4b/P6+F4 require replayable recorded behavior and executable proof before closure; profile owns test/six proof contents, project design module proof surface. (5) P3/P1/P6+I4 require shared types and runtime validation; profile makes six seams mandatory, project schema mechanism. (6) P2/P6+I1 require public-capability accessibility declarations and recorded internal-debug exemption; profile owns five declarations, WCAG AA is only recommended web default, project may strengthen. (7) P2/P1+I3 permit stack freedom, never rankings; project owns choices, profile owns compliance tests and stricter fail-closed handling. (8) P6+F11+I3 require admitted adoption/one authority and ambiguity outcomes. (9) P6/P4b+F4/F11/F13+I5 require authorized scoped scaffold exemption with retirement, no production by accumulation, visible bounded payable proof escrow and classification of every close finding; profile owns default-governance/escrow/trigger choices, TICKETS generic escrow and six close classifications, SPEC_METHOD sprint boundary. (10) P5/P6+F3 require four predicate-specific refinements, one core mapping per value without conflating review/replay/closure/carrier results. Pillar associations by row are respectively {4,5,9},{3,4},{4,8},{6,8,9},{2,3,4},{1,9},{4,8},{1,7,9},{1,9},{3,9}. P0 is recovered; P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent; P5 derives from P0/P6 with open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts. No policy choice is presented as foundational derivation. Adoption-opening steps, failure patterns and review questions apply these consequences; each clause names its requiring principle.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed five accessibility declarations, default-governance conditions, escrow inventories, classifications and four result refinements are referenced but not enumerated in the supplied source.

conditions: When consumers enter the foundation-to-law rows.
semantic.statement: Authored consumer loci remain directional applications, not extra authority: carrier row→ACTIVATION §2, relationship clause, both realization tests, adoption step5, escrow, failures7/13, review3/4, §15 carrier/block results; process row→both tests, adoption4/9, failures1/2/8/10, review1/2/6/10/11, surface review; membrane row→discretion, transitions, view shape, adoption6/9, failures3/5/11, review5/10, surface review; replay row→adoption7, escrow, failures4/12, review7/12, replay/closure results; types row→discretion, failures6/14, review8/9, surface review; accessibility row→adoption8, escrow, failure9, review10, closure; stack row→adoption2, review11, stricter §15 review; authority row→adoption, failure16, §15 fail-closed; scaffold/escrow row→relationship, failures15/17, review10/14, closure and §15 scope/classification boundary; results row→authority, carriers and both tests. Consumers decide nothing beyond owning sections. No other member returns the UX refined values, and FOUNDATIONS owns their core without applying this UX section's rule.
semantic.uncertainty: Most target loci are not supplied; their detailed rules cannot be reconstructed from consumer indexes.

semantic.statement: UX refines rather than duplicates DESIGN_MODULE: parent-governed immutability, totality, effect edges, no semantic centre and coupling remain parent law; UX extends render lifecycle, browser events, layout and accessibility. For a UX module, both apply and its design module reads both; for a non-UX module, only DESIGN_MODULE applies and UX is ignored. A graph-execution Product projection/query surface including UX follows UX realization law. Graph execution determines Product graph-native shape, DESIGN_MODULE module discipline, UX additional surface discipline.

grounds.heading: UX/2. Role and composition/Relationship to other members

semantic.statement: UX sprint compliance escrow is permitted under referenced §12 only when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof visible, bounded and payable. WORLD_MODEL governs world-model semantic law only for Products with that dimension; UX over world-model state still binds AssetSurface or equivalent under §7.
semantic.uncertainty: Detailed escrow and world-model laws are not supplied.

semantic.statement: UX profile does not supply styling/design-system specification, component library, brand/visual identity, wireframing/prototyping process, user-study method, stack ranking or framework recommendation. These valid concerns belong to Product-local surfaces.

grounds.heading: UX/3. Product truth and admitted carriers

conditions: A Msg changes Product truth.
exceptions: UX-local messages may govern genuinely view-local expansion, sort, filter, focus and draft concerns.
semantic.statement: Every Product-truth-changing message maps to one admitted Product carrier. Such changes include asset writes/creation/moves/deletion; Context, selection authority, pinning/global state; session spawning/attachment/resumption; agent/job/workorder/graph-call/runtime-command dispatch; closure/approval/continuation/lineage/provenance/evidence; publishing/accepting/rejecting/superseding records. UX cannot become a hidden constructive carrier. Without an admitted carrier, surface is blocked until one is authored or requirement repriced.

grounds.heading: UX/4. Process model/Process model without stack mandate

conditions: For a project selecting a realization stack.
semantic.statement: Project records chosen stack and short justification in design module. Each discretionary choice must preserve §4 Elm model and §6 membrane. Process model is non-negotiable, stack free within it; profile tests realizations and never ranks frameworks. One clause tests §4–§8; Realisation discretion tests §4–§10 under inspection plus absence of §13 failures. Source explicitly retains this difference for governing authority and refers to §15's stricter fail-closed selection. Reject view-owned state continuation, render effects, state mutation outside typed reducer, multi-step view state machines bypassing Msg, two-way binding without Msg, imperative DOM manipulation in render and handlers used as controllers. Non-normative examples are language-integrated reducers, typed reducer plus effect interpreter, reactive signals behind reducer with no external signal mutation, and server-rendered hypermedia using server derivation and request/response effect boundary; examples confer no compliance verdict.
semantic.uncertainty: Full §13 and §15 are absent; no implementation's compliance is evaluated.

exceptions: Sub algebra is required when subscribing to external or runtime events.
semantic.statement: Surface declares State shape, Msg algebra, pure Update:(Msg,State)→(State,Cmd), Cmd algebra and conditional Sub algebra. State changes through typed Msg reduction. Each Cmd names effect kind, typed input, admitted carrier/external target, typed outcome Msg family covering every materially possible observed or unresolved result including success/failure, outcome-selection evidence and observations resolving uncertainty, and any required deterministic correlation among Cmd, invocation, outcome messages and replay. Outcome Msg represents available evidence; intended-effect meanings completed, not_effected, completion_unknown answer 'the intended effect occurred' without replacing Product message vocabulary. Lost/failed transport alone proves neither completion nor non-completion; sufficient independent observation may decide, otherwise Msg and State retain completion_unknown, correlation and missing observation. Reducer performs no I/O, side-channel logging or global mutation; runtime interprets effects at membrane.

Effects are isolated to declared membrane. It interprets reducer-produced Cmd and returns outcomes through Msg; branching, conditional state derivation and multi-step business decisions belong in reducer. One declared Cmd is interpreted per effect. Unresolved outcome returns typed unresolved Msg without coercion to success/failure. Before repetition or dependent effect whose safety depends on outcome, Product observes owning state and follows referenced recovery with current authority/territory retained; recovery is explicit Cmd/Msg. Any useEffect/createEffect/onMount/subscribe/server-action or other handler belongs to membrane only when interpreting a declared Cmd. A handler deciding transitions violates the law; move that logic to reducer. Render, render helpers and reducer have no I/O, subscription or imperative platform manipulation.
semantic.uncertainty: Full ACTIVATION recovery law is referenced but absent.

conditions: When Product publishes typed AssetSurface contracts under graph-execution carrier law and Product design.
exceptions: Without AssetSurface, the design module names an equivalent typed contract and applies the same law.
semantic.statement: Bind one or more AssetSurface contracts as data sources/action targets. State derives from their projections without local asset-shape redeclaration. Truth-changing Msg variants map one-to-one to action-registry entries or documented projection wrappers with no hidden semantic change. UX-local variants remain local concerns. Selection emits Context update/equivalent consistent with selection contract. Writes use action registry, never direct file/service calls. Shared typed contract is ground truth on both sides; no admitted equivalent contract means truth-changing actions are blocked.

conditions: For source-described prompt construction for UI/operator-surface work.
semantic.statement: A UI/operator work prompt carries needed governing UX law using a current derived surface/projected frame where suitable, otherwise deciding sections directly, rather than requiring raw-member rediscovery. If work changes Product truth through UI, prompt names admitted carrier and action path; failure to identify them yields block/re-entry rather than local invention. This is a represented prompt-processing requirement, not an instruction to execute that workflow here.
semantic.uncertainty: Acquisition mechanics are owned by absent ACTIVATION §2.

semantic.statement: Runtime owns continuation; view owns none. All transitions use declared Msg interpreted by reducer. View cannot independently decide next state, chain local updates without separate Msg emissions or hide inter-event state in refs, closures or module variables. A needed multi-step machine belongs in reducer State with explicit phase Msg; view projects the phase. Inability to replay behavior from Msg log against empty State indicates leaked view continuation.

conditions: Before a Product UX surface claims closure under the profile.
exceptions: A pure projection-only surface may use a no-effect proof.
semantic.statement: Require at least one executable replay proof per Product-meaningful interaction family, with all six declared proof components. Correctness depending on unrepresented DOM state; mutable refs/module variables/closures/timers/handler memory; network/file results bypassing Msg; or local state affecting Product after unmount/replay fails proof. Where effect may be unresolved, cover correlated unresolved Msg, retained State and recovery, including no outcome-dependent repeat before required observation. Reproducing that State proves only replay, never external completion: replay_passes and completion_unknown may coexist. Projection-only no-effect proof can be Msg log, final State and empty Cmd sequence.

exceptions: Out-of-render mutation is excepted from the cited §6 violation when part of declared membrane, such as a design-module-named imperative-interop platform handle.
semantic.statement: View accepts typed State/props/context, returns typed ViewTree, declares every consumed input, captures no mutable cross-render closure state and reads no undeclared source. Function/component/template/server handler/signal expression/other framework shape is a recorded stack decision; constitutional State→ViewTree and no body side effects remain. An effect-handler-written ref read during rendering violates §6 unless covered by the narrow declared-membrane exception.
semantic.uncertainty: The membrane-handle exception does not expressly waive typed inputs, declared reads or replay requirements.

conditions: At every untrusted or out-of-process seam.
exceptions: UX-local types may describe view-local concerns but cannot shadow back-end types.
semantic.statement: Import UX-consumed/back-end shapes from shared front/back contract rather than redeclaring them; same package or contracts/ package is typical, not mandatory. Runtime validation is obligatory for HTTP/RPC responses, MCP payloads, file-loaded records, websocket/event streams, agent/worker outputs and URL/storage/clipboard/browser integration payloads. One typed-schema definition produces compile-time types and runtime validators; mechanism is project-local. Compile-time TypeScript alone is insufficient. View-local form drafts, sort enums and filter strings may have local types without shadowing back-end types.

conditions: The UX surface is the public face of a product capability.
exceptions: Accessibility is optional for internal-only debug surfaces, with the exemption recorded in the design module.
semantic.statement: Declare semantic structure or platform equivalents; keyboard or platform-equivalent navigation for every pointer action; focus management for dynamic changes; annotations for every custom interactive element lacking native semantics; and contrast at the project's declared standard. WCAG AA is a recommended web default, not an unconditional mandate. Projects with stricter obligations author a local accessibility refinement and cite it from design modules.
semantic.uncertainty: Other supplied sections mention recorded public-surface exemptions; their relationship to this section's non-optional language is retained as a residual.

conditions: Product authority adopts the profile for a project.
semantic.statement: Record the profile name, chosen realisation stack and justification, irreducible architectural carrier set and required structural diagram, State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub shapes for each surface before implementation, consumed and emitted AssetSurface or equivalent typed-contract bindings, effect-membrane mechanism and interpreted Cmd algebra, executable Msg-replay proof surface, required accessibility refinements and explicit view-shape/effect-membrane exemptions.
semantic.uncertainty: The referenced UX §§1, 4, 6–9 and DESIGN_MODULE §§6–7 are not supplied in full.

conditions: Any one trigger holds: reachable from product shell; used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release or review; can mutate product truth; can spawn, attach, resume or dispatch work; or can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence or provenance.
exceptions: A scaffold, prototype, debug pane or temporary proof surface can be exempt only with the specified record.
semantic.statement: Any listed trigger brings a surface under the profile by default.

conditions: A scaffold, prototype, debug pane or temporary proof surface claims exemption.
semantic.statement: The design module or ticket must record scope, permitted operations, forbidden or explicitly bounded mutation, visible scaffold/debug label when user-facing, authoritative replacement, retirement condition and owning ticket, and a non-closure condition preventing release while the scaffold remains. An exempt scaffold cannot become production UX by accumulation: retire it, reprice it into governed UX or keep it outside product closure.

conditions: Any non-escrowable change appears during a UX sprint.
semantic.statement: Record the finding and exit the UX sprint path through standalone repricing or sprint supersession; the UX layer cannot become a hidden constructive carrier.
semantic.uncertainty: Generic escrow law and close mechanics belong to unsupplied TICKETS §3; SPEC_METHOD §4 admits this profile statement.

conditions: UX sprint close is considered or claimed.
exceptions: Explicitly recorded exemptions can cover replay or accessibility closure obligations.
Explicit local paydown tickets permit close only for debt local to UX realisation and only where the governing method allows follow-up.
semantic.statement: A sprint should close when further iteration is costlier or less trustworthy than review. Valid triggers include timebox expiry, too many changed states for casual review, obsolete screenshots/walkthroughs, interaction changes beyond polish, or reviewer uncertainty requiring reconciliation. Close reviews every changed screen, state and meaningful interaction against cited authority, classifying every finding as accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice or remove. Accepted means profile-and-design compliant; local_paydown means local UX debt captured by ticket. Unclassified carrier gaps, hidden state continuation or authority drift prohibit close. Replay and accessibility obligations may be deferred, never erased.
semantic.uncertainty: The six classifications are TICKETS-owned and are not mapped by the UX result section.

conditions: Any listed failure pattern is present on a surface to which the profile applies.
exceptions: The source expressly conditions view-shape and accessibility failures on absence of recorded exemptions; scaffold failure refers to its required exemption record.
semantic.statement: Each independently constitutes a violation: render code directly mutates state/props/context; view-local cells carry product meaning rather than ephemera; effect-handler conditional logic decides transitions; multistep state machines live in views instead of reducers; render reads mutable refs outside the declared membrane; UX-local types shadow/redeclare backend types instead of importing shared contracts; selection/action emission writes file/network without AssetSurface action; unrecorded view-shape exemption; public-capability accessibility omitted without recorded exemption; two-way binding emits no typed Msg and bypasses reducer; Cmd logic implemented imperatively inside an effect handler; behaviour unreplayable from Msg log against empty State; truth-changing message lacks admitted carrier, graph function, runtime command or typed product contract; external data enters UX state without runtime validation; reachable, mutating or proof-used scaffold/debug surface lacks §12 exemption record; local ADR/convention/existing code weakens the profile; sprint claims closure with deferred proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold or authority debt unclassified or un-ticketed. Repetition does not normalise violations: repair or reprice.

conditions: A UX surface review is performed under the profile.
The sprint-specific question applies if the work used a UX sprint.
semantic.statement: Review should answer: State/Msg/Update; Cmd/Sub algebra; bound contracts; truth-changing messages' admitted carriers; membrane location and interpreted Cmds; provable View=f(State) purity; Msg-log replay proof; shared-contract import of all consumed types; runtime validation of all out-of-process payloads; documented view/membrane/accessibility/scaffold/debug exemptions; chosen stack's preservation of the Elm process model; non-ownership of replay continuation by the view; design-module carrier set and structural diagram for closure; and, if a sprint was used, classification of every deferred proof/accessibility/carrier/scaffold/authority finding. Any unanswerable question makes the design module incomplete.
semantic.uncertainty: Answerability is not an instruction to evaluate a particular surface here.

conditions: A surface review is evaluated on its exact basis.
semantic.statement: compliant→satisfied requires §§4–10 under inspection, no §13 failure and every §14 question answered from the design module. violation→falsified when a failure pattern, §4-rejected realisation or broken §§4–10 rule supplies a counterexample. design_module_incomplete→invalid_basis applies only with no violation counterexample and an unanswered design-module question, which is named. The source chooses the stricter §§4–10 test over the competing §§4–8 compliance test and retains the disagreement for authority. Ambiguity requires the stricter fixed interpretation; ambiguity alone cannot yield compliant. If an undefined required term prevents fixing a stricter interpretation, return out_of_frame naming term and owner. Repricing and scoped exemption are re-entry/scope, not results.
semantic.uncertainty: The two §4 tests and §1 authority are only described here, not supplied directly.

conditions: The relevant predicate is evaluated; closure obligations apply where product-UX closure is claimed.
exceptions: A recorded exemption can cover a closure obligation.
Inside an open UX sprint closure is not claimed; deferred obligations are escrow.
semantic.statement: For replay: replay_passes→satisfied iff injected deterministic values reproduce expected final State and ordered Cmds without a §8-prohibited correctness dependency; replay_fails→falsified for divergence or such a dependency, naming it. Replaying unresolved outcomes establishes replay only, not external completion. For closure: closure_obligations_met→satisfied requires every meaningful interaction family's proof and surface accessibility declarations or applicable recorded exemptions; closure_unproven→falsified identifies a missing uncovered proof/declaration. For carrier admission: carrier_admitted→satisfied requires every truth-changing message/action to map to a §3-admitted carrier and bind to the published AssetSurface contract, otherwise the equivalent typed contract named in the design module; carrier_missing→falsified identifies a message/action without admitted carrier or typed contract.
semantic.uncertainty: The §8 forbidden-dependency list and detailed carrier admission law are outside the supplied source.

semantic.statement: Every mapping carries its own predicate, maps to exactly one core result and cannot raise standing or satisfy another predicate. Where no refinement applies, return indeterminate for undecidable admissible evidence and name deciding evidence; out_of_frame for undeclared required relation/capability; invalid_basis for unsupported subject/basis other than design_module_incomplete. Missing carrier yields carrier_missing for admission and violation for review; a construction step needing it stops with re_entry_requested(authority), naming carrier, design owner and re-entry to author it or reprice the requirement. This is distinct from ACTIVATION ambiguity blocked; design_module_incomplete is distinct from construction incomplete. Exempt scaffold is scope, not result; evaluations outside its scope use this algebra. TICKETS close classes are not mapped here.
semantic.uncertainty: ACTIVATION owns the construction-stop mapping; its full semantics are not supplied.

conditions: World-model publication occurs under this profile.
semantic.statement: The declared binding runs profile→tier 1: FOUNDATIONS Object's scoped identity, boundary, state and material relations, plus P3's boundary proof obligation, bind to published entity cut and §9 admissibility. Identity declaration and survival under admissible change, and boundary proof, are preserved; here change means treatment across adjacent domains. Changes to §9, FOUNDATIONS Object or P3 require re-evaluation. Clauses name their requiring principles. Imports include FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, IDENTITY, SPEC_METHOD, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, RELEASE and TICKETS under PROFILES §1, without redefining their objects; ODD is the graph-execution profile.
semantic.uncertainty: Imported members' complete definitions and principle laws are not supplied.

semantic.statement: The profile claims institutional systems often retain values while losing interpretive context. Records require function, provenance and treatment context; mappings treat governed meaning; catalogs and schemas project deeper semantics. World-model work traces authoritative sources, records accepted semantic claims in ledgers and publishes bounded cuts as inspectable, versioned, machine-reasonable truth supporting probabilistic reasoning and correspondence.
semantic.uncertainty: These are source-authored position claims, not empirical findings established by this interpretation.

semantic.statement: The two constitutional intents are building published domain artifacts and composing them into higher-order world models. Query, traversal and serving are delivery concerns, potentially later realised through a dedicated plane, without redefining those intents.

Observe before standardising; comprehend enacted meaning before schema flattening; use bounded functional domains and contextual data evidence; recover experts' implicit objects, boundaries, states, transitions, treatments and reference artifacts; materialise governed understanding rather than leave it in people/pipelines/detached documentation; provide conceptual knowledge beyond metadata; tether probabilistic reasoning before cross-domain alignment/comparison/interpretation; fully qualify names before deeper transformation; model cross-domain change through treatment/covariance/adjoint interpretation; publish immutable cuts with explicit supersession; compose without erasing local authority; keep probabilistic correspondence in epistemic overlays and compile accepted meaning where delivery needs volume; derive projections from the kernel without co-equal truth; permit generation only after descriptive grounding. Failure of these commitments excludes the source's world-model-driven characterisation.

conditions: World-model work adopts this profile.
semantic.statement: F21 imports F2 transitions/refinement, F3 results, F8 identity, F9 a_c calculus and F12 method binding; similarly spelled profile ledgers/cuts/overlays/treatments/projections are not calculus records by spelling. Adopted, non-foundational premises are I1 source sovereignty/non-replacement, I2 context-dependent records and pre-existing human object commitments, I3 probabilistic correspondence with deterministic volume delivery, I4 some geometric identity spaces. The table attributes consequences as follows: P1/P6+I1/I2→derived semantic truth; P3/P6+F8/I2 and P1 naming→qualified discriminated entity cuts; P4b/P6/P3+I1→recoverable immutable provenance; P1/P4b+F2/F9→declared treatments and traceable subordinate projections; P1/P3+F12→owner-preserving imports and directional specialisation; P6/P5+F3→candidate construct/gate and run-specific falsification; P3/P6/P4b+F9/I4→space-bound, verified, traceable directions; P2/P6/P0+I3→epistemic control and deterministic compilation; P2/P5/P4a→bounded saturation, explicit gaps, sparse publication and authority-preserving composition; P2→bounded proof wedge; P5/P6+F3→predicate-specific result mappings and no result for unrun verification. The source labels P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent, P0 recovered, P4b derived from P0/P2 given non-reacquirable step facts, and P5 derived from P0/P6 given open-world premises. Profile choices include constitutional intents/manifesto/evidence order, entity-cut surfaces and binding, append-only ledger and initial Git publication lane, five treatment fields and preferred projection order, Builder Project narrowing, working refinements/gate, mean-offset methods and exclusions/verification/publication/storage packages, plane split, preferred mesh, wedge/spec applicability and seven result refinements. Builder projects choose discrimination techniques; consumers choose carriers/layouts/schemas/storage; ACTIVATION owns treatment licensing and adequacy; FOUNDATIONS owns lineage concepts and hypothesis; PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns relation carrier coordinates.
semantic.uncertainty: These are authored derivation and ownership claims, not independently proved derivations.

conditions: A consumer enters a foundation-to-law rule.
semantic.statement: Consumer links preserve ownership and add no decisions. Derived-semantic-layer consumers are Flow Observe, Materialisation and plane split; ODD/UX defer world-model semantics without applying those rules. Entity-cut consumers include world-model definition, working refinements, epistemic status, Markov discovery obligations, sparse materialisation, geometric specialisation/verification and result predicates. Ledger/publication consumers include immutable Markov cuts and overlay supersession. Treatment/projection consumers are Flow Relate and Project. Builder Project consumes directional specialisation; GLOSSARY only locates it. Epistemic-status consumers include CONFORMANCE discriminator 12, FOUNDATIONS hypothesis, effective blanket, Markov theory, verification-versus-formal-blanket distinction and promotion-gate results. Overlay-construction consumers include variance exclusion, overlay/Markov units, geometric materialisation and direction/publication/storage/null-peer/unrun-verification results. Plane rules are applied by builder alignment/compilation and tooling; Output decides nothing. Saturation/composition consumers include sparse refinements, Materialise/Compose and result predicates. The proof wedge is adopting-builder policy, merely inventoried by PROFILES. Result evaluations belong to §§9–11/14; FOUNDATIONS owns the core without applying profile rules. Uncited opening §4, effective blanket, design relation, remaining units, opening §9 and Output apply the stated consequences and name principles; this omission from rows adds no authority.
semantic.uncertainty: Some consumer loci and all external consumer texts are unavailable; their asserted roles are retained without invented endpoints.

conditions: The selected complete method basis applies.
semantic.statement: SPEC_METHOD owns general process constitution; this profile is the primary world-model method refinement for existing-system observation and bounded publication. Its four exact lineage imports preserve FOUNDATIONS ownership and meanings, use the same concept identities in source and target, expand applicability and mint no aliases. A change to either context, any cited concept/taxonomy clause or selected basis invalidates import until re-evaluation. Same-spelled alternatives are not imported; GLOSSARY only locates meanings. For products both graph-native and world-model-driven, graph execution governs execution shape/traversal/product-authoring structure while WORLD_MODEL governs semantics/publication/composition; the profiles compose.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/2. Role and imports/Builder Project specialisation

conditions: World-model construction under this profile, using the same selected complete method release containing both cited clauses.
semantic.statement: The source-to-target specialisation has no inverse, equivalence or universal claim that every Source Project is a Builder Project. Preserve mutable next-cut workspace meaning and distinction from Release Cut, Product, Install and Artifact. Exclude general Source Projects lacking builder configuration and refuse substitution of installed builder Product or Install. FOUNDATIONS retains source ownership; WORLD_MODEL owns only the target. This clause is the normative relation carrier. Changes to either concept/context, basis, builder configuration relation or governed scope invalidate translation until owning authorities re-evaluate.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/3. What a world model is

semantic.statement: A world model should expose bounded-context objects, coherent boundaries, relevant state/transitions, supporting evidence, governing value lists/classifications, adjacent-domain reinterpretations, covariance and what is preserved/changed/aggregated/delayed/lost. It is not a replacement system of record, local-semantics-erasing monolith, generic catalog entry, copied warehouse or schema registry standing in for comprehension.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/3. What a world model is/Objectives

semantic.statement: The profile should produce bounded, inspectable, challengeable, evidence-backed, versioned, composable, projection-capable and machine-reasonable models. Successful use should enable explanation of a record's object and boundary, claim evidence, local source authority, downstream meaning-changing treatment, relations between differently treated objects, time-applicable classifications and downstream figures' explainability from upstream reality.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/3. What a world model is/Evidence hierarchy

exceptions: Source code, rules and configuration are used when available; their availability is never a prerequisite to comprehension.
semantic.statement: Use strongest available explanatory surfaces, with preferred order: realised behaviour and emitted records/events; available code/rules/configuration; interfaces/schemas; large-scale observational data; documentation/catalogs/operator testimony. Code is high-fidelity when available, but realised behaviour is broader for proprietary, partially visible or output-intelligible systems.
semantic.uncertainty: This is a preference ordering, not a rule excluding lower-ranked evidence.

semantic.statement: The profile rejects fixed-set blanket membership: for any domain attribute basis, firing attributes are not a crisp partition, outside-set overwrites leak partial identity transfer, and individually insufficient attributes distribute identity. Geometric direction and behavioural support do not establish statistical conditional independence; the reading remains a candidate hypothesis subject to the promotion gate.
semantic.uncertainty: The universal attribute-basis claims are source assertions at working-hypothesis standing.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Four working refinements
WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Four working refinements

conditions: The construct or overlays built on it are in scope.
exceptions: The four refinements are not entity-cut admissibility conditions; §9 governs those.
semantic.statement: Four candidate commitments apply: geometric identity survival under treatment, not set membership; schemas partially sense/fragment identity and published overlays expose the axis rather than attribute profile alone; invariant semantic identity, not core size, discriminates objecthood, allowing sparse invariants but excluding rich clusters with no context invariant; identity is mean/DC offset from a null peer rather than dominant variance, excluding principal-component/maximum-variance identity constructions. Applications record their own boundary/overlay evidence; no refinement constitutes formal closure or replaces promotion.

exceptions: Entity cuts do not inherit the construct's candidate status; they stand on their own §9 admissibility.
semantic.statement: Adoption does not require established statistical Markov theory. Blanket claims remain candidate working commitments until a direction-native conditional-independence result meets its predicate for the exact subject and basis: given identity projection, residual variation in remaining components should be independent of the target under plausible treatments. No qualifying result preserves candidate standing; failed runs falsify only their run predicate without moving the gate or by themselves falsifying the construct. Published overlays are candidate-class, not certified blankets. Unadmitted candidate entities remain candidates; lawful published entity cuts do not. Downstream tooling should default to candidate-class publication and reserve formally closed kinds for real gate-backed cuts.
semantic.uncertainty: No statistical test procedure, threshold or actual run is supplied.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Relation to the design profile

conditions: A Markov object is read as a candidate identity-bearing cut.
semantic.statement: Good boundary design should prefer the smallest lawful carrier set preserving real authority; subordinate payloads unless independently authoritative; resistance to promoting sensed fragments into peer objects without irreducible need; and strongly typed semantic boundaries rather than fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned identities. This is one theoretical account of DESIGN_MODULE's general engineering law, not an established-theory prerequisite for all design work.
semantic.uncertainty: DESIGN_MODULE §8's analogue account is not supplied.

semantic.statement: Operational truth stays with enacting systems; the model derives semantics and externalises existing expert understanding. Data is constrained-function evidence and invalid in isolation from context. Every treatment declares preserved structure, changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity; ACTIVATION owns refinement licensing, and meaning-changing treatments are approximate steps with adequacy relations. Fully qualified naming is mandatory. Changing classifications/code sets/value lists are governed temporal artifacts. API and schema contracts project structure/function and are not highest semantic authority. Canonical cuts should remain bounded semantic identities; probability belongs in epistemic overlays, distinct from accepted treatments, publications and compiled execution.
semantic.uncertainty: ACTIVATION's licensing and adequacy laws and IDENTITY's full naming law are external dependencies.

conditions: Builder projects start from looser object candidates.
semantic.statement: Publication converges looser candidates into entity cuts or explicitly leaves them as non-object treatment, covariance or temporal-reference artifacts. Markov theory explains recovered boundaries rather than authorising invention of entities: institutional objects are already committed in code, records, workflows, schemas or policy. Optional geometric overlays add representation-substrate obligations without replacing ordinary recovery.

exceptions: Align, Compile and Serve/query are optional; Compile concerns actual execution needs and Serve/query depends on justified delivery needs.
semantic.statement: Observe strongest available behaviour/records/events/code/configuration/interfaces/schemas/docs/metadata; Trace source locators so later claims should re-enter concrete spans, fields, paths or records; Extract reviewable inventories and object/event/lifecycle/treatment/authority candidates and ambiguity registers, which are not yet the model; Assure should expose claim, observed/derived/interpreted/composed status, supporting sources, aspect-specific authority and gaps; Ledger accepted qualified claims append-only; Bound by function, authority, state and adjacency, rejecting schema-first or vocabulary-cluster modelling; Materialise ledger-derived cuts, permitting bounded, distinguishable, evidence-backed sparse publication; Relate treatments/covariance/adjoints/temporal references; Publish immutable cuts without overwriting, with Git/filesystem sufficient at low volume; Compose recursively, inspectably and boundedly without erasing local authority; optional Align yields epistemic candidates/rankings/ambiguities/mapping/anomaly suggestions, not published truth; Project tables, schema/API/event contracts, mapping documents, transformation specifications, covariant transforms, tests and applicable scaffolds from one kernel; optional Compile accepted understanding into deterministic jobs/plans/records/implementation, with scale execution recommended through compiled artifacts rather than per-row inference; optional Serve/query exposes published/composed models via filesystem or later query plane.
semantic.uncertainty: This records the source's staged procedure without performing any stage.

conditions: An entity cut is published.
exceptions: Outside a declared representation space, the boundary law is discharged semantically under §9.
semantic.statement: Every published cut is prompt-sufficient for reasoning and should expose the eight surfaces. Boundary means identity survival under adjacent-domain treatment, not attribute membership; schemas evidence identity. In a declared representation space, the boundary takes low-rank geometric form, and overlays should expose evidence plus the identity-recovering projection.
semantic.uncertainty: Prompt sufficiency is asserted by the source; no concrete cut is assessed.

semantic.statement: A materialised cut is builder-authored canonical object-level semantic truth, not a raw source emission or replacement operational source. Published artifacts should be versioned and explicitly superseded. The provenance sequence is source→tracing→assurance→attribute ledger→entity cut. A cut selects bounded identity/boundary with evidence and acceptance basis; one ledger state can support multiple identities, boundaries and contexts. Each accepted attribute should be recoverable through its cut, supporting entries, assurance and traced sources; attributes should not lack ledger support, entries assurance or assurance traceable sources. §10 applies only to geometric selections.

Published truth should be immutable per cut, diff-reviewable, evidence-traceable and explicitly superseded rather than silently overwritten. Both distinct ledgers should remain append-only and replayable. Initial publication can use filesystem and Git; a later database is a query complement, not constitutional publication authority.
semantic.uncertainty: Other clauses state cut immutability categorically; this clause's 'should' wording is preserved.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication/Attribute ledger law

semantic.statement: The ledger immediately supplies entity-cut semantics. Each entry should be fully qualified and may include quantities, rules, classifications, topology/relations, provenance/authority and effective/observed/publication coordinates. One or more document, code or data evidence surfaces may support it. The assumption is one lawful claim record per accepted attribute fact, not one source per attribute.
Construct cuts by recovering already-committed operating-model boundaries from authoritative sources and qualifying them into published truth; do not invent entities.

The whole constitutional test is explicit, traceable eight surfaces and discrimination from plausible alternatives at evidence altitude proportional to the claim, without prescribing builder technique. Each surface may state a value, absence, or non-applicability with reason. Missing adjacent treatment is stated, not manufactured. Sparse, unique, historical, single-context, inaccessible or regulated entities remain publishable when the test holds and residual ambiguity is declared. Missing comparison populations, repeated contexts or intervention permission bound evidence altitude and must be stated; they are not publication bars.

A cut explains why its boundary rather than a nearby operationally distinct boundary; stronger claims need stronger discrimination. Semantic adjoint round-trips perform the analogous role of geometric boundary tests. Where intervention is possible it discriminates more strongly than declaration, and cuts should state which evidence kind supports them. Field-set-only boundaries are weaker than boundaries naming identity-preserving reinterpretations and should be read accordingly.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/9. Entity cut construction/Publishing a cut

conditions: An entity cut is published or its identity/boundary revised.
semantic.statement: Publish all eight surfaces visibly and traceably with lawful surface values and discrimination basis. Cuts are immutable: changed identity or boundary creates a superseding cut. Consumer-selected storage form must preserve all published surfaces.

conditions: The builder operates in a declared learned representation, ledger embedding or equivalent metric space where identity is a geometric direction.
exceptions: Overlay construction is not required for ordinary institutional recovery.
semantic.statement: §10 specialises entity construction only on the stated representation substrate. Use the directional, interventional procedure and retain its minimum structure on publication. Representation space is part of the overlay; a direction without its space is uninterpretable and directions computed in different spaces do not compose.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Paired evidence collection

conditions: Overlay construction under §10 applies.
semantic.statement: Collect candidate ledger evidence across multiple contexts and at least one structurally similar null peer lacking candidate identity content in the same contexts. Pair candidate/context and null/context entries to separate identity from context signal. Distributed ledger entries remain evidence, not the object.

conditions: Overlay identity-direction extraction is performed.
exceptions: Supervised variants are admissible only when targeting mean offset rather than within-class variance.
semantic.statement: Derive a low-rank projection over paired evidence, canonically d(object)=μ(evidence_object)−μ(evidence_null) across contexts. Linear-discriminant, logistic-regression-normal and difference-in-conditional-means variants may target mean offset. Principal-component and maximum-variance constructions are inadmissible identity directions regardless of verification; a direction is a geometric combination, not a column.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Verification by treatment

conditions: A candidate direction is considered for acceptance/publication.
exceptions: The underlying entity cut remains independently lawful and publishable without the overlay.
semantic.statement: Acceptance requires identity preservation under held-out treatment and at least one recorded acceptable verification: α-sweep x−α·d showing expected identity shift and saturation in held-out contexts; transplant x+α·d showing null-peer identity acquisition; or outside-projection-support overwrite showing survival. No acceptable verification leaves a candidate; publication then violates Representation law. Passing verifies publication, not formal Markov closure.
semantic.uncertainty: The results section additionally excludes acceptance when any recorded verification shows identity lost.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Core and coat decomposition

conditions: The candidate appears in multiple contexts.
semantic.statement: Decompose evidence into invariant core, whose identity-direction contribution is stable across ≥ N of N contexts, and context-selected coat carrying reinterpretation. Both are evidence; core carries identity and coat treatment. Coat/core ratio characterises rather than measures quality.
semantic.uncertainty: The source does not define N or a numerical stability criterion.

conditions: Before overlay publication, an accepted Markov object is discriminated from incidental clusters.
semantic.statement: Compare null peers before publication. Shared core-size range is expected and acceptable, not diagnostic. Identity-loaded core attributes should be unique among peers and direction transfer should be cleaner than a random diagonal. Failure of uniqueness or transfer leaves a cluster not yet lawful even with internally consistent invariants, as the result mapping makes explicit.
semantic.uncertainty: No operational uniqueness or transfer-quality threshold is specified.

conditions: An overlay is published.
exceptions: Effective coordinate α is included where applicable.
semantic.statement: Expose versioned declared space and attribute basis; vector/equivalent projection; core/coat evidence traced to ledger; verification treatments/outcomes/held-out contexts; identity-preserving projection support; null-peer tests and accept/reject decisions; and applicable α coordinate. Overlay projections are immutable. Revising directions for new contexts/evidence/refitted spaces creates supersession; any representation-space change supersedes every direction even if ledger entries did not change. Never mutate prior overlays in place.

conditions: An overlay is stored.
exceptions: The supersession record identifies a replaced overlay if any.
semantic.statement: Store a package attached to the entity cut, not merely a table row or membership list: space/version, direction/support geometry, ledger evidence pointers, treatment/context/outcome verification trace, accepting authority and assurance provenance, and supersession record. Losing any surface makes storage unlawful; downstream query/projection conveniences cannot substitute.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/11. Saturation, composition and projection/Saturation law

semantic.statement: Builders may repeatedly work a bounded source-object set until judged sufficiently saturated: material attributes have traceable support, remaining gaps are explicit ambiguities, and the cut is stable enough to publish and later supersede. Sparse publication remains lawful; silently creating unsupported attributes does not.
semantic.uncertainty: Materiality and publishable stability are bounded judgment criteria, not numeric thresholds supplied here.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/11. Saturation, composition and projection/Composition law

semantic.statement: Build local publications/cuts before stitching; do not start with a central monolith. Composition preserves fragment authority, bounded meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and ambiguity without erasing artifacts. A federated mesh is preferred. Developing topology may remain Product-local; profile mesh law should be ratified only after reusable node/edge structure stabilises.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/11. Saturation, composition and projection/Projection law

exceptions: Trace temporal reference artifacts where applicable.
semantic.statement: All projections should trace governing objects, evidence, treatments, covariance, adjoints and applicable temporal references; the semantic kernel stays primary. Tables/schemas/APIs/mapping documents/covariant transforms publish the same kernel. Preferred order is world model→API contract→schema contract because APIs usually carry more business meaning. Query/traversal may be a first-class delivery pillar without constitutional-core status.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/12. Planes, proof and development/Control plane and data plane

semantic.statement: Probabilistic systems belong primarily in semantic control and should aid comprehension, candidate alignment, ambiguity reduction and correspondence ranking. When semantic understanding is accepted and compilable, they should not execute large-scale data movement row by row.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/12. Planes, proof and development/Proof law

exceptions: Compilation proof is additionally recommended where the line is mature enough.
semantic.statement: Adoption should not await winning standardisation. Preferred incremental wedge: comprehend one bounded source slice, publish a fragment, stitch an adjacent fragment, answer a difficult incumbent-pipeline question, emit conventional and covariant outputs together. The practical obligation demonstrates both output classes from one semantic substrate rather than immediate central convergence. Mature lines should also demonstrate deterministic compilation retaining traceability and challengeability.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/12. Planes, proof and development/World-model-driven development

exceptions: Simpler lines can use world model→application projections→implementation.
semantic.statement: World-model development parallels spec-driven development: specifications are usually normative and models descriptive. Well-formed models can project application surfaces without duplicate semantic authoring. Preferred route is world model→epistemic correspondence overlay→deterministic compiled artifacts→implementation. Use normative application specs for primarily interaction, workflow choice, non-domain behaviour or extra-domain operational policy; use models as substrate where software mainly interfaces stable domain reality.

conditions: The profile is working as intended.
exceptions: Inspectable Markov overlays apply where a representation space is selected; compiled execution artifacts apply where real volume must move safely.
semantic.statement: Expected outcomes are durable published domain artifacts, composed models, primary entity cuts, applicable inspectable Markov overlays, explicit treatment/covariance semantics, grounded epistemic correspondence overlays, temporal reference artifacts, familiar projections, applicable deterministic execution artifacts and a basis for AI reasoning over institutional meaning.
semantic.uncertainty: This is a conditional output account, not evidence that any output exists.

grounds.heading: WORLD_MODEL/13. Output and companion surfaces/Companion surfaces

semantic.statement: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional specification method; RELEASE owns immutable-cut publication and version-line selector promotion for installed bases; TICKETS owns bounded execution from discovery. Research can support/challenge hypotheses but neither amend this profile nor replace promotion. Working-commitment changes follow SPEC_METHOD §4 under governing authority.
semantic.uncertainty: The companion methods themselves are not supplied.

conditions: Cut admissibility or saturation is evaluated.
semantic.statement: Cut predicate: eight surfaces explicit/traced/discriminated at claim-proportional altitude. cut_admissible→satisfied for lawful stated value/absence/non-applicability with reason, tracing and discrimination, including declared evidence bounds and residual ambiguity; cut_inadmissible→falsified for missing lawful surface value, missing trace or evidence-established nondiscrimination, naming the surface/alternative; discrimination_undecided→indeterminate only without counterexample and with evidence unable to decide claimed discrimination, naming deciding evidence. Saturation predicate: material support, explicit gaps and stable publishable cut. saturated→satisfied when all three hold, carrying gaps as residuals; not_saturated→falsified when any fails, naming unsupported attribute, silent gap or other counterexample. Lawful absence/non-applicability is a surface value, not a non-satisfied result.

conditions: Direction acceptance is evaluated.
exceptions: Unrun verification has its own no-result rule when neither extraction_inadmissible nor representation_space_invalid applies.
semantic.statement: direction_verified→satisfied requires admissible extraction in declared space, at least one recorded acceptable held-out preservation and no recorded loss. extraction_inadmissible→falsified for principal-component/maximum-variance construction regardless of verification. verification_failed→falsified for admissible extraction with recorded held-out identity loss. verification_inconclusive→indeterminate requires admissible extraction and declared space, a verification that actually ran, no acceptable preservation or loss, and names deciding treatment/verification. representation_space_invalid→invalid_basis applies without extraction/verification counterexample when space is undeclared or directions from different spaces are composed.

conditions: The corresponding publication, storage, null-peer or gate-run predicate is evaluated.
semantic.statement: Publication: published_verified→satisfied for recorded acceptable verification; published_unverified→falsified for publishing without it. Storage: storage_retained→satisfied for all six package surfaces; storage_lossy→falsified naming any lost surface. Null-peer discrimination: null_peer_discriminated→satisfied for core-attribute uniqueness and cleaner-than-random-diagonal transfer; not_yet_lawful→falsified if either fails, naming the test. Promotion: gate_met→satisfied when that run meets the conditional-independence predicate; gate_not_met→falsified only that run, leaving construct standing unchanged. Construct candidate/established standings and candidate/formally-closed publication kinds are not results.

Mappings preserve their own predicate and standing and combine only in the core. Where no refinement applies, indeterminate names evidence needed to decide, out_of_frame identifies required undeclared relation/capability, and invalid_basis covers unsupported subject/basis beyond representation_space_invalid. Without extraction-inadmissible or invalid-space grounds, unrun verification yields no direction-acceptance result, never indeterminate or another core value, and leaves the direction candidate. In conjunction it is a planned assessment without closed result if planned, otherwise uncovered coverage. A stopped construction needing that verification is incomplete for ACTIVATION's candidate-available predicate, never indeterminate, with unrun work retained as residual. Publishing it still yields published_unverified.
semantic.uncertainty: External conjunction and construction mappings are referenced but not fully supplied; no evaluation is performed here.

semantic.statement: The guide prescribes claim and reason without performative framing for technically fluent, time-constrained readers.

exceptions: One claim per sentence is qualified by 'when possible'; examples are permitted only when reducing ambiguity.
semantic.statement: Prefer direct positive statements and precise technical vocabulary; remove announcing setup paragraphs; use concrete nouns/verbs instead of promotional language; keep one claim per sentence when possible; restrict examples to ambiguity reduction; prohibit tone-only filler transitions.

Remove the habits 'not X, but Y', 'simply', 'just', 'clearly', 'obviously', 'powerful', 'robust', 'seamless', 'game-changing', generic reassurance and dramatic phrasing, which usually add tone without information.
semantic.uncertainty: The source characterises these as habits; this is not interpreted as a ban on quoting those words as data.

semantic.statement: Good prose is factual, bounded, explicit about authority/uncertainty and challengeable. Cut polished sentences carrying no new constraint or observation.
Bad-prose criteria are ungrounded implied conclusions, paraphrastic repetition, unlabelled mixing of reality and intent, basic explanations to experts and branding of straightforward instructions.
Method tone should be constitutional, requirements normative, design structural and commentary analytical. Rewrite tone that does not match its authority layer.

conditions: A specification artifact is being written.
exceptions: Design detail belongs in constitutional layers only when the detail is itself constitutional.
semantic.statement: State live truth rather than narrated transition, keep sentences in their proper layer, remove stale law and exclude nonconstitutional design detail from constitutional layers. Cut sentences changing no authority, constraint or derivability.

conditions: A specification artifact is written or revised.
semantic.statement: Check downstream derivability, current truth rather than work in progress, and whether any sentence belongs lower. Rewrite or delete when an answer is wrong.

conditions: Constitutional specification or current-surface writing is in scope.
exceptions: Explicit version labels are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings or clearly historical/superseded material.
semantic.statement: The guide attributes force to SPEC_METHOD §2: constitutional specification uses present tense; nonlive material is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary; version labels have the stated restricted uses. During change waves the guide prefers active, current, base, live, shared and tenant-local.
semantic.uncertainty: The owning SPEC_METHOD clause and release-boundary rules are not supplied.

conditions: A JSON instance is checked against this schema.
semantic.statement: Root is a closed object requiring kind='stdo.installed-release-manifest', schema_version=1, release, standards and auxiliary. release is closed and requires cut, tag_object, commit, tree and standards_tree. cut is a string matching ^v(?!.*-rc\..*-rc\.)[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]*-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*$. Git identifiers are strings matching ^[0-9a-f]{40}([0-9a-f]{24})?$; SHA-256 values match ^[0-9a-f]{64}$. These are syntactic schema constraints, not verification of referenced Git objects or bytes.

conditions: Any project_release_namespace, qualified_ref, project_subtree_root or project_subtree_tree release property occurs.
exceptions: The four properties may all be absent.
semantic.statement: Any project coordinate requires the other three. Namespace is a nonempty string matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$; qualified_ref matches ^refs/tags/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*/v[^/]+-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*$; project_subtree_tree is a Git identifier. project_subtree_root is a nonempty string matching ^(?:\.|(?!/)(?!.*(?:^|/)(?:\.|\.\.)(?:/|$))(?!.*//).+)$: literal '.' or a non-absolute path without dot/dot-dot segments or doubled slash. No equality between qualified_ref's namespace/cut and other fields is expressed.

exceptions: member_set_sha256 is optional in generic memberSet and auxiliary.plugin but required in standards.
semantic.statement: memberSet is a closed object requiring nonempty string source_root/installed_root, integer member_count≥0 and members array, with optional SHA-256 member_set_sha256. Members are closed objects requiring nonempty string path matching ^(?!/)(?!.*(?:^|/)\.\.(?:/|$)).+$ and SHA-256 sha256. uniqueItems prohibits duplicate complete member objects; it does not prohibit equal paths with different hashes. No minItems, ordering rule or member_count/length equality is expressed. standards intersects memberSet with fixed roots specification/standards and standards and required set hash. auxiliary.plugin intersects memberSet with both roots plugins/spec.
semantic.uncertainty: Schema inventory syntax alone does not establish actual installed membership or hash correctness.

semantic.statement: auxiliary is closed and requires plugin, license and release_note. license is closed and requires path='LICENSE' and SHA-256 sha256. release_note is closed and requires string source_path matching ^releases/v[^/]+\.md$, installed_path='release/release-note.md' and SHA-256 sha256. No cross-field equality ties source release-note name to release.cut.

conditions: Structural validation of an overlay against the supplied schema.
semantic.statement: The root is an object requiring exactly the declared root fields $schema, kind, product, constitution, local_constitution, reference_frame_bases, what, how, ticketing and composition; kind is stdo.product-definition and $schema is referenceUri. Every object shape defined in this schema excludes additional properties. Product requires definition_id: identityUri, nonempty string name, source_project: referenceUri and bounded_context. The bounded_context property is required but its value is either null or an object requiring id: identityUri and definition: referenceUri; it describes an optional enclosing context, not an exhaustive registry of subordinate, peer, composed, tenant, user or runtime contexts.

conditions: Structural validation against the supplied schema.
semantic.statement: Constitution requires stdo: stdoBinding, additional_authorities: references, entrypoints: a nonempty unique array of constitutionalEntrypoint objects, and agent_bootstrap: agentBootstrap. Local constitution requires unique arrays axioms: localAxiom, overrides: localOverride and disambiguations: localDisambiguation, each permitting zero items. reference_frame_bases is a nonempty unique array of referenceFrameBasis. WHAT requires intent and product referenceUri values and specification: nonEmptyReferences. HOW requires common: references and build_tenants: a nonempty unique array of buildTenant. Composition is a unique array of compositionEdge permitting zero items. Array uniqueness is item uniqueness; unique definition or tenant identities are separately checked by conformance.

conditions: Structural validation against the supplied schema.
semantic.statement: Ticketing requires goals: referenceUri, tickets and comments: carrierRoot; sprints: carrierRoot is optional. Tickets requires root: referenceUri and lanes; lanes requires backlog, active and completed, each referenceUri. carrierRoot requires root: referenceUri. No additional properties are permitted in ticketing, tickets, lanes or carrierRoot.

conditions: Values use the schema's reusable scalar and collection definitions.
semantic.statement: identityUri is a nonempty string annotated uri; referenceUri is a nonempty string annotated uri-reference. Conformance additionally requires assertion-capable validators for both formats. references is a unique array of referenceUri permitting empty; nonEmptyReferences additionally requires at least one item. sha256 is a string matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}$. stdoChannelUri intersects identityUri with ^stdo://channels/(?![^/]*-rc\.)[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]*/?$. stdoReleaseUri intersects identityUri with ^stdo://releases/v[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]*-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*/?$. These distinct patterns permit optional terminal slash and require a positive, non-zero-leading RC number for a release.

stdoBinding requires source, selector and basis. Source requires repository: referenceUri identifying the Git repository carrying the selected release line and immutable RC cuts. Selector is stdoChannelUri and is never operative constitutional authority without digest-bound explicit resolution and adoption. Basis requires uri: stdoReleaseUri identifying the exact immutable installed cut and manifest_sha256: sha256 identifying its deterministic installed-release manifest. constitutionalEntrypoint requires basis and uri, both referenceUri; its reading URI resolves relative to the referenced constitutional basis. These objects disallow additional properties.

conditions: A declared agent bootstrap target is processed under manager conformance.
semantic.statement: agentBootstrap is a closed object requiring entrypoint: referenceUri to the constitutional entrypoint loaded by the stable bootstrap and targets: a nonempty unique array of bootstrapTarget. Targets identify instruction files relative to product.source_project whose marker-bounded projection is manager-controlled. bootstrapTarget intersects referenceUri with ^(?![A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:)(?!//)(?!/)(?!\.\.(?:/|$))(?!.*\/\.\.(?:\/|$))[^?#\\]+$. Manager conformance additionally confines the resolved file to source_project and refuses absolute paths, authorities, parent traversal, queries, fragments, backslashes, symlinks and reparse points.
semantic.uncertainty: The structural pattern does not by itself perform filesystem confinement or symlink/reparse-point checks.

conditions: Structural validation of the named binding objects.
semantic.statement: localAxiom and referenceFrameBasis each require uri: referenceUri plus authority and applies_to: nonEmptyReferences. localOverride requires these and overrides: nonEmptyReferences. localDisambiguation requires uri and resolves_to: referenceUri, term: nonempty string, context: identityUri, and disambiguates, authority, basis and applies_to: nonEmptyReferences. buildTenant requires id: identityUri, root: referenceUri, design and implementation: nonEmptyReferences. compositionEdge requires product_definition and relation: referenceUri, target_definition_id: identityUri and contracts: nonEmptyReferences. Every listed object disallows additional properties.

The owning carrier selects the exact resolves_to concept; conformance separately verifies its membership in the complete material disambiguates candidate set for the declared term, context, basis and scope. Authority references must be existing lawful owners of the resolution and any cross-context relation; bases are those needed to interpret candidates and resolution; applies_to identifies exact governed scopes. For cross-context resolution the carrier declares the complete authorized import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation relation.
semantic.uncertainty: The schema does not itself prove ownership, semantic completeness or candidate membership.

conditions: Before constitutional work in the scope routed by each respective bootstrap template.
semantic.statement: Each template prescribes the same ordered prework: resolve the applicable scoped stdo_<label>.json; use constitution.stdo.basis rather than selector; resolve and verify that exact installed release through the manager; load the declared bootstrap entrypoint then exact owning standards as needed; resolve the applicable accepted frame basis or declared composition; bind exact outcome, basis and existing work grant. Direct Writer entry requires both accepted-configuration permission and one sufficient capable context; material coordination uses Executive or the declared equivalent. Only applicable dependency-ready evaluations may activate, with unknown applicability and required independence preserved. Executive cannot mutate files or Git; those effects require separate Writer activation. Missing, ambiguous, stale or out-of-scope Product Definition, frame basis, subject, authority or activation causes fail-closed behavior.
semantic.uncertainty: This records the two templates' prescribed workflow without performing it or supplying missing admission law.

semantic.statement: In each template, mutable methodology source, another installed version, a cache entry and the bootstrap cannot replace the selected exact basis. Prompts, summaries, symbolic maps and prior results may route attention but cannot replace current source authority or a closed frame result.

conditions: Filling the Project Goals document.
semantic.statement: State current overriding concerns in present tense; resolve and verify the applicable Product Definition's exact installed STDO basis while filling the document. Explain goals' project role and difference from intent, product definition and requirements; list active current-wave goals. Each goal should orient work and should not masquerade as a requirement or release version label.

conditions: Filling the Project Intent document.
semantic.statement: State project direction in present tense; resolve and verify the exact installed basis declared by the applicable Product Definition while filling the document. Describe why the project exists, list outcomes it must deliver and list its shaping constraints.

conditions: Filling the Project Product document.
semantic.statement: State current product realization in present tense and resolve/verify the applicable exact installed basis while filling the document. Describe product kind and provided domain; how goals focus one bounded body of work and feed intent and downstream product change; intended end-state shape concretely; and current realization in terms decomposable into requirements.

Declare every bounded context's stable identity, owning authority, applicable basis and governed scope; define key Product concepts used by downstream requirements/design. Spellings are labels, not context-free identities. When another context uses the same term, keep meanings isolated or declare the exact authorized import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation relation. Explicitly define material Product meanings, including user, tenant, account, actor, owner, frame and product where material; do not rely on a shared glossary default.

grounds.heading: Project Reference-Frame Basis/Exact Method And Optional Profile Basis

conditions: Completing and admitting a project frame-basis declaration.
semantic.statement: Replace every placeholder and admit through existing owners. Severity, priority, frame result, boundary effect and disposition remain distinct. No universal numeric scale is imposed. S0..Sn, P0..Pn and a P2 cutoff require exact declared direction/effect.
