Uncertain completion includes completion_unknown and not_effected with an unestablished end.
semantic.label: External effect outcome and end

semantic.definition: Total handling declares a next move for every admitted condition class, including an explicit unknown class. It does not assert recognition of every external condition, provider termination or completion of every request. A hanging call, unsatisfiable demand and lost post-effect response remain distinct cases.
semantic.label: Total handling and reconfiguration

semantic.definition: Refinement decomposes an outer transformation T: A → X with success predicates P₀ … Pₙ into steps. A rewrite replaces a representation, step or composite by another claimed to keep its meaning, including partitioning, regrouping, reordering, merging or substitution. Exact steps preserve meaning under the subject's declared interpretation; approximate steps instead require an adequacy relation and a composite end-to-end bound.
semantic.label: Refinement, rewrite, exactness and approximation

grounds.heading: ACTIVATION/4. Totality and refinement/Complete enclosing-relation admission

conditions: A material transition is proposed for admission.
semantic.definition: The complete enclosing admission relation includes every participant and equality join whose identity, validity, authority, currentness or transition can affect or be affected by admission, including relevant far sides of crossing seams. Each admission owner independently derives and validates it from authoritative inputs.
exceptions: A crossing seam's far side may be excluded when authoritative evidence establishes that it cannot participate.
semantic.label: Complete enclosing-relation admission

grounds.heading: ACTIVATION/4. Totality and refinement/Standing structural qualification

conditions: An admission owner and supported boundary are declared by accepted design.
semantic.definition: Standing structural qualification instantiates the admission law for every such owner and boundary, with case applicability determined by supported inputs, state and operating or threat model. It examines direct, composite or nested, forged, ambiguous, stale, incoherent, competing-authority, reconstructed, replay and atomic-publication-failure forms.
exceptions: Unsupported forms require a design-grounded not_applicable disposition and no weaker or competing path.
semantic.label: Standing structural qualification

semantic.definition: Work state is an object comprising the current persistent workspace, governing basis, applicable closed results and judgments with invalidators, residuals and known uncertainty over external effects. Resumption re-enters the same method from current material state, possibly with another actor. Checkpointing, resumption and progress accounting are carrier-independent procedures.
semantic.label: Work state, resumption and checkpoint

semantic.definition: Progress is accepted material movement toward the selected outcome. Prerequisite work names the obligation enabled; preservation and repeated proof are evidence without new progress; rejected or superseded construction is churn; discovering hidden distance revises the forecast without being negative progress. These are semantic categories, not a numeric progress algorithm.
semantic.label: Progress categories

grounds.heading: ACTIVATION/5. Work state and restart/The workspace and an actor's account

semantic.definition: The persistent workspace and authoritative inputs are the work's continuing truth surface. An actor's context is its bounded, revisable and disposable account, not a second truth surface. Later intake reconstructs governing relations without the prior actor's private context.
semantic.label: Workspace truth surface and actor account

semantic.definition: Proportionality relates semantic ambiguity removed to effective reasoning complexity introduced. Complexity includes independent concepts and authority surfaces, cross-document joins, exceptions, branching, states, transitions, reconciled duplicates and decision-relevant detail; it is not raw lines, artifact count or context-window size.
semantic.label: Proportionality

conditions: A cost claim is the governed question.
semantic.definition: A selected cost claim declares an allowance and reports spend measured under the selected execution binding or explicitly unmeasured. Material startup, framework processing, external computation, transport and assurance costs are distinct components. Transferred-context cost includes every delegated actor.
semantic.label: Selected cost claim

semantic.definition: A resource limit bounds context, attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or machine resources consumed by activation. Its intake, capability envelope or selected execution binding must declare it. This law supplies no numerical limit; the selected execution binding supplies values and measurable units and boundaries.
semantic.label: Declared resource limit

semantic.definition: A closed result identifies frame and activation, subject, basis, evaluation, actor, evidence, verdict, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. Its reuse depends on exact applicability and three invalidator kinds: material input change, changed basis and a declared revising observation that occurs.
semantic.label: Closed result and invalidators

grounds.heading: ACTIVATION/7. Closed result and reuse/Transition evidence

semantic.definition: Transition evidence is a consumer-represented read model identifying exact candidate, affected relations, changed realisation paths, added or removed authority paths, retained and open seams, focused and required integration proof, explicit non-changes, any activated assessor's recommendation and the owner's disposition once made. It is not specification, design or admission authority.
semantic.label: Transition evidence

semantic.definition: ASSURANCE is presented as a tier-2 owner of assurance and testing law: verification layers; testing taxonomy, proof authorities and portability; test authority; scenario bundles; installed development proof; significant paths; product testing frames; combinatorial coverage and testing value; legitimate-path and technical-debt erasure; evidence composition; subject acquisition; counterexample localisation; and interface integration. Its family table is F14. It consumes tier-1 laws without adding tier-1 definitions.
semantic.label: ASSURANCE document role

semantic.definition: The verification layers preserve distinct truths: requirements preserve invariant truth and ask what must be true; design preserves structural choice and asks how that truth is realised; scenarios preserve operational meaning and ask whether the realised system can do the claimed thing. Scenarios are concrete end-to-end product-owner use cases validating intent through realised behaviour.
semantic.label: Requirements, design and scenarios

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/1. Verification layers/Foundation to law: assurance and testing

semantic.definition: F14 is the source's foundation-to-law account for evidence about realised products and its organisation. Its additional instance premises are runnable product (source and deployed, installed or runnable forms can produce execution or observation evidence), composition (modules, interfaces and owners form causal paths), users (claims concern supported-surface outcomes), external boundaries (workers, transports or fixtures outside source), and designed modules (a design profile may govern a boundary and module ownership). Commitments do not supply these premises. Fourteen rows distinguish claimed consequences from domain and policy choices.
semantic.label: F14 assurance and testing foundation account

conditions: The selected complete STDO basis supplies the bounded context.
semantic.definition: The product-assurance bounded context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance. Its Product-level taxonomy distinguishes design or module conformance authority from UAT or acceptance authority independently of execution breadth. Conformance asks whether implementation realises the module or design boundary; UAT asks whether the composed product satisfies its claimed requirement or scenario.
semantic.label: Product-assurance proof taxonomy

semantic.definition: Sandbox UAT exercises an isolated composed product through declared application, public, runtime or control surfaces using a requirement-sourced scenario or acceptance case. Harnessed mode uses deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker or result surfaces; live mode uses a real configured worker, tool, agent, service or external probabilistic transport where the product depends on that boundary.
exceptions: An explicitly equivalent isolated composed-product proof lane may also be called UAT or acceptance testing.
semantic.label: Harnessed and live sandbox UAT

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/2. Testing strategy taxonomy/Fixture and proof portability

semantic.definition: Fixture and proof portability concerns reproducibility of required closure lanes from their declared source boundary and the classification or declared acquisition of external project evidence.
semantic.label: Fixture and proof portability

semantic.definition: Written test-case authority is traceable authority for each live requirement's proof. It includes each expected result's assertion provenance: owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation, shared dependencies and whether the asserted predicate is the obligation itself, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction.
semantic.label: Written test-case authority

semantic.definition: An ordered proving surface showing the exercised feature or use-case boundary, the test-case sequence and expected outcomes at significant steps, making operational meaning inspectable. Declared scenarios and use cases expose operational boundaries, sequences, actors, controls and outcomes and are the preferred source for identifying significant code and control paths.
semantic.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The system has an installable or runnable development form.
semantic.definition: The decisive proving lane exercises an installed development version as an independent project or externalised target.
semantic.label: Installed development proof

semantic.definition: Claim-relative meaningful paths deliberately named and exercised by the proving surface. Relevant paths usually include success, fail-closed or rejection, boundary or control, integration or dispatch or transport, and recovery or retry or replay.
semantic.label: Significant paths

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/The set

conditions: Governing frame configuration or admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion, closure or release-assurance claim.
semantic.definition: A claim-relative testing configuration ordinarily containing four distinct frames: user acceptance, end to end, integration and unit. Availability in this member does not activate the set or its supporting sections 8–13.
semantic.label: Product testing frame set

semantic.definition: A frame whose evaluation executes or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim using an explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification condition.
semantic.label: Testing frame

semantic.definition: The declared ordinary causal composition from a supported user or public entry through the exact selected interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery boundaries to the outcome projection required by the Product claim.
semantic.label: Authoritative Product path

semantic.definition: The claim-relative population of independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change an outcome, violate an invariant, select another authority path or expose failure. Unit dimensions include module-owned public-contract laws, algebraic operators, calculation regimes, states, transitions, boundary classes and failures; cross-participant interface, Product, persistence, configuration and user-role combinations belong to integration, end-to-end or user-acceptance frames.
semantic.label: Material combinatorial complexity

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/User-acceptance frame

conditions: The claim asks whether a declared user can obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary surface.
semantic.definition: The primary Product-outcome evidence frame for claims that a user can use the Product. Its subject is the exact deployed, installed or runnable form under current Product, requirement, UX, identity, policy and acceptance authority, declared role, environment and harnessed/live mode. Its manifold covers goals, entries, permissions, inputs, configuration, ordinary dependencies, declared worker/transport substitutions, visible state and outputs, refusals, recovery and acceptance interval. Coordinates bind Product/artifact identity, install, role, capability, configuration, dependency realisation, mode, data, workspace, invocation, time, outcome and scenario. Evidence includes actual supported requests/responses, visible projections, claimed durable effects, refusals, recovery, scenario records and exact subject/dependency identities. Capability requires acting as the declared user, perceiving material outcomes/refusals and detecting hidden setup or unsupported assistance.
semantic.label: User-acceptance frame

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/End-to-end frame

semantic.definition: Evaluates whether the exact runnable Product realises an outcome through every material interface, owner, state transition, effect, persistence, continuation, recovery and projection boundary of the complete authoritative path. Basis includes composition design, supported entry, selected owners/dependencies, ordinary runtime configuration and Product claim. The manifold includes entry-to-outcome producers/consumers, contracts, authority transitions, state, events, persistence, processes, continuation, retry, recovery, projections and competing paths. Coordinates identify artifact/install, entry, operation, definition/owner, path/edges, process, event prefix, state, configuration, dependency, result, replay and scenario. Evidence includes entry invocation, observed semantic path/authority edges, owner receipts, durable events, transitions, outputs, claimed replay/reconstruction, installed identity and negative paths. Capability requires observing the complete path without changing it, distinguishing rivals and reproducing material state/failure relations.
semantic.label: End-to-end frame

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/Integration frame

semantic.definition: Evaluates actual participants at one declared material composition boundary against their joint contract across outcome-changing state, authority, configuration, timing, failure and recovery combinations. Basis binds the exact declaration, actual implementations or exact admitted substitutes, Product/requirement/design law and interaction population. The manifold includes both sides, shared carriers, pre/postconditions, authority/ownership, ordering, state, configuration, failure, retry, recovery, translation and competing participants. Coordinates bind participant/version, interface/carrier revision, state, configuration, dependency, interaction case, input, output, failure and evidence. Evidence comprises exchanges, admitted carriers, transitions, contract verdicts, failures, retries, recovery, combinations and participant identities. Capability requires exercising/observing the seam, detecting substitution and varying every material interaction dimension.
semantic.label: Integration frame

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/Unit frame

semantic.definition: Evaluates one module-owned law across material operator, calculation-regime, state, transition, public/private boundary-class and failure combinations. Basis includes the exact module boundary, accepted ontology/design, active declared carrier inventory, owned requirements/public contracts, implementation and module-bounded decidable oracle. The manifold includes public contracts, algebras, calculations, parsers, reducers, state machines, transitions, combinators, admission predicates, conservation laws, invariants, numerical boundaries and failures. Coordinates bind module/implementation revision, law, operator/function family, state, input/boundary class, expected relation, generated case, mutation and result. Evidence includes law-derived examples, equivalence classes, available finite exhaustive cases, properties/generation, metamorphic relations, calculation/algebra oracles, boundary cases and killed internal mutations. Capability requires an independently law-derived oracle, identifying bounded combinations and distinguishing violations from implementation restatement.
semantic.label: Unit frame

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/8. Combinatorial coverage and testing value

semantic.definition: A claim-relative index of the material combinations a frame can discriminate. It considers at least subject/claim congruence, independent dimension number/materiality, covered interaction strength, authoritative-path exactness, oracle independence/precision, realistic-fault/rival-path/historical-failure sensitivity, observability/reconstruction/reproducibility, and explicit residual combinations/invalidation. It is not inherently a scalar.
semantic.label: Testing-value index

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/9. Legitimate path and technical-debt erasure

semantic.definition: Evaluation of two distinct finite subject-relative graphs: production closure over the exact runnable Product/configuration and transitive imports, exports, package paths, switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers, generated runtime artifacts, recovery and fresh-process reconstruction; and assurance/source closure over relied-on source consumers, fixtures, proof scripts, generators, mutations and assurance tools.
semantic.label: Technical-debt erasure

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/11. Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation

semantic.definition: Distinct acquisition and evaluation relations: acquire actual owner-issued subjects through exact runnable owner surfaces, validators, projections, receipts or reconstruction relations, then evaluate with an independently contract-derived oracle.
semantic.label: Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation

semantic.definition: Return of a testing counterexample to its earliest supported causal frontier: causally minimal violated owner relations or seam coordinates under the declared causal relation, not log or clock order. Its four exclusive domain forms are unique locus, jointly established incomparable earliest loci whose combined violation is necessary, unresolved alternative frontiers, and an unbounded frontier represented by indeterminate.
semantic.label: Counterexample localisation

conditions: Selected by governing frame configuration or admitted work authority under the exact selected basis.
semantic.definition: Composite refinement urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1, resolving in urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation owned by REFERENCE_FRAME. It relates public-boundary, design, operator, owner and proof evaluation to integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames. It asks whether one outcome remains constructable, understandable and correctly realised across its material interface chain with sufficient context and conserved meaning, authority and cause. Design subjects bind declared roles, functional paths, dependencies, configuration and capabilities; realisation subjects bind actual participants, callable selection, supported entry/exit and exact runnable artifact/install. Both bind an independent oracle, requirements/design, exact source/workspace checkpoint, contracts and finite cases. The manifold covers producers, consumers, transformations and effect owners, seam pre/postconditions, value/reference domains, lifecycle/time, context, mutable subject, refusals, observations and visible results. Coordinates distinguish Product, artifact/install, workspace, observation, invocation, candidate, admitted result and evidence, including revisions, domains, units, cardinality, ordering, empty/null/default meaning and validity intervals.
semantic.label: End-to-end interface integration refinement

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame/Claim boundaries

semantic.definition: Four distinct claims: contract sufficiency asks whether every participant can determine and perform its responsibility from declared interfaces/context; boundary congruence asks whether actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority; path realisation asks whether the exact runnable subject uses the authoritative entry-to-outcome path; user usability asks whether the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtains the outcome using only declared context, access and supported surfaces.
semantic.label: Interface refinement claims

grounds.heading: ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame/Computational whole-path evaluation

conditions: Material computational composition or recurrence work.
semantic.definition: Bounded composition of selected interface claims with evaluations of path operators, owners, reused foundations and proof, covering one complete producer-to-consumer path under DESIGN_MODULE computational-realisation and recurrence law. It binds fact establishment, every consumer, validity/invalidation, effects, retained alternatives and accumulated work, and evaluates equivalent computation across domain names without presuming semantic equivalence.
semantic.label: Computational whole-path evaluation

conditions: A new or materially changed realisation boundary is governed by a design profile.
semantic.definition: Two directed evidence chains: semantic derivation from constitutional WHAT and owning requirements through accepted ontology, declared carriers, target design and domain/sequence/state evidence to implementation and module-derived tests, reconciliation/acceptance, promotion/design-method closure; and feedback from implementation/tests through evidence, counterexamples or falsification to affected ontology/design relations. Assertion and execution provenance remain distinct.
semantic.label: Design-to-module evidence route

conditions: Unit tests under the design profile.
semantic.definition: Module-owned proof lanes derived from realisation authority owned by DESIGN_MODULE and from module ownership evidence. Their authority is for module proof; Product UAT and acceptance meaning remain with Product authority.
semantic.label: Module-derived unit lane

conditions: A boundary is governed by the design profile.
semantic.definition: Confirmation at the realisation boundary, before design-method closure, of the operational lifecycle of every designed module, function, application/runtime/plugin/public/data surface and published profile function or module. It consumes SPEC_METHOD §2 phases without redefining them; its checklist detects ambiguity about ultimate intended use and is neither a release plan nor a replacement for RELEASE.
semantic.label: Module lifecycle confirmation

semantic.definition: Subject-described Tier 1 STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, a_c: domain-specific and carrier-neutral, with stable identity urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c in urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus. Its member owns position/scope, signature, record shapes, AC-001–AC-020, traversals/functor kinds, interpretation/models, three layers, calculus identity, application/import/exclusion boundaries and conformance obligations. It consumes FOUNDATIONS ontology and core results without redefining them; clauses identify their requiring P0–P6 principles. Its definitions do not depend on derivation-record layout, selected interpretation, carrier, provider, runtime or repository topology.
semantic.label: Subject-described a_c calculus

semantic.definition: An interpreted model a_c.X is downstream of a_c plus exact subject X. A carrier a_c.X.C encodes that model with an exact accepted semantic judgment J_X and exact carrier C. Calculus, interpreted model and encoded carrier have separate content identities and proof boundaries.
semantic.label: Calculus, interpreted model and encoded carrier

semantic.definition: Finite local derivation owners cover scoped identity/authority and bounded-context meaning in FOUNDATIONS §2; bounded probabilistic construction in P0, Work boundary and ACTIVATION §1; delegation/candidate production/independent assessment in ACTIVATION §1 and EVALUATION §3; ambiguity/human adjudication/hard stops in ACTIVATION §4; exact basis, authority, evidence/verdict separation and results in RF-005–007 and FOUNDATIONS; constitutional derivation/re-entry in SPEC_METHOD §§1,4; closure/projection/residual/capability law in REFERENCE_FRAME §3; singular release authority in SPEC_METHOD §6 and PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4. AxiomaticCalculusBasis resolves these to immutable absolute clause addresses in derivation_basis.principle_refs. Generic F_D, F_P and F_H originate here, independently of equal-spelled runtime/profile/application terms.
semantic.label: Calculus derivation basis

semantic.definition: Material family F9's premise-to-rule account distinguishes derived consequences from owner-selected choices. Instance premises, not supplied by commitments, are: a finite model represents governed objects/relations/constraints/residuals/traversals/transformations/judgments; exact subject, interpreted model and possible carrier have separate identities; some predicates are mechanical and others need bounded probabilistic construction or explicit human adjudication. P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are marked independent; P0 recovered; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. Nineteen rows bind these premises to position, scope, signature, identity/typing, authority/basis, results, latitude, residuals, closure/projection, overlay, transformation, judgment separation, traversal/composition, interpretation, layers, identity issuance, application/import boundaries, constraint surfaces and qualification.
semantic.label: Foundation-to-law account

semantic.definition: Sigma = (RecordKind, Sort, RelationKind, ConstraintKind, ResidualKind, FunctorKind, JudgmentKind, StopKind). RecordKind_ac fixes eight urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind: identities ending semantic-object, typed-relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation and judgment. Each signature member is a finite closed identity set for one model family. The signature specifies fields/value domains, reference domains/cardinalities, relation endpoint sorts, constraint subject/predicate domains, residual subject/uncertainty/consequence/re-entry domains, judgment input/output/evidence/stop contracts and permitted traversal functor kinds.
semantic.label: Subject a_c signature

semantic.definition: M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J), with exact basis b, closed identity universe I and finite populations for semantic objects, directed relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations and judgments. Population_M is total over the eight core kinds. Local_M is their disjoint union; I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M. RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field) yields cardinality, allowed local kinds, semantic-object sorts, external target kinds and required basis relation.
semantic.label: Subject a_c model

semantic.definition: SemanticObject has exactly id, sort, context, owner, scope, basis and value. id/sort/context/owner/basis are identities; scope is the closed governed domain; value is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or an exact-content reference. It carries a FOUNDATIONS Object, with scoped identity in id/owner/sort and boundary in scope.
semantic.label: SemanticObject record

semantic.definition: TypedRelation has exactly id, kind, source, target, context, owner, scope, basis and qualifiers. Endpoints resolve into I; qualifiers is a closed kind-specific record carrying required direction, cardinality, preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other signature-defined semantics.
semantic.label: TypedRelation record

semantic.definition: Constraint has exactly id, kind, applies_to, predicate, context, owner, scope, basis, judgment_kind, latitude_ref and refusal. Its kind and judgment_kind resolve declared ConstraintKind and JudgmentKind; the owning signature supplies predicate language and judgment semantics.
semantic.label: Constraint record

semantic.definition: Explicit permission set within a constraint boundary, represented by Latitude with id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis and invalidation.
semantic.label: Latitude record

semantic.definition: First-class model uncertainty carrying FOUNDATIONS Residual, with fields id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry and invalidation. Its declared ResidualKind and lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains belong to the signature.
semantic.label: Residual record

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/4. Fundamental laws/AC-007 Constraint and refusal

semantic.definition: Subject-described constraint judgments and operation outcomes map to the FOUNDATIONS core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis without raising standing. A refinement maps each value to exactly one core value. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis), distinguished by cause and predicate.
semantic.label: Subject-described core results and stops

conditions: Seed set, dependency relation family, required-edge semantics, basis and scope are exact; the fixed point is finite and unique.
semantic.definition: Material closure is closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q)), the least lawful record closure under the exact dependency family R.
semantic.label: Material closure operation

semantic.definition: A meaning-preserving model view: project(M, Z, R) returns (M_Z, Boundary_Z), gap or refusal. M_Z contains the material closure; Boundary_Z records excluded, external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams.
semantic.label: Model projection

semantic.definition: Addition of explicit records to declared Population_M families of a basis model without mutating that basis.
semantic.label: Model overlay

semantic.definition: An operation-bearing specialisation of one exact traversal v. Its record t contains id, traversal, domain_model, codomain_model, context, owner, scope, basis, operation_authority, preconditions, preservation_relation, preserved, introduced, removed, external_preserved, external_introduced, external_removed, external_resolution_witnesses, residuals, evidence, provenance, stop_states, invalidation and re_entry. Its application T[t](M_b, inputs) returns a proposed successor M_b_prime*, hold, gap or refusal; the input remains unchanged.
semantic.label: Subject transformation record and operation

semantic.definition: A signature-supplied model coordinate, not a ninth record family: Resolution_M(x) = {external_identity, reference_domain, external_target_kind, resolved_target_identity, basis_relation, resolution_basis, evidence_identity}. Every field is exact and identity-bearing; ResolutionSet_M contains one such tuple for each External_M identity. ExternalResolutionPreservationWitness contains external_resolution, domain_model, codomain_model, domain_resolution, codomain_resolution, decision equal and evidence.
semantic.label: External resolution coordinate and preservation witness

semantic.definition: FOUNDATIONS Judgment carried as a model record pointing to an unchanged subject, with id, kind, subject, subject_digest, context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance and decided_at.
semantic.label: Subject Judgment record

semantic.definition: This member's traversal is a typed contract with id, domain, codomain, context, owner, scope, basis, preconditions, postconditions, authority, evidence, provenance and stop_states.
semantic.label: Traversal contract

semantic.definition: F_D, urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d, classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared properties. It returns a judgment without performing the domain construction judged.
semantic.label: F_D

semantic.definition: F_P, urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p, classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or proposal under an exact traversal contract. Usefulness or repeatability confers no semantic, admission, acceptance or closure authority on its result.
semantic.label: F_P

semantic.definition: F_H, urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h, classifies explicit human adjudication under exact identity, authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence grants no ambient authority.
semantic.label: F_H

semantic.definition: F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v denotes one functor kind applied under one exact traversal identity to its typed input domain, yielding its typed result domain or a value of its closed stop algebra. Omega_v refines the core result algebra without adding a core value.
semantic.label: Functor application and stop domain

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/5. Traversals and functor kinds/AC-016 Typed composition

semantic.definition: Typed composition orders a first traversal v and a second traversal w, written F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v], while retaining their separate contracts and results.
semantic.label: Typed composition

semantic.definition: Interpret_a_c(subject_basis, signature, interpretation_contract) applies a_c to one exact subject and yields a proposed M_subject* or hold, gap or refusal. The star denotes absence of the applicable semantic acceptance judgment; stops take their cause-dependent core values under AC-007.
semantic.label: Exact subject interpretation

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/6. Interpretation and models/AC-018 Structural and semantic separation

semantic.definition: Structural conformance covers closed syntax, types, identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates. Semantic fidelity covers interpretation meaning and materiality. Semantic acceptance is a separately recorded authority judgment.
semantic.label: Structural, semantic and acceptance assessments

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/6. Interpretation and models/AC-019 Valid model

semantic.definition: M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma] names a valid-model claim under an exact signature and calculus basis, subject to AC-019's necessary conditions.
semantic.label: Valid model claim

semantic.definition: a_c is the pure calculus layer.
semantic.label: a_c

semantic.definition: a_c.X is subject X interpreted as a model of a_c. Acceptance is external to its unchanged content identity; an accepted interpretation is the pair (a_c.X, J_X).
semantic.label: a_c.X

semantic.definition: a_c.X.C is the accepted model encoded in carrier C. G_C denotes encoded bytes; J_X is external semantic acceptance over unchanged M_X; D_C is deterministic carrier admission under v_carrier_admission using G_C, Profile_C and CarrierBasis_C, over unchanged carrier bytes. The admitted encoding evidence is the exact triple (G_C, J_X, D_C).
semantic.label: a_c.X.C and encoding evidence

semantic.definition: AxiomaticCalculusBasis is an external, post-publication record distinguishing the stable calculus concept from an immutable edition. It binds governing premise clauses through derivation_basis and the published member through publication_basis within one exact immutable package.
semantic.label: AxiomaticCalculusBasis

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/9. Application boundary, imports and exclusions/External imports and specialisations

semantic.definition: An application binding is an external typed import, translation or specialisation of an a_c concept declared under the application's own exact authority, context, basis, scope, preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation law.
semantic.label: External application binding

grounds.heading: AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/9. Application boundary, imports and exclusions/Constraint surfaces

semantic.definition: A constraint surface is a derived task view specifying a declared subject and work boundary's objects and meanings, predicates and dependencies, admissible operations, required results, authority, evidence, permitted freedom and unresolved conditions. It bounds work without prescribing internal strategy beyond those obligations and supports recovery of task constraints within finite attention.
semantic.label: Constraint surface

semantic.definition: Calculus review and qualification evaluate explicitly bounded claims about the member, including its signature, laws, identities, references, conservation properties and absence of hidden application dependencies.
semantic.label: Calculus qualification

semantic.definition: CONFORMANCE is a Tier 2 catalogue importing method rules for shared owners and consumers without defining a competing result algebra. A discriminator is a situation whose expected distinction separates a conforming application from a defective one. A case names subject, mechanism and expected distinction; a separate execution record binds exact tested subject, basis, acquired context, observations, assessor and result.
semantic.label: Conformance catalogue and cases

semantic.definition: The named core values are satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis. CONFORMANCE imports them from FOUNDATIONS. Its re_enter, re_entry_requested(authority), not_effected and completion_unknown are ACTIVATION-defined refinements mapped into that core. Non-performance has no result.
semantic.label: Imported conformance result domains

semantic.definition: Counterexample cases C-01 through C-12 identify failure mechanisms and local rules expected to distinguish them; they are assessment designs rather than reports of observed failures or passes.
semantic.label: Counterexample cases

semantic.definition: Construction trials T-01 through T-08 test bounded construction, ambiguity, composition, failure conservation, recovery, requirement change, defective acceptance and broader sourced decision work.
semantic.label: Construction trials

semantic.definition: R-01 and R-02 test fresh-context recovery of governing relations from the corpus, including matched comparisons when claimed and operation without validator folklore, author memory or whole-corpus loading.
semantic.label: Recoverability cases

semantic.definition: CD construction-discriminator cases exercise configurations, executor bindings and workspace recovery through actual use. AR assurance-relation cases exercise weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error and change selection.
semantic.label: Construction-discriminator and assurance-relation cases

semantic.definition: Discriminator coverage associates each situation and expected distinction with local owning sections and checks. L-n denotes a qualified reviewer's reasoned textual review without execution; actual-use cases add observed evidence. J53–J59 concern integrated assessment across members and their material composition.
semantic.label: Logical and integrated discriminator coverage

grounds.heading: CONFORMANCE/5. Discriminator coverage/Universal-construction and assurance discriminators

semantic.definition: UC-1–UC-9 are construction cases and AS-1–AS-12 are assurance cases with stated expected distinctions. Each receives local-owner logical review and applicable actual-use evidence where required by the claim. These cases remain assessment design.
semantic.label: Universal-construction and assurance discriminators

conditions: Applies within boundaries governed by this optional profile.
semantic.definition: DESIGN_MODULE is a Tier 3 optional realisation-design profile covering ontology-first derivation, proportional sequencing and decision completeness, bounded frames, native constructability, capability and foundation selection, entity/authority/admission/function completeness, Prime atoms and contraction, IACS, three-view design, reconstruction, computational realisation, module taxonomy, realisation rules, review, adoption and bound-runtime identity defaults.
semantic.label: DESIGN_MODULE

conditions: These terms have profile-local ownership.
semantic.definition: The profile names Ontology as the engineering Ontology of one designed boundary; Prime; Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS); Subordinate Payload; Promotion Test; Boundary Inflation; carrier; three-view design asset; module; and decision_complete(B) and co_evolution_admissible(B). Their detailed definitions are referred to §§5–9.
semantic.label: Profile-owned design terms

semantic.definition: Tier-2 ASSURANCE supplies the design-to-module evidence route, module-derived unit tests and module lifecycle confirmation (§§14–16), and names generic carrier inventory, accepted ontology/design, domain/sequence/state projections and decision-completeness/co-evolution conditions that this profile binds for its own boundaries.
semantic.label: Imported ASSURANCE design roles

semantic.definition: Profile evaluation results, Ontology/design dispositions and author-declared design-record entries are distinct categories. Reconstruction decisions and axiom verdicts are the profile's two result refinements. Other closed design vocabularies are records without core-result mappings; their evaluations return their own core values.
semantic.label: Design results, dispositions and record entries

conditions: Once the project has decided its outcomes and capabilities.
semantic.definition: The profile concerns realisation design and implementation shape. Its goals are reduced ambiguity, entropy, avoidable debt, hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift; increased refactorability; and preserved evidence for audit and reconstruction. Bounded intermediate traversal gives finite inspectable units for reasoning, implementation, evaluation, proof and refactor; a module boundary is one such tool.
semantic.label: Bounded realisation design

conditions: Within the profile's governed boundaries.
semantic.definition: Functional design discipline is required, with a preferred functionally biased realisation: explicit typed carriers and transforms hold meaning, imperative coordination is subordinate to admitted truth, effects are isolated at explicit boundary modules, and mutable shared state is minimised and justified. A functional programming language is not required.
semantic.label: Functional design discipline

conditions: Scoped to boundaries governed by DESIGN_MODULE.
semantic.definition: The core realisation-shape rule is owned once by SPEC_METHOD §2. Its stated test is that a design is too imperative and coupled when a reader must inspect orchestration to learn the system's meaning. The profile's subsequent rules refine it.
semantic.label: Imported realisation core rule

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/1. Purpose and position/Foundation to law

conditions: A project adopts the profile for a named realisation boundary.
semantic.definition: DESIGN_MODULE is optional material family F17, software design. Actors enter it when designing, implementing or reviewing a governed boundary. It governs realisation of decided Product outcomes, not the constitutional decision about those outcomes. Its foundation-to-law table distinguishes derived consequences from domain and policy choices and their owners.
semantic.label: Software design profile, F17

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/1. Purpose and position/Foundation to law

semantic.definition: The table's cited commitments have distinct standing: P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with P0's non-reacquirable step-fact premise; P5 derived from P0 and P6 with P0's open-world premise. Imported families are F1 frames/context, F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work state/resumption/reuse, F6 claims/evidence/assessment/acceptance, F8 identity, F10 constitutional chain/outcome/build-tenant binding, F12 project adoption, F13 work carriers, and F18 graph-native construction. Adopted instance premises are I1 decided outcomes/capabilities and named-boundary adoption; I2 alternative and possibly multiple code locations for one meaning; I3 bounded actors whose later actions generally lack original design reasoning; I4 local or existing-foundation mechanisms and recurrence across boundaries and time.
semantic.label: Commitments, imports and instance premises

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/1. Purpose and position/Foundation to law

semantic.definition: Named rule and consumer loci in FOUNDATIONS, PROFILES, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, IDENTITY, SPEC_METHOD, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, TICKETS, ODD, ASSURANCE, UX, WORLD_MODEL, CONFORMANCE and EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, together with later DESIGN_MODULE clauses. These are references with the roles explicitly stated in the supplied text; their absent bodies are not reconstructed.
semantic.label: Referenced owning and consuming rule loci

conditions: The Product is governed by the graph-execution profile.
semantic.definition: For Product movement between typed asset states, the governing structure is outcome traversal, then declarative graph carriers (GTL and ABG), then deterministic module realisation. A module is a realisation cut inside this graph program, not the program itself.
semantic.label: Graph-execution and module alignment

conditions: The profile governs the boundary.
semantic.definition: Three overriding boundary-closure evaluators are authority seam closure, essential carrier consolidation and enforcement after proof. Ingress collapse specifies the accompanying foreign-input boundary discipline.
semantic.label: Boundary closure evaluators

semantic.definition: The functional-bias and typing rule family combines language-independent carrier, composition and effect preferences with a Python-specific full-typing and strict-checking requirement.
semantic.label: Functional bias and typing

conditions: The boundary is governed by this profile.
semantic.definition: An Ontology is the boundary's prior semantic-design authority: entities, identities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle, authority, atomic functions, higher-order composition, effects and projections. It derives from constitutional intent, Product, requirements and applicable graph/domain profile. Accepted design supplies structural HOW: topology, interfaces, carrier placement, module boundaries, algorithms and local realisation. Implementation and tests derive through requirements and accepted design while preserving the Ontology.
semantic.label: Accepted Ontology and design layers

semantic.definition: A material semantic boundary is one whose change affects identity, authority, lifecycle, public contract, externally observable Product meaning, cross-module topology, or accepted effect or closure law.
semantic.label: Material semantic boundary

conditions: B is one governed boundary.
semantic.definition: M(B) is the complete material-relation network: entities; identities; relationships; cardinalities; invariants; authorities; authority transitions; functions; higher-order composition laws; topology; lifecycle states and transitions; public contracts; externally observable Product meaning; declared domains and admission conditions; failure and refusal routes; effect and closure laws; projections; module mappings; material algorithmic obligations. U(B) is its unresolved subset. Decision completeness requires empty U(B), joint satisfiability, and semantic equivalence of every admitted network under governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations. Co-evolution admissibility is exactly decision completeness. The design gate is the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish it.
semantic.label: Decision-complete material-relation network

semantic.definition: A material design frame records governing frames and accepted relations, bounded affected relations, inherited invariants, crossing authority/composition seams and subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions. Global and local are relative to the selected frame. Governing frames form a constraint network and may be multiple rather than a mandatory hierarchy.
semantic.label: Bounded design frame

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Capability and foundation selection (UP-023)

semantic.definition: Native constructability concerns whether the chosen substrate can construct required identities, relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle, composition, publication and retirement. Foundation selection separately compares bounded candidate compositions for material generic capabilities, common mechanics, algorithms and dependencies.
semantic.label: Constructability and foundation selection

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Entity and lifecycle completeness

semantic.definition: Entity-lifecycle evidence enumerates active entities, identities, relationships, cardinalities, invariants, lifecycle states and authority owners. Its matrix has Entity, Identity, Authority owner, Declare/create, Read/project, Update/transition and Delete/retire columns. These are completeness questions, not a mutable-CRUD mandate. Domain-entity lifecycle is distinct from ASSURANCE §16's operational build, release, deployment, observation and retirement lifecycle.
semantic.label: Entity and lifecycle completeness evidence

semantic.definition: Authority is part of the Ontology. The authority matrix distinguishes proposer, evaluator, verifier, admitter, executor, projector and retirement owner for each relevant function/transition. Actor identity, capability on a basis, attribution, permission, domain-meaning ownership and runtime-effect ownership are distinct.
semantic.label: Ontology authority model

conditions: A consequential entity-transition domain is present.
semantic.definition: The singular transformation-admission relation decides which candidate becomes durable entity truth. It spans entity identity, predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision cardinality, admission predicate, durable result and supersession law. Singularity belongs to the complete decision relation, not a single actor, callable or component. The evidence table records Entity transition domain, Predecessor basis, Candidate family, Admission relation, Durable result and Competing-path disposition.
semantic.label: Complete transformation-admission relation

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Atomic functions and higher-order composition

semantic.definition: Atomic function families are the smallest parameterised families completing entity lifecycles. Function derivation records Discovered functionality, Entity, Atomic function or template, Higher-order composition, Effect class, Required authority and Disposition. Higher-order behaviour uses an explicit composition/effect algebra; illustrative categories are unit/lift, sequential, parallel/applicative, fold/evaluation, retry/recovery, recursion/fixed point and projection.
semantic.label: Atomic functions and higher-order composition

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Prime semantic atoms and admitted domain

semantic.definition: A Prime semantic atom is an irreducible design relation—atomic function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure or composition law—that cannot honestly be expressed by composing accepted atoms while preserving meaning. Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude. Smallness, typing, naming, separate testing or a file/class/module boundary do not establish it. Whole-family contraction examines every candidate atom kind and every proposed realisation projection.
semantic.label: Prime semantic atom and family

semantic.definition: Ontology projections include domain/class, sequence, state/lifecycle diagrams; authority/effect matrices; IACS; APIs, operation registers, SDK/CLI surfaces; schemas, codecs, manifests, catalogues; target architecture/module design; implementation through accepted target design; and tests/proofs through requirements and accepted design. They preserve one semantic truth and are not independent semantic authorities.
semantic.label: Ontology and realisation projections

semantic.definition: IACS is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family needed for a boundary's functionality and authority flow. Subordinate Payload is internal payload detail, not top-level by default. Promotion Test is the explicit prerequisite for elevating it to a top-level type. Boundary Inflation is promotion into peer types without irreducible need. Example carrier roles are source truth, admission, execution, yielded/recovery, effect plan and public projection.
semantic.label: IACS, subordinate payloads, promotion and inflation

conditions: Realisation derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.
semantic.definition: Reference-derived module design carries the derivation chain constitutional WHAT → reference design → target Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping → target design mapping → target module boundary assets → implementation. Code comparison alone does not establish design-method completion.
semantic.label: Reference-to-target derivation

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate

semantic.definition: The design-gate asset combines one accepted Ontology with three distinct fidelity-checked views: classDiagram domain, sequenceDiagram execution and stateDiagram-v2 lifecycle. Together they provide the sign-off surface for identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle and axiom conformance.
semantic.label: Ontology and three-view design asset

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Invariant reconstruction sufficiency (UP-018)

conditions: An accepted material-frame basis and a proposed bounded action are declared.
semantic.definition: Invariant reconstruction is the sufficiency of selected method basis plus accepted design to recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected set and classify the action against each as preserves, changes, duplicates or violates. Method supplies required relations and reasoning law; accepted design supplies concrete invariant values. These inputs do not substitute for one another.
semantic.label: Invariant reconstruction sufficiency

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Domain model

semantic.definition: The domain model is the structural Ontology projection. It uses stereotypes <<prime-conformant>>, <<subordinate>>, <<effect-edge>>, <<deferred>>, <<authoritative>>, <<downstream>>; '+' means public/exported and '-' module-local/private. Standard relationships use composition for owned subordinate payloads, association for downstream consumption and inheritance only for actual variant/outcome families.
semantic.label: Domain model

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Sequence model

semantic.definition: The sequence model projects Ontology functions and authority onto supported execution from admitted input to a result or truthful stop.
semantic.label: Sequence model

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/State model

semantic.definition: The state model projects Ontology entity lifecycle, including every admitted refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal state the active boundary can produce.
semantic.label: State model

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Cross-view axiom evaluation

semantic.definition: Cross-view axiom evaluation records Axiom, Ontology evidence, Authority, Domain evidence, Sequence evidence, State evidence, Native enforcement, Admission/compiler enforcement, Verdict and Gap owner. The refined verdicts pass, fail and not_applicable map to core values for the exact-basis disjunction 'the design meets the axiom, or the axiom does not apply'; unresolved evaluation and absence of evaluation remain separate.
semantic.label: Cross-view assessment and axiom result domain

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Gate and retrospective work

semantic.definition: Ontology and design verdicts are separate owner acceptance decisions consuming availability and assessment results at the design gate. The decision owner is the design authority accepting the Ontology. 'accepted' is the ACTIVATION disposition 'accept', mapped to satisfied for 'the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary'. Other dispositions or no disposition are not acceptance; no disposition means no acceptance result.
semantic.label: Design-gate acceptance and retrospective work

semantic.definition: An operational engineering profile for preferred realisation structure and design discipline. Its engineering Ontology concerns one designed boundary; using the profile does not require adopting a world-model, Constraint-Emergence Ontology, or metaphysical or empirical programme.
semantic.label: Design-module profile

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Computational realisation projection (UP-019)

semantic.definition: The three domain views show domain structure, execution and lifecycle. A computational realisation projection additionally exposes abstract data types, identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings, including repeated machinery obscured by domain names.
semantic.label: Computational realisation projection

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Computational realisation projection (UP-019)

semantic.definition: The explicit semantic and operational roles declared for a material realisation component. The declared role set is design authority; technological capability creates no authority.
semantic.label: Component role set

semantic.definition: Optional theoretical framing in which a Markov object is a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern with an effective blanket separating identity-bearing from contextual structure. IACS analogises the smallest such cut; the Promotion Test asks whether a payload has independent boundary authority; Boundary Inflation mistakes fragments for peer objects; semantic-boundary strong typing keeps the cut explicit.
semantic.label: Markov-object theoretical framing

conditions: The profile governs the realisation boundary.
semantic.definition: Recommended module roles: carrier modules define typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells perform emission, publication, network, subprocess, persistence or delivery effects; projections derive read models or reports from authoritative truth; bindings/adapters translate external boundaries to internal carriers without inventing law; constructors/materialisers write generated or built artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. Module boundaries constrain traversal reasoning under finite context, attention and time, expose ownership, consumption, emissions and sufficient proof, and make recurrence visible for library consolidation.
semantic.label: Module role taxonomy

semantic.definition: Typed values carrying source truth, preferably produced by a constructor or parser, consumed by transforms that return another carrier or closed result, and read by projections without mutation.
semantic.label: Typed truth carrier

semantic.definition: A Product semantic function may encounter input outside its admitted domain. Its returned outcomes are Product domain values, distinct from the method's core results; an evaluation consuming those outcomes returns its own core result.
semantic.label: Semantic function and Product outcomes

semantic.definition: An explicit boundary for effects such as file writes, network calls, subprocess execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation.
semantic.label: Effect edge

semantic.definition: A hidden semantic centre is an orchestration or wrapper surface that procedurally holds meaning which should already reside in carriers, contracts or explicit design modules. Its diagnostic is needing to read that module to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth.
semantic.label: Hidden semantic centre

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Governance and strategy separation

semantic.definition: A boundary governing, observing, routing, auditing or evaluating another actor, executor, builder or substrate. Governance surfaces describe facts, state, boundary and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should work.
semantic.label: Governance and strategy surfaces

conditions: A realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation work.
semantic.definition: Opportunistic optimisation is local improvement subordinate to constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Cross-boundary improvements are repricing inputs rather than silently enlarged clean-up.
semantic.label: Opportunistic optimisation

semantic.definition: Review of repeated realisation machinery as a commonisation candidate. Typical candidates are authority-neutral, not Product truth, reused across two or more tickets or boundaries, and locally adaptable without changing semantic ownership: expectation derivation, nested contract or policy carriers, proof helpers, fixtures, effect plans and constructors that own no semantic law.
semantic.label: Recurrence extraction and commonisation

conditions: A ticket applies the profile to a boundary and claims that boundary has been processed.
semantic.definition: A bounded design check against the accepted design basis and exact closure claim. Its complete selected function is the claim's causal closure, not the whole Product or construction history; it reconstructs governing requirements through Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, target modules, implementation and module-owned proof.
semantic.label: Post-ticket bounded design check

semantic.definition: An interface family has one authoritative source truth consumed downstream. Interface bleed includes reconstructing another family's truth, projection becoming closure, reports/prompts becoming admission, wrappers deciding kernel semantics, or adapters inventing meaning.
semantic.label: Interface family and semantic bleed

semantic.definition: A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that forwards to old authority, reconstructs missing truth from it, keeps it executable under a new name, or leaves proofs green while old law governs. Such substitution is bridge debt, distinct from explicitly retained compatibility.
semantic.label: Proxy interface and retained compatibility

semantic.definition: Review under the design profile includes provenance-bearing prompts, design-review questions, and an explicit functional-realisation checklist when functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low coupling is claimed.
semantic.label: Design review and functional checklist

semantic.definition: Product authority's adoption of an available design profile for a named boundary and, for partial adoption, a named rule family. Inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available but does not adopt it or create another adopter.
semantic.label: Product adoption of the profile

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/12. Adoption and relations/Relationship to other members

semantic.definition: The source's allocation of member responsibilities: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and migration; RELEASE owns release cut, Product, install, qualification and version-line promotion evaluation; ODD owns graph-native constructive carrier law; DESIGN_MODULE owns preferred implementation/design module structure; UX adds rendering, state-transition, effect-membrane and AssetSurface-binding discipline for UX surfaces. ASSURANCE module lifecycle confirmation detects sufficient lifecycle signal for building and review, not release or rollout eligibility.
semantic.label: Responsibilities of related members

grounds.heading: DESIGN_MODULE/12. Adoption and relations/Identity defaults from a bound runtime realisation

conditions: A runtime realisation is consumer-bound to the ABG role under the graph-execution profile.
semantic.definition: A bound ABG runtime realisation may publish default identity generators, validators and normalisers for its own runtime surfaces and default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers.
semantic.label: Role-scoped runtime identity defaults

semantic.definition: A Tier 1 member owning justification and acceptance of claims, evidence, independent assessment, review results, acceptance, realisation conformance and the equivalence ladder, frame and method qualification, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention. It consumes FOUNDATIONS' core results and defines no result values itself.
semantic.label: EVALUATION member

semantic.definition: A load-bearing assertion over an exact subject, property and governing basis, with a declared witness relation, excluded nearest weaker property and falsifier. Construction claims about recursive or repeated work distinguish preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction.
semantic.label: Load-bearing claim

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/1. Claims/Foundation to law: claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance
EVALUATION/1. Claims/Foundation to law: claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance
EVALUATION/1. Claims/Foundation to law: claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance

conditions: Exact-subject claims are relied on for promotion, closure or release.
Evidence is finite and may observe a weaker subject, another subject or another basis.
A constructor may be probabilistic or otherwise fallible.
Each reliance boundary has a decision owner.
semantic.definition: F6 is the claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance family covering EVALUATION §§1–5. Its instance premises are conditions of governed work, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. Its table traces consequences, rule owners, added policy/domain choices and consumers. P1, P2, P3 and P6 are cited as independent; P0 is recovered with named candidate-output or non-reacquirable-fact premises; P5 is derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise, and P4b from P0 and P2 with the step-produced-fact premise.
semantic.label: Foundation-to-law family F6

semantic.definition: Three distinct bases: semantic basis comprises constitutional and accepted-design relations defining claim meaning; evidence basis comprises exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations; state projection is a current view derived from admitted semantic and evidence bases. Four distinct roles define law, supply observations, apply the declared evaluation relation and dispose by decision authority. Structural conformance concerns closed syntax, types, identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates; semantic fidelity concerns meaning and materiality.
semantic.label: Bases, roles and structural/semantic separation

semantic.definition: Assessment independent in authorship and evidence conditions. Constructor self-review remains construction output. Author identity is the party responsible for realised content; actor identity identifies whoever performs an operation and is not authority. Independence is not established by a fresh context or assumed across actor families.
semantic.label: Independent assessment

semantic.definition: A review returns one FOUNDATIONS core result per declared predicate actually evaluated, accompanied by exact subject and basis, consulted evidence, consequence-ranked findings with evidence and smallest bounded correction, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions. A planned but unperformed predicate has no result, unlike an evaluated undecided predicate or required coverage with no planned assessment.
semantic.label: Review result and absence of evaluation

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/4. Review results/Result and triage projection

conditions: A review returns findings with technical triage.
semantic.definition: Finding-level, evidence-bound assessment against the exact evaluated claim and basis. Severity is the assessor's consequence grade; priority, current promotion-boundary effect and disposition belong to the decision owner. Triage payload classes complete, indeterminate and not_applicable are neither core results nor dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states.
semantic.label: Technical triage projection

semantic.definition: Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject, bounded to its named instance and interval. Work-item closure is satisfaction of the item's stated closing condition; review is an input rather than closure.
semantic.label: Acceptance and work-item closure

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/5. Acceptance/When a finding blocks promotion

semantic.definition: A finding is a reported defect against the exact evaluated claim. Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act over that finding. EVALUATION §5 supplies the shared blocking conditions; profiles and work carriers add only domain triggers.
semantic.label: Finding-dependent promotion blocking

semantic.definition: A realisation conforms to specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Several realisations may conform; sufficiency does not require unique derivation or incumbent equality.
semantic.label: Realisation conformance

semantic.definition: Four listed, unordered, mutually non-implying claim kinds: conformance; semantic equivalence of realisations, meaning identical interpreted behaviour on a stated domain including behaviour outside Σ; computational equivalence, meaning the same function at equal cost for declared workloads on architecture H; and categorical equivalence of categories and maps. Semantic equivalence here is not cross-context concept equivalence. Preservation of identities and composition by a map is a further distinct claim.
semantic.label: Unordered equivalence ladder

semantic.definition: A layered specification is sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from every layer. The test is sufficiency, not unique derivation or determinism; reconstructability requires a correct route, not executing it on every use.
semantic.label: Layered sufficiency and reconstruction

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Return of a reconstruction

conditions: A task builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor.
semantic.definition: A reconstruction return separates semantic conservation, demonstrated reduction and mere relocation. Conservation preserves the meaning of a disposed predecessor claim, judged by reading both texts against the disposition. Reduction shows lower cost for the same deciding path on a declared measure through traces of both paths and declared tradeoffs. Relocation moves text between owners or carriers without changed meaning or a traced deciding-path change.
semantic.label: Three-part reconstruction return

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification

semantic.definition: F7 concerns whether realisations, frames and the method are fit for their claims. Its instance premises allow several realisations per specification, fallible constructors and reliance by other actors, and finite qualification cases within declared envelopes. These are work conditions, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. The cited actor-change premise permits reacquisition of declared sources, not private memory.
semantic.label: Conformance, equivalence and qualification

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification

semantic.definition: Conformance is satisfaction of a specification by interpreted realisation behaviour under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Semantic, computational and categorical equivalence are distinct claims; preservation of identities and composition by a map is a further claim.
semantic.label: Conformance and equivalence claims

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification
EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification

semantic.definition: Layered sufficiency concerns a competent finite actor's ability to derive a conformant next layer from each layer. A reconstruction return distinguishes semantic conservation, demonstrated reduction and mere relocation.
semantic.label: Layered sufficiency and reconstruction

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification
EVALUATION/6. Conformance of realisations/Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification

semantic.definition: A conformance case identifies its subject, mechanism, independently specified expected distinction and status. A bounded construction trial additionally declares actor context and total-work bounds.
semantic.label: Conformance cases and bounded trials

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/7. Qualification of frames and of the method

semantic.definition: Document section grouping qualification of frames and qualification of the method; the heading alone adds no test or verdict.
semantic.label: Qualification of frames and of the method

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/7. Qualification of frames and of the method/Frame qualification
EVALUATION/7. Qualification of frames and of the method/Frame qualification

semantic.definition: Qualification of a candidate frame in proportion to its claims. Capability includes separately evaluated fit and adequate attention: context fit compares measured selected-representation size with declared capacity; adequate attention concerns evidenced actual use on declared tasks and conditions.
semantic.label: Frame qualification, fit and adequate attention

grounds.heading: EVALUATION/7. Qualification of frames and of the method/Method self-qualification

semantic.definition: Method self-qualification uses the ordinary qualification process, the work boundary, construction/assessment relation and layered sufficiency. Its population is every claimed function and failure relation. It includes qualification of changed derived guidance and a recoverability benchmark using fresh actors and published documents.
semantic.label: Method self-qualification

semantic.definition: Optional tier-3 operational profile mapping Executive, Worker, Reviewer and specialist frames onto tiers 1 and 2. It owns its direct-entry additions, empirical revision boundary, frame mappings and allocation explanation, specialist catalogue, engagement procedure, Worker value readings and adoption/configuration/qualification/closure records. It imports, without redefining, FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, SPEC_METHOD, PRODUCT_DEFINITION and ASSURANCE.
semantic.label: EXECUTIVE_BASELINE

semantic.definition: Canonical engagement projection: existing authority, complete method basis including REFERENCE_FRAME, exact Product or Product-chain outcome/workspace and known evaluations/dependencies/residuals support sufficient direct Worker entry or material coordination. Coordination locks outcome/basis and finite readiness, obtains applicable Worker/specialist and required Reviewer evaluations, consumes closed results, applicable triage and declared conjunction, applies bounded decisions, records results and next lawful action, updates basis/coverage/residuals/frontier, and repeats or stops.
semantic.label: Canonical engagement projection
