semantic.label: FOUNDATIONS subject document

semantic.definition: Each foundational claim, whether commitment or hypothesis, has exactly one standing: recovered is an adopted premise consolidating named source rules without treating them as proof; independent is an adopted premise argued by a case where other commitments hold and it fails; derived is a consequence with named premises; hypothesis is unestablished by the method, not law, and held for falsification. This differs from result standing and successor disposition.
semantic.label: Foundational claim standing

semantic.definition: Four distinct uses of join: categorical join is a map between categories; composition boundary joins successive steps; join of results combines closed results under one decision rule; relation join is equality join of participants in an enclosing relation. Unqualified join in a result context means join of results.
semantic.label: Four context-dependent meanings of join

semantic.definition: Ontology categories: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, identified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for a subject. Interpretation is a declared context-bound representation-to-meaning contract identifying reliable distinctions and residuals. Context declares subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations. Outcome U is an owner-selected directly verifiable state with acceptance interval. Object O has scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, state and material relations. Actor performs a step within context, attention, time and capability limits; role is an occupied relation selected by configuration. Step is bounded intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. Step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded. Claim binds subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence comprises admitted exact observations/artifacts with provenance, subject identity, basis and scope. Judgment is recorded evaluation over unchanged subject, with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Authority is identity-bearing scoped permission to operate or dispose acceptance. Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation awaiting authorised disposition. Basis is every exact version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration or evidence coordinate whose change can alter the bound step, claim, result or evaluation. Materiality is evaluation-relative potential to change result, basis validity, admissible evidence, operation performer or decision owner, including uncertainty and closure.
semantic.label: Foundational ontology objects

semantic.definition: Frame objects: Evaluation is a declared question with known result family, evidence basis, decision authority and material-operation authority where needed, admitting judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. Evaluation family shares required manifold, authority basis and result algebra. Workspace is bounded reasoned-over or acted-on material, potentially broader than a repository. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions needed by a family, allowing overlapping coordinate charts without implied geometry or runtime. Coordinate is complete locally required basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority information. Topology is the material relation structure visible at one basis, not necessarily complete workspace topology. Capability envelope is required competence, context capacity, tools, access, independence and configuration. Reference frame specifies finite attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for a family and basis. Activated frame binds declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary. Frame set is a human-declared available family permitting overlaps, alternatives, specialists, exploration and separate assurance. Active frame configuration is activations and declared result relations for one evaluation or decision. Lens is a reusable question family, becoming a frame only on full bounded instantiation. Role allocates responsibility/authority; persona changes approach/salience; abstraction hides/contracts detail; component is structural. None is a frame merely by identity.
semantic.label: Reference-frame ontology

semantic.definition: Distinct kinds: frame-set authority is human declaration/acceptance of a project frame set; semantic authority owns meaning of a material relation; evaluation authority permits evaluation; operation authority is an owner-issued grant to construct, transform, admit, publish or mutate a material subject; decision authority permits accepting, rejecting or otherwise disposing results. Actor identity identifies the human, agent, tool or process and is not authority. These may lawfully coincide but never collapse by default.
semantic.label: Authority kinds and actor identity

semantic.definition: Frame disjointness is structural absence of shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for declared evaluations. Evaluation independence is procedural separation of activations that neither consume nor influence one another's unclosed working results; they may share subject or manifold and later contribute closed results to one conjunction. Assurance independence is claim-relative separation prescribed by assurance law, including non-authorship, acquisition, exposure, actor and configuration conditions. Disjointness does not imply independent evaluation, independent activation does not imply disjointness, and the unqualified word independent establishes none of the three.
semantic.label: Disjointness, evaluation independence and assurance independence

semantic.definition: Reference frame F = ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩: evaluation family; workspace/topology basis; manifold; coordinate/equality law; invariants; authority; evidence/provenance law; exclusions/prohibited assumptions; closed core result algebra or mapped refinement; invalidation/rechart condition; capability envelope; optional declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs and outputs. This relation is an evaluation contract, not a required schema/runtime carrier. Prompt, context packet, symbolic program or other representation projects an activated frame rather than being the frame.
semantic.label: Frame tuple

semantic.definition: Distinct identities in FOUNDATIONS-owned urn:stdo:bounded-context:recursive-product-taxonomy, with corresponding urn:stdo:concept:recursive-product-taxonomy:<name> identities: substrate is a lower product/runtime used to build products; development-product is the role of one exact released-product install acting as builder for a source project, creating no new Product identity or authority transfer; source-project is mutable workspace building the next release cut; release-cut is immutable annotated candidate boundary over a published feature set; product is the immutable released thing after cut acceptance; install is a stamped workspace instance; artifact is published output built by a source project or configured install; product-definition is present-tense source-project WHAT authority, conventionally PRODUCT.md, not released artifact. Separate release neighbours are candidate source, a mutable successor-building state non-operative for released consumers; release subject, the exact member set/artifact bound by cut-scoped claims; and version-line selector, a mutable alias for the highest-ordinal published cut on one project's version line, useful for discovery but insufficient as exact immutable basis.
semantic.label: Recursive product taxonomy and release neighbours

semantic.definition: Boundary object around a probabilistic, agentic or delegated work unit. Live specification and design should declare six parts: input/output contract; required context; capability/role expectation; admissible evidence/evaluator regime; provenance obligation; lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion states. ACTIVATION §1 makes this unit's intake, context and result algebra exact.
semantic.label: Declared work boundary

semantic.definition: Construction realises a selected outer contract through steps. Three independently variable accounts remain distinct: algorithmic description of steps; informational interpretation of data under an Interpretation contract; computational realisation by people, machines or mixtures in a declared execution environment, with build-tenant environment owned by SPEC_METHOD §11. A construction may need all three; none is a corpus tier. This distinction is an added choice, not a commitment, and has none of the foundational claim standings.
semantic.label: Three accounts of construction

semantic.definition: Reference-only import carries identical owner-qualified meaning from named source to importing context, with no loss, translation, ownership transfer or authority. It takes either a collected declaration or a point-of-use reference naming the owning section. Adoption is the target's use of an imported concept under source-owned adoption premises; lifecycle remains source-owned.
semantic.label: Import and adoption between members

semantic.definition: P0 Bounded construction is recovered: finite actors realise selected outer contracts through fitting steps, owning their internal path; actors may change and reacquire declared sources but not private memory, step-produced facts are not reacquirable, the world is open and output is candidate until evaluated. P1 Interpretation is independent: subject, representation and context-bound meaning differ; structural success is not fidelity and semantic decisions require exact contracts. P2 Purpose is independent: selected outcome defines adequacy and interface obligations derive from the served transformation. P3 Identity is independent: declared authority/kind/value identity survives admissible change and boundaries carry proof obligations. P4a Typed composition is independent: prior type and judgment must satisfy the next exact domain and preconditions, retaining identities, intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. P4b Conservation is derived from P0 and P2 plus non-reacquirability: producing steps record outer-contract-needed judgments, residuals, observations and authority decisions; reacquirable sources follow sufficiency rather than conservation. P5 Totality is derived from P0 and P6 plus open-world premise: no success on outside-context conditions, first-class non-success and named next moves. P6 Justification and authority is independent: definitions, assumptions, observations, candidate judgments and accepted claims have distinct standing; evidence supports basis-bound claims and authority permits or disposes only within scope.
semantic.label: P0–P6 commitments

semantic.definition: Derived consequence synthesising commitments for movement from observed current state to acceptable destination under finite resources; not a further commitment. P0 bounds acquisition/work and preserves internal strategy; P1 preserves comparison meaning among conditions, observations and predictions; P2 selects destination Z and adequacy criteria; P3 separates persistent subject, observations and dependencies from accounts; P4a carries obligations through steps/refinement/boundaries; P4b conserves non-reacquirable facts through observation/correction/reuse; P5 accounts for resource tradeoffs, recursion, recovery and truthful undecided stops; P6 establishes support and authority without minting either. ACTIVATION §1 owns the construction relation.
semantic.label: Construction synthesis

semantic.definition: A material family groups deciding rules whose outcomes matter to the selected method outcome. Its owner-located entry table traces labelled instance premises and one row per consequence using five columns: premises with standing; consequence; linked owning rule; only additional domain/policy choice with owner or none; pillar contributions. Ten numbered contributions are specification/project structure; world models/identity/Markov objects; algebraic calculus; functional design; outcome-driven development; information/interpretation; reference frames; computational calculus/execution binding; evidence/correction/authority; axiomatic calculus. Tables, consumer paragraphs and family index are traces, not owners, added determinations, new authority or proofs of entire rules.
semantic.label: Foundation-to-law family traces and index

semantic.definition: Subject-defined algebra of typed step composition, conservation accounting, sufficient references, explicit latitude, shared implementation without identity/authority merger, and conditional demonstration requirements for categorical claims. These are descriptions of the supplied subject's calculus and create no operation in this interpretation.
semantic.label: Subject algebra and formal fragment

semantic.definition: H1 proposes 𝒜 as the free category on typed primitives, ℐ as selected carrier sets with total functions, and 𝒞_H as function pairs with additive costs; S: 𝒜 → ℐ and R_H: 𝒜 → 𝒞_H would be functors, with S neither faithful nor an equivalence. H names architecture, never runtime. The source explicitly leaves the whole claim unsupported and unresolved.
semantic.label: H1 categorical-structure hypothesis

semantic.definition: The single core result domain for every performed evaluation, directly or through refinement: satisfied means the declared predicate holds on the exact basis; falsified means a declared counterexample defeats it; indeterminate means available admissible evidence cannot decide it; out_of_frame means a required material relation or capability is undeclared; invalid_basis means the subject or basis cannot support evaluation. Constraints, judgments, frame evaluations, stops, work steps and effects use this core or a refinement mapped into it.
semantic.label: Core result algebra

semantic.definition: A finer outcome vocabulary defined by a member, profile or adopting Product for a named question and mapping predicate. Each refined value has exactly one core value; cause-dependent alternatives are separate refined values. Further refinement by a member, profile, project or adopting Product splits parent values by named causes while retaining each parent's core value.
semantic.label: Result refinement and parent-value rule

conditions: An evaluation was required or planned but was not performed.
semantic.definition: Absence of a closed evaluation result, distinct from every core value, undecidable evidence, a step's stop state and unresolved work. In conjunction it is a planned-assessment gap when assessment was planned; required coverage with no planned assessment is uncovered coverage.
semantic.label: Evaluation not performed

semantic.definition: Three separate results with separate predicates: availability establishes that a step produced a candidate; assessment addresses whether the candidate meets declared criteria; acceptance addresses whether the decision owner accepts it at its boundary. Candidate production and successful work do not establish fitness or acceptance.
semantic.label: Availability, assessment and acceptance

semantic.definition: The source's family F3 trace register connects result and combination rules to commitments, added choices, owners and consumers. Its instance premises are declaration of predicate, subject and basis; combination of evaluations, steps or members into a decision; and a need for finer outcomes. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are treated as independent; P5 is derived from P0 and P6, and P4b from P0 and P2. The register attributes the core names and non-success division to Results; refined meanings to their definers; conjunction choices to its applying member/profile; acceptance to EVALUATION §5; step stops to ACTIVATION §3; transformation record fields to AC-013; composition-law need to the governing evaluation under RF-010; latitude to the contract owner; shared implementation to accepted design; categorical claims to their claimant.
semantic.label: Result rules, owners and consumer register

semantic.definition: Combination of component results into one result for a composite predicate, a decision over evaluations, or the outer contract of composed steps. Its three distinct inputs are returned closed results with predicates and domain outcomes; planned assessments lacking an applicable closed result; and required coverage R minus coverage C admitted by planned assessments. Missing applicable results include non-performance, absence, staleness, another subject or basis, or inability to establish the required claim.
semantic.label: Conjunction of results

semantic.definition: The rule for a particular conjunction declares mandatory results, conflict and indeterminacy handling, basis relations required to agree, a coherent composite basis for different bases, the owning decision authority, treatment of nonmandatory results, and any veto or deferral. It supplies the ordering or choice among non-satisfied returned values; no universal such order is supplied.
semantic.label: Declared conjunction rule

conditions: Applicable instance premises are a construction with intake-bound governing basis and material assumptions Γ; a declared case domain Ω including material inputs, behaviour and environment; and a checker with declared observations and an admitted evaluation relation.
semantic.definition: Shared source-owned preservation, assertion, provenance, quantified-assurance, reuse and formal-representation obligations connecting construction to supporting claims and evidence. The family table explains the six following owners and adds no separate decision. Its instance premises are conditions of governed situations, not commitments. ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, ASSURANCE, RELEASE, SPEC_METHOD and a_c interpretations apply these relations without declaring a second relation.
semantic.label: Assurance relations and family trace

semantic.definition: A construction binds starting state A, required outcome Z and Γ, its intake-bound governing basis plus material assumptions. Z includes required effects and trace properties where material. For boundary state or trace domains X_i, declared transitions F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1), and properties P_i, preservation states: for all x and x', P_i(x) and F_i(x,x') implies P_(i+1)(x'). This is a proof obligation, separate from real execution's conformance. Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts respectively state required operation, retained meaning/distinctions, and realisation of work/observations.
semantic.label: Construction preservation

semantic.definition: For a selected obligation r, Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω) is its required predicate over declared cases Ω. An assertion targets q_t and identifies whether it expresses the full obligation or a narrower claim. Conditional on Γ and Ω, Q_r implies q_t makes q_t necessary; q_t implies Q_r makes q_t sufficient; a stated conjunction q_1 and ... and q_n implying Q_r is sufficient collectively.
semantic.label: Obligation interpretation and assertion direction

semantic.definition: A checker has observation map π: Ω → O and admitted evaluation relation T ⊆ O × R, where R is the core result domain. Deterministic checking is a functional special case; human or probabilistic checking may admit different conclusions for identical observations. Universal soundness covers every admitted conclusion: for every s in Ω, (π(s), sat) in T implies q_t(s), and (π(s), fal) in T implies not q_t(s). sat and fal denote judgments about q_t, not execution states.
semantic.label: Observation and admitted checking relation

grounds.heading: FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Parallel derivation and mutual assurance

semantic.definition: Assertion provenance comprises the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies. Execution provenance comprises actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. Authentication binds a returned assessment to producer, subject, basis and evidence but establishes neither provenance. Construction and assurance may derive along different paths from a common obligation, such as requirement → refinement → realisation; these example roles prescribe no stage names or test classes.
semantic.label: Assertion provenance, execution provenance and authentication

grounds.heading: FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Parallel derivation and mutual assurance

semantic.definition: Comparison of independently justified constructions or assertions within declared scope. Agreement is compatible with correctness or shared error; disagreement calls for diagnosis and does not identify the faulty party. Material shared causes include specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations and copied material.
semantic.label: Mutual assurance

conditions: Quantified assurance is claimed.
semantic.definition: A model of a specified population or uncertainty with prior information, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. For violation V and evidence E, P(V | E, Γ) = P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)]. For check misses M_i under specified conditions, P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ) = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)). These are model-conditional claims, not truth values for the whole Product.
semantic.label: Quantified assurance

FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Change impact and evidence reuse

semantic.definition: Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation; evidence validity identifies dependencies affecting behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and governing assumptions. For a material change Δ, including discovery of an invalid assumption, I(Δ) conservatively covers changed facts and affected dependents; D*(t) covers transitive dependencies material to assertion, execution and evidence use. Candidate selection is S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }. For a new subject and basis, E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
semantic.label: Change impact and evidence reuse

semantic.definition: An a_c interpretation represents material assurance obligations and dependencies while distinguishing five support kinds: stated formula, discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked structure, externally assessed predicate and execution evidence. Mathematical proof, exhaustive finite-model checks, sampled tests and observed use retain distinct scopes; source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain separate evidence.

semantic.definition: Claims carried for falsification, expressly not law: categorical equivalence of 𝒜 and ℐ under some reformulation; universal algorithmic capture of meaning; the statistical Markov boundary with candidate status referenced to WORLD_MODEL §4; and traversal composition laws of any runtime.

A concept outside all bounded contexts declared by its member uses the member as source context; §16 indexes it without declaring a new context.
