semantic.label: Clause-owned senses of shared labels

semantic.definition: Tier 1 member owning identity law: scoped uniqueness, type, stability, readable/opaque forms, hierarchy, engine/domain split, authority conservation, default-format overrides and publication, parsing, object/release boundary, minimum questions, examples and implementation consequences. It consumes FOUNDATIONS §2 Object, Authority and Basis without redefining them. AC-002 applies scoped identity to every calculus identity with a coordinate map; calculus-edition identity remains owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §8 and release names/forms by RELEASE. Clauses name their requiring P0–P6 principles; identity is P3's commitment and authority P6's.
semantic.label: IDENTITY member

semantic.definition: Object identity is always scoped and typed, unique in its lawful scope and stable enough for its governed purpose. Its minimum semantic model is authority + kind + value, through which identity should be interpretable. It is not a universal naked-string convention.
semantic.label: Scoped object identity

semantic.definition: A useful identity hierarchy is authority / kind / value / revision. Examples distinguish product-authority requirement REQ-F-CAPABILITY-001, product-authority requirement_family REQ-F-CAPABILITY, runtime-authority run UUID and release-authority release 1.0.0-rc.1. Family/member and runtime/domain identities remain different semantic kinds even when serialised as strings.
semantic.label: Identity hierarchy

grounds.heading: IDENTITY/2. Core law/Boundaries and sufficiency claims

semantic.definition: An object's boundary states what belongs to it and what its identity does not depend on. It is an evidence- and basis-bounded claim with a proof obligation, not something established by storage, schema or name.
semantic.label: Object boundary claim

grounds.heading: IDENTITY/2. Core law/Boundaries and sufficiency claims

semantic.definition: Material sufficiency under RF-003 is a claim that observed boundary state suffices for a particular task. Statistical Markov boundary is the stronger hypothesis that the boundary screens the interior from everything outside it. Task sufficiency establishes neither completeness nor that stronger claim.
semantic.label: Task sufficiency and Markov hypothesis

semantic.definition: Identity for runtime-owned objects, including runs, function calls, jobs, execution frames, continuations and events. The substrate/runtime may provide defaults, opaque forms and engine-local generation rules.
semantic.label: Engine-owned identity

semantic.definition: Derived domains own semantic identity grammar for their constitutional objects, including requirements, requirement families, acceptance criteria, scenarios, ADRs/design decisions and published domain assets. The domain defines kinds, distinctions, uniqueness and parsing/reading.
semantic.label: Domain-owned identity

semantic.definition: Authority is an identity-bearing semantic relation preserving owner, kind, governed subject, scope and governing basis. It is not a display label, capability string, actor identity or reachable code path. FOUNDATIONS §2 owns Authority and its kinds.
semantic.label: Authority identity

conditions: Human authority acts through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy.
semantic.definition: A proxy grant names grantor, actor, subject, scope, permitted and excluded decisions, validity, delegation rights, revocation and provenance. Proxy actor identity remains distinct from human-authority identity.
semantic.label: Bounded proxy grant

grounds.heading: IDENTITY/7. Default formats and overrides/Derived domain overrides

semantic.definition: A derived domain's published replacement of format or structure defaults supplied by its bound runtime realisation for the domain's own kinds. Defaults are starter conventions and convenience contracts; the realisation's actual default surfaces belong to DESIGN_MODULE §12 realisation law.
semantic.label: Domain identity override

semantic.definition: An identity reader/parser operating under published identity law. Regex over prose is at most a provisional extractor over a surface with identity law defined elsewhere; it is not a complete identity model.
semantic.label: Identity parsing

semantic.definition: Distinct coordinates: object identity, release identity, publication/revision coordinates and mutable discovery selectors. An immutable release cut is the only exact operative release identifier; a mutable version-line selector names only the highest-ordinal published immutable cut on its line. Release version is a release-process fact, not the live constitutional identity of every project object.
semantic.label: Release and object identity coordinates

semantic.definition: A surface defining or exposing identity, whose adequacy is tested by seven questions about owning authority, denoted kind, uniqueness scope, lifecycle stability, over-trust in readability, unambiguous parsing of families/members/aliases/revisions, and runtime/domain/release category.
semantic.label: Identity surface

semantic.definition: F8 identity's authored foundation-to-law table distinguishes consequences from owned choices. Instance premises not supplied by commitments: (i) many object kinds with runtime/domain owners; (ii) serialised/readable forms read by people/parsers; (iii) release versions belong to releases, not every object. Premise/standing map: scoped/type/uniqueness P3 independent+i; stability P3 independent and P4b derived from P0/P2; boundaries P3/P6 independent, P5 derived from P0/P6 with P0 open-world premise+i; readability P3/P1 independent+ii; hierarchy P3+i,ii; authority split P3/P6+i; authority conservation P6/P3/P4b; defaults P3/P6; parsing P3/P1+ii; release boundary P3/P6+iii; minimum questions P3/P6; implementation policy P3/P1 independent and P0 recovered. Choice ownership remains with the stated owner: object owner for extra coordinates/kinds/form/visible segments; runtime for its generation/defaults; domain for semantic grammar, overrides and family need; WORLD_MODEL/RF-003 for their refinements; issuing authority for grants/decisions; IDENTITY for hierarchy model, grant fields, seven questions and enduring-repair policy; RELEASE for release forms. Examples add no decisions. Consumer applications add no authority beyond their owning rule.
semantic.label: F8 foundation-to-law derivation

semantic.definition: Tier 3 Outcome-Driven Development profile for graph-native product authoring over a declared asset graph. It owns graph-native terms in urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd under the selected complete STDO basis, imports listed families by reference and restates none. Its traversal and F_D/F_P/F_H shorthands are distinct from a_c traversal records and functor kinds. Executive, Worker and Reviewer are roles over steps; actor, executor, domain operation and functor kind are distinct coordinates. It owns structural traversal-governance and product-authoring law, not consuming-domain semantics or same-spelled runtime carriers.
semantic.label: Outcome-Driven Development profile

semantic.definition: GTL, Graph Transformation Language, is the capability role of a typed declarative graph language and the language expression of ODD. It does not require a particular repository, package, vendor or implementation.
semantic.label: GTL role

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is/ABG

semantic.definition: ABG is the singular traversal-governance and runtime-truth role. Its owned operations and facts include traversal, dispatch, actor invocation, process supervision, graph-call realisation, runtime facts, event emission/replay, frames, continuations, retry/correction control, closure folds, re-entry after publish boundaries, lineage and provenance. This describes source-defined authority, not an authority granted by this interpretation.
semantic.label: ABG role

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is
ODD/10. What an ODD product is/ODD product

semantic.definition: Configured GTL/ABG domain product whose published graph functions construct typed domain assets. Its ten-part application boundary comprises Bootstrap Surface, Initialization Surface, Domain Configuration, Typed Domain Assets/Nodes, GTL Function Catalog, GTL Module, Policy Hook Bindings, ABG Runtime, Projection/Query Surface and Proof Surface. The product owns domain asset and graph-function meaning, catalogue, policy overlays, domain projections and domain closure/gap interpretation.
semantic.label: ODD domain product

semantic.definition: Declared asset graph over state transitions relevant to the product's work; it is the product's process model and declared program space.
semantic.label: Declared asset graph

semantic.definition: Durable truth surface or product asset naming a bounded state of truth. Illustrative software-product names are intent, product, requirements, design, module_decomp, code, uat_testcases, integration_tests, bootloader and build targets; these names are product-local.
semantic.label: ODD node

semantic.definition: A lawful admissible transition between nodes. Its declaration gives required upstream assets, target asset, governing evaluators/gates and output contract; the probabilistic-work boundary additionally declares required context, role/capability expectation, provenance obligation and lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion states.
semantic.label: ODD vector

semantic.definition: Source-described workflow over the graph: bind current target, locate admissible vectors, traverse one vector, materialise next asset, prove that vector closed and continue until the selected target closes. One declared vector/edge traversal is the profile's bounded unit of probabilistic compute.
semantic.label: ODD graph traversal

semantic.definition: FOUNDATIONS P0's bounded step, referenced here as the source of ODD's binding: selected context fits the actor's envelope, internal path belongs to the actor, and traversal supplies admissible external space. Its full foundational definition is not supplied.
semantic.label: Referenced foundational bounded step

semantic.definition: urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p: bounded probabilistic worker turn preserving bounded non-human construction under declared policy and narrowing it to one graph traversal contract.
semantic.label: ODD F_P

semantic.definition: urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d: deterministic evaluation or proof over declared traversal properties. It may optimise or validate a domain-local path where the domain makes work precise, without moving domain HOW into GTL, ABG or the framework.
semantic.label: ODD F_D

semantic.definition: urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h: explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared authority and ambiguity policy. It grants no ambient traversal, semantic or closure authority.
semantic.label: ODD F_H

semantic.definition: Referenced source concept urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing, owned with its context by SPEC_METHOD §5. Only its preserved meaning of bounded non-human construction under declared policy is supplied here.
semantic.label: Referenced lawful probabilistic processing

semantic.definition: Referenced substrate-neutral source concept urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication, owned with its context by SPEC_METHOD §5; the complete source definition is not supplied.
semantic.label: Referenced human adjudication

semantic.definition: Named constructive program realising a vector: directly, through a small inner workflow refining one outer vector, or as a reusable higher-order library function. The outer vector remains its constitutional callable contract.
semantic.label: GraphFunction

semantic.definition: Referenced ACTIVATION §4 typed refinement allows earlier outputs to reach later steps only through a declared adapter or specialised contract whose declared domain names them. ODD binds it to a graph function refining one outer vector; the full general law is external.
semantic.label: Referenced typed refinement

semantic.definition: ODD §11.8's specialised cumulative carried environment, conserved as profile law rather than generalised into the core. A later function's declared domain is environment.requires and may require any typed binding available in the cumulative environment, not only the preceding output. Retained functions should declare environment.requires, environment.provides and environment.carries.
semantic.label: Cumulative carried environment

semantic.definition: The mutable source library authors a future method release; consumers select one complete immutable release distributed in the shared versioned STDO store. Both libraries contain method members, guides and templates. Only README-designated method members—tier 1, tier 2 and selected tier 3 profiles—are constitutional method surfaces. *_GUIDE.md documents refine application; *_TEMPLATE.md files are reusable starter forms/examples and convenience artifacts only.
semantic.label: Method library and document classes

semantic.definition: The installed graph-native product supplies the method, runtime and carrier surfaces, owning traversal-control substrate, runtime/control/command surfaces, release-managed methodology and scaffold templates. It is distinct from the target project and, in self-hosting, from the next version under development.
semantic.label: Installed ODD builder

semantic.definition: The project built with an installed ODD product owns its business domain; one stdo_<label>.json definition per distinct product WHAT locating constitutional, local/collective reference-frame basis, realisation, work and composition surfaces; constitutional surfaces; one or more how.build_tenants realisation roots; domain outputs and evidence. Software examples include design, code, tests, documents and proof surfaces; other domains name their own artifacts.
semantic.label: Target project

grounds.heading: ODD/8. Responsibility layers and local binding

semantic.definition: A structural responsibility layer expresses one capability class, which the product binds to local domain semantics and the GTL carrier exposes through lawful transitions. Examples are bootstrap/intake, design, implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and retrofit; they are not mandatory instance names.
semantic.label: Responsibility layer

semantic.definition: Source-defined evaluation of a move against the current ODD profile. For the predicate 'the move complies with the current profile', compliant maps to satisfied; non-compliant maps to falsified with the violated law as counterexample; valid and worth incorporating maps to out_of_frame because current law lacks what the move needs. Incorporation names the needed law, profile owner and update, and is neither compliance nor failure.
semantic.label: ODD method audit and outcome domain

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5 Current state is a projection over constructive history

semantic.definition: Downstream read models over admitted carrier, runtime, event or source truth; visible current state is projected constructive history. Possible views include assets, catalogue, checkpoint/provenance overlays and domain explainability.
semantic.label: ODD projection and query lane

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is/Product specification (software-development topology)

semantic.definition: Authoritative WHAT located by product-definition what bindings; specification/ is the default software-development location. It defines intent, product position, goals, requirements and scenarios.
semantic.label: Product specification

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is/Product realisation (software-development topology)

semantic.definition: Authoritative HOW located by product-definition how bindings; build_tenants/ is the default software-development location. It carries design, GTL publications, code, tests and local proof surfaces.
semantic.label: Product realisation

grounds.heading: ODD/10. What an ODD product is/Query and service layers

semantic.definition: Service/query layers may own transport, sessions, routing, browser-safe projection and APIs; they own neither runtime truth nor continuation truth.
semantic.label: Service and query layers

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.3 The function catalogue is published

semantic.definition: Machine-readable catalogue of retained graph functions on the live line; recommended minimum fields are name, inputs, outputs, intent and public/helper role.
semantic.label: Function catalogue

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.4 The GTL module is the operative publication surface

semantic.definition: Operative publication surface for public graph-function carriers, traversed graphs, typed node/vector surfaces and bound semantic jobs or equivalent outer callable contracts. Refined live inner boundaries have lawful GTL boundary surfaces such as RefinementBoundary or CandidateFamily.
semantic.label: GTL module

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5B Execution authority audit

semantic.definition: Audit of the unique execution authority for an affected ODD traversal, including traversal selection/advance; invocation/supervision; retry/correction/continuation/re-entry; runtime event emission/append/replay/projection; and closure fold/assurance gate. It examines authority-bearing implementation surfaces, not artifacts alone.
semantic.label: Execution-authority audit

conditions: A product is built with the ODD profile.
semantic.definition: F18's authored foundation-to-law table imports F1 frames/context, F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results, F4 work-state/resumption/reuse, F6 claims/evidence/assessment/acceptance, F9 a_c, F10 constitutional chain/outcome/build tenants, F11 change/ambiguity, F12 project binding, F13 work carriers and F15 release/successor conservation; rules and choices retain their owners. Adopted instance premises, not foundational deductions: I1 externally admitted selected Product outcome; I2 mutable workspace beside immutable ledger/event log; I3 bounded probabilistic workers whose reports/artifacts are observations; I4 installed method-product release, possibly an earlier self release. The 25 rows distinguish derived consequences from profile/product/consumer/other-member choices. Standing includes P0 recovered; P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2; P5 derived from P0/P6. Consumer applications decide nothing beyond rule owners. §1's opening, §16 failure patterns, §19 checklist and §20 compression add no independent law; §11 decides built correctness and §9 move compliance.
semantic.label: F18 foundation-to-law derivation

semantic.definition: Source-described constructive evaluation loop, referenced through §11.5D: separate authorities for synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action; immutable ledger/event log admitting observations; closure fold; replay; lawful yield; selected-outcome-bounded action selection. Closure decisions form a closed sum type with seven decisions and cause-dependent core mappings; evaluate_next is total. The supplied table names only some states and does not supply the full operational algebra.
semantic.label: Referenced constructive evaluation and yield loop

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

conditions: Applies to every ODD product over GTL/ABG.
semantic.definition: The profile's constructive homeostasis loop runs from intent lineage and model synthesis through observation to the next lawful action. Its operative functions are synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action. It corrects toward required conditions as observations arrive, without guaranteeing convergence or the adequacy of those conditions.
semantic.label: Constructive evaluation and yield loop

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop
ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.definition: Loop carrier vocabulary: IntentLineage is admitted source intent and lineage from a human, imported source, prior product, intent engine or prior synthesized construction intent, backed by ABG event-log truth. ProductAssetModel is desired and known typed asset truth synthesized from lineage, prior model and admitted product truth, with admitted-event and product-projection publication refs; it is neither runtime fact nor action authority. Worksite is the observable workspace, runtime archive, transform assets, product asset root, profile and file/process state. RuntimeEventLog is append-only admitted runtime facts; RuntimeProjection is replay-derived runtime state over event log and execution basis. ObservationSnapshot is a read-only runtime/worksite view; GapPressureRow represents missing, partial, blocked, waiting or ambiguous asset/evidence pressure. TargetObligationBinding binds pressure to the exact selected outcome, admitted prerequisite/experiment basis, assets, roles, evidence and admissible outcomes. ActionCatalog publishes lawful graph functions, vectors, targets, inputs and eligible outcomes. NextActionBasis is the dispatch sum initial_selection, post_yield_resume, post_close_graph_continuation, post_retry, post_repair, post_reenter, post_reprice or post_block, not a controller. PriorityProjection deterministically ranks bound lawful actions under visible policy. ConstructionIntent is an admitted selected action for one bounded invocation preserving outcome/basis refs. AdmittedEvidence includes worker, process, product, execution, materialization, liveness and postflight evidence, without worker self-closure. EdgeFulfillmentLedger carries evidence and convergence for one edge attempt/version. EdgeClosureDecision carries closure truth. NextActionProjection reads current truth and NextActionBasis and selects only when lawful.
exceptions: post_reprice carries a re-entry request and no action-selection authority.
semantic.label: Constructive loop carriers

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.definition: The selected Product outcome is external authority for the loop under SPEC_METHOD §3. An admitted bounded prerequisite or experiment can also supply a bounded work basis. Models, gaps, assurance, ledgers and projections interpret these bases but do not author, select or enlarge the outcome.
semantic.label: Selected outcome and admitted bounded basis

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.definition: Four separate authority functions: synthesize_model takes IntentLineage, prior ProductAssetModel and admitted product truth and produces ProductAssetModel; eval_gap takes ProductAssetModel, RuntimeEventLog, RuntimeProjection and Worksite and produces ObservationSnapshot and GapPressureRow; evaluate_next takes NextActionBasis, fresh eval_gap, TargetObligationBinding, ActionCatalog and Policy and produces PriorityProjection, NextActionProjection and selected_action, plus its own core result for typed no-action; evaluate_action takes ConstructionIntent, AdmittedEvidence, TargetObligationBinding and Policy and produces EdgeFulfillmentLedger and EdgeClosureDecision.
semantic.label: Model synthesis and three evaluation functions

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.definition: The governed work pair comprises mutable workspace W and immutable ledger L of closure-relevant work over W, anchored and ordered by immutable event spine E. Evaluator work Ev evaluates declared L snapshots. L records admitted callout basis, observed deltas, file refs, digests, execution evidence, touched obligations, claims, evaluator inputs/outputs and admission status, rather than copying W. Ledger attention is a structural analogy: typed, immutable, lineage-constrained, policy-bounded and replayable, without a transformer-attention implementation dependency.
semantic.label: Workspace, ledger and evaluator attention

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.5D Constructive evaluation and yield loop

semantic.definition: The closed closure-decision vocabulary is close, yield, retry, repair, re-enter, reprice and block. These evaluate the predicate that the edge's obligations are fulfilled on the exact basis. Cause refinements map each refined value to exactly one core result without adding decisions or core values. Selection results evaluate whether a published lawful action can be selected for the current gap on the exact basis. Candidate availability, candidate acceptance and edge fulfillment are distinct predicates; ACTIVATION acceptance dispositions accept, local_repair, re_enter and reject are not closure decisions.
semantic.label: Closure, selection, availability and acceptance results

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.6 Product-specific semantics sit above the shared carrier

semantic.definition: ODD supplies structural product shape; each domain product owns its asset meanings, proof lanes and query overlays. The same structural law can build different domain products.
semantic.label: Structural profile and product semantic law

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7 Manual walkthrough must still be lawful

conditions: The operator uses only declared authority surfaces.
semantic.definition: A manual walkthrough identifies current asset/node state, the next lawful vector and its public graph-function carrier, required inputs/evaluators/output contract/carried environment, constructs or assesses the next asset/checkpoint, and repeats to target-relative closure. A vector is the constitutional transition contract; its graph function is the published constructive program realizing it.
semantic.label: Lawful manual traversal

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7A Conforming agentic development

semantic.definition: Agentic conformance has two halves: an F_P walkthrough proves the constitutional process can be followed on real work from declared authority, and an F_D deterministic gate admits produced artifacts. The walkthrough covers intake triage, smallest lawful re-entry, specification/requirement/design/ticket chain, constructive evaluation and closure proof. A minimal authority packet carries input/output contract, required context, role, evaluator regime, provenance and the smallest sufficient declared authority with source refs.
semantic.label: Agentic walkthrough and artifact admission

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.7B Real authority-path negative proof (STDO-UP-010)

conditions: Applies to an ODD or graph-native boundary.
semantic.definition: Real authority-path negative proof exercises the supported Product authority path. Closure-grade evidence identifies entry and authority, invalidates the actual authority-bearing input, exercises that path, proves refusal before the prohibited effect and establishes that no legacy, fallback, reconstruction or parallel path succeeds. Source, packaged, installed and runtime absence are distinct claims.
semantic.label: Real authority-path negative proof

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.8 Cumulative environment law is mandatory

semantic.definition: Graph composition uses a cumulative typed environment. A later function can require any typed binding available in that carried environment. Each retained GraphFunction should declare environment.requires, environment.provides and environment.carries.
semantic.label: Cumulative typed environment

grounds.heading: ODD/11. Core law/11.9 Global convergence must be stable under zoom

semantic.definition: Global convergence requires lawful inner closure, preservation of the enclosing coarse contract after fold-back and agreement between zoomed and unzoomed open/closed status. Current requirement proof is proof-lane aware: a governed realized witness appropriate to the requirement class is required; realized testcases or archived test evidence are the usual immediate pressure for an active software line.
semantic.label: Global convergence under refinement

semantic.definition: Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces. A bundle should identify the exercised feature/use-case boundary, pre-existing assets, expected vectors, significant paths and closure evidence. Declared scenarios and use cases are preferred sources for selecting significant code/control proving paths because they pressure feature intent and design decisions.
semantic.label: Scenario bundle

conditions: The product has an installable development form.
semantic.definition: Installed-development proof is decisive proof run against that installed form in isolation. For graph-native ODD products the proving lane should exercise installation, project bootstrap, graph traversal, evidence collection and target-relative closure. ASSURANCE §5 owns this rule.
semantic.label: Installed-dev proof

semantic.definition: ODD dogfooding is development through the graph-native method the product provides, increasingly using explicit assets, vectors, graph functions, scenario bundles and target-relative closure.
semantic.label: ODD dogfooding

semantic.definition: Release versions belong to release process/metadata, not constitutional graph truth. Graph-native method concerns current assets, vectors, closures and authority; immutable RC publication, version-line selector advancement and exact-cut acceptance belong to the separate RELEASE process surface.
semantic.label: Graph truth and release process boundary

conditions: An agent or designer is instructed to build a product using ODD.
semantic.definition: The expected invocation sequence is: read SPEC_METHOD; read an existing product-specific method; read local Intent, Product, relevant requirements and active design; identify source-to-outcome semantic chain, typed assets and public graph functions; define the machine-readable catalogue; define/update GTL outer callable carriers and live traversal boundaries; define scale-consistent coarse/inner/proof closure; complete the execution-authority audit for affected runtime/plugin/worker/event/projection/assurance/closure/continuation surfaces; define the constructive loop and closure vocabulary including lawful yield; define projection/query over admitted history with source coherence; only then implement code, policy and transport.
semantic.label: ODD product-authoring sequence

grounds.heading: ODD/18. Cold-start reading order/General ODD product

conditions: Starting cold in a concrete ODD product.
semantic.definition: Cold-start reading is ordered. General route: SPEC_METHOD; ODD; product stdo_<label>.json; applicable bound project reference-frame basis and authorized activation packet; bound Intent; bound Product; relevant bound requirements; active bound design; GTL module, catalogue and queries. World-model route inserts WORLD_MODEL after ODD, uses relevant bound requirement families and current bound design, and includes the proof lane with the final GTL/catalogue/query surfaces. ODD sets structural expectations, the product method sets domain law and local surfaces set the current build line. Skipping the order usually risks missing domain meaning or realizing it through the wrong carrier.
semantic.label: General and world-model cold-start routes

semantic.definition: ODD's canonical compression describes graph-native GTL/ABG product authoring: typed assets, named functions, published catalogue, operative GTL module, ABG execution authority, one constructive loop, current-state projections over constructive history, lawful manual explainability, outcome-first framework realization and agentic walkthrough plus deterministic admission. It is a derived acquisition surface with no determination of its own; its declared sources are same-digest §§1, 2, 11.1–11.5D, 11.7 and 11.7A.
semantic.label: ODD derived canonical compression

semantic.definition: POSTING_GUIDE owns the governed project's commentary layer: post purpose, authority boundary, location, identity, categories, structure, discussion state, posting rules and ratification. It consumes PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8 ticketing.comments, TICKETS §1 work carriers, SPEC_METHOD §2 authority surfaces and EVALUATION §1 claims/evidence without redefining them; SPEC_METHOD §6 owns shared-method adoption. Clauses cite FOUNDATIONS principles P0–P6.
semantic.label: POSTING_GUIDE

semantic.definition: A post is working commentary for analysis, criticism, proposed changes, handoff or repricing confidence. It may influence later specification/design but is not constitutional truth. Its category is one of REVIEW (critique), STRATEGY (proposed technical/method direction), GAP (precise insufficiency/contradiction), SCHEMA (data/event/interface/contract shape), HANDOFF (bounded context/task-state transfer) or MATRIX (explicit decision-option comparison).
semantic.label: Post and category vocabulary

semantic.definition: A post carrier is bound by ticketing.comments.root, defaulting locally to .ai-workspace/comments/<agent>/. Default file identity is YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS_CATEGORY_SUBJECT.md; 20260327T120000_REVIEW_bootloader-boundary.md is an example, not a required post. Non-file carriers preserve equivalent stable identity, publication time, category, subject, author, discussion state and supersession history.
semantic.label: Commentary carrier and post identity

semantic.definition: The post template has title CATEGORY: Subject; Author; ISO 8601 Date; Addresses identifying the artifact/issue/boundary; Status initially Draft; optional ISO 8601 Updated; Summary; Analysis; and Recommended Action. MATRIX uses a central decision table instead of free prose. Discussion states are Draft (author shaping), Open (published active discussion) and Closed (discussion concluded).
semantic.label: Post structure and discussion state

semantic.definition: PRODUCT_DEFINITION is a tier-2 member owning project binding through the overlay, definition relations, constitutional-set sufficiency, installed release/toolchain management, semantic resolution, local binding, collective frame basis, WHAT/HOW/work carriers, discovery/composition, conformance cases, STDO-SURFACE-001 and bootstrap. It consumes tier-1 FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION without adding tier-1 definitions. Its contexts are product-definition-routing (§§1–4, 9, 12), semantic-resolution (§§5, 6, 10) and build-tenancy (§8). Generic WHAT/HOW, lineage, build-tenant, release and assurance law remain with the cited owners. Its schemas/templates/filenames/fields/commands are Product realization shapes accepted as interoperability boundaries, not profile terms.
semantic.label: PRODUCT_DEFINITION member

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
semantic.definition: The product-definition-routing context, urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing, owns overlay, definition, discovery, locator and composition meanings. A product definition is a JSON locator/relation overlay for one continuing product WHAT, independent of existing layout. Its definition root is its containing directory; relative URI references resolve against the definition file's retrieval URI. product.source_project locates a source-project root that may be elsewhere. The conventional filename is stdo_<label>.json, with stdo_default.json the single-definition source-project default.
semantic.label: Product definition overlay

semantic.definition: Definition Label is a stable lowercase ASCII-letter/digit/hyphen/underscore discovery label unique only within a directory, not Product identity. Product-Definition Identity is product.definition_id, a stable URI for the mutable definition line, unique within the discovered workspace definition set. Immutable Products/releases retain separate identities. The normative JSON schema is schemas/product-definition.schema.json and the single fill-in form is templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json; they standardize identity/location/relation/discovery fields without absorbing referenced meaning.
semantic.label: Definition identities, schema and template

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/1. Overlay and layout independence/Foundation to law: binding a project to the method

semantic.definition: F12 traces project-binding rules to foundational commitments plus instance premises: independent project authorities; chosen existing layout; shared workspace/machine; recurring terms with different context meanings; and immutable released method versions selected, installed and replaced by projects. P1, P2, P3 and P6 are independent; P0 is recovered; P5 derives from P0/P6 with the open-world premise; P4b derives from P0/P2 with the premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable. The family traces imports without owning that law, distinguishes consequences from member-owned interoperability/domain choices and supplies a per-row consumer-locus index.
semantic.label: F12 foundation-to-law family

semantic.definition: A Constitutional Set is the complete selected governing document set for a product, with no prescribed file count. It collectively makes recoverable axioms (starting truths, invariants, refusal conditions), ontology (real kinds, identities, relations, boundaries, lifecycle), epistemology (evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification, acceptability and decision authority), taxonomy (classifications preventing category collapse), and semantics (governed meanings of terms, relations, states, operations and outcomes). These are sufficiency dimensions, not filename classes or folders.
semantic.label: Constitutional Set

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

conditions: Within product-definition-routing.
semantic.definition: Installed Release Basis is the pair of immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI and installed-manifest SHA-256. The URI identifies an annotated immutable RC cut; the deterministic manifest binds tag object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. Its schema is schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json. The manifest is transport/integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution.
semantic.label: Installed Release Basis

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

semantic.definition: An Adoption Plan is a read-only deterministic acceptance object binding current Product Definition identity/bytes/current basis to one resolved immutable target cut, tag object, commit, tree and manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is an operator-presentable acceptance token, whose possession alone grants no authority. A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorized fleet root and the complete ordered per-definition plan-digest set.
semantic.label: Adoption and Fleet Adoption Plans

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager

semantic.definition: The STDO Toolchain Manager is a bounded executable realization that installs each immutable cut once in a shared versioned store, resolves logical release URIs to verified bytes, inventories/verifies complete distributions, synchronizes selected exact bases, plans and explicitly acceptedly performs adoption, manages declared marker-bounded agent bootstrap and applies operations to an explicitly discovered fleet. The store registry maps release URIs to paths/digests and owns neither Product selection nor method meaning.
semantic.label: STDO Toolchain Manager

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

semantic.definition: A Complete Consumer Update Plan binds one explicitly selected Product Definition and the complete companion population of one exact upstream release-matched cohort to owner-selected consumer bindings. Its invocation/plan/result are operation evidence, not a persistent dependency declaration, registry or lock. cohort-update presents a whole plan binding effect destinations, preimages, exact cohort bytes, companion tags/commits/subtrees/inventories, replacement dependency locators, native routes and declared derived-source observations. Product Definition owns composition; upstream cohort and Product release records own release/member identities.
semantic.label: Complete consumer update

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update

semantic.definition: Toolchain outcomes are cause-refined core results for separate predicates: external effect occurrence; lawful admission/activation on an exact subject and basis; candidate availability after commencement; and a read-only command's own evaluated condition. Completion status, effect-end establishment, refusal cause and partial effects remain distinct data.
semantic.label: Toolchain effect and refusal result domains

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
semantic.definition: Semantic-resolution law is owned in urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution. A term is a lexical label in an occurrence. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope whose vocabulary, concepts and relations are jointly interpretable under named authority. A concept reference exactly locates an authority-owned meaning on a selected basis without minting meaning or authority. Every material occurrence's semantic address is (term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope).
semantic.label: Bounded-context semantic resolution

semantic.definition: Four owner-authorized cross-context relation kinds: Semantic Import applies unchanged source meaning in declared target scope under FOUNDATIONS import law; Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import; Semantic Equivalence is an equality established by governing authorities while both concepts retain owners/contexts and neither adopts the other's meaning; Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating alternatives, using a declared import/translation/equivalence if the selected meaning is external. Specialisation is directional translation preserving declared source meaning while narrowing admissible instances or adding target constraints.
semantic.label: Semantic relations and specialisation

semantic.definition: Local constitutional entries locate local axioms, overrides and disambiguations whose authority belongs to an existing lawful owner. A local disambiguation carrier owns the resolution; overlay metadata only makes its exact context, candidates, selected concept, bases, authority and scope discoverable/checkable.
semantic.label: Local constitutional binding

semantic.definition: A Project Reference-Frame Basis is a Product-owned accepted declaration of the shared frame set through which finite actors engage a governed scope/outcome. It binds exact frame law and optional profile basis, admitting authorities/scopes, frame declarations/evaluation inventory, actor-binding rules/capability envelopes, semantic/evaluation/operation/decision grants, result/conjunction/translation/coverage relations, lifecycle triggers and invalidation. REFERENCE_FRAME supplies principles/declaration shape and the Executive baseline supplies an optional profile; Product authority owns the concrete declaration and every grant.
semantic.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

semantic.definition: Agent Frame Activation is an execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable frame/configuration, exact evaluation, subject, basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope. Its packet is carried by a ticket or other authorized work instruction, while the Product Definition locates the durable shared frame basis. Profile availability, Product adoption and execution activation are distinct relations.
semantic.label: Agent Frame Activation

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/8. WHAT, HOW and work carriers

conditions: Under the selected complete STDO basis.
semantic.definition: The build-tenancy context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy. Build tenancy is one constitutional WHAT realized by one or more independent project-owned HOW tenants: one is the singleton case; multiple independent realizations of the same WHAT constitute multi-build-tenancy. SPEC_METHOD §11 owns build-tenant meanings/bindings, and TICKETS §4 owns the multi-tenant work-item relation through explicit owner relations.
semantic.label: Build tenancy

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/8. WHAT, HOW and work carriers

semantic.definition: Tenant Registry is canonical how.build_tenants, identifying independent HOW realizations by stable identity and locating roots/design/implementation; tenant surfaces declare bindings under SPEC_METHOD §11. how.common locates common realization law explicitly adopted across multiple tenants. WHAT bindings locate current Intent, Product and specifications. ticketing.goals locates the work wave; ticketing.tickets locates durable tickets with backlog/active/completed lanes; ticketing.comments locates commentary; optional ticketing.sprints locates bounded execution-batch manifests.
semantic.label: WHAT, tenant registry and work-carrier bindings

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

semantic.definition: A mutable Product Definition discovered as stdo_*.json within a selected workspace boundary, including its root and arbitrarily deep project roots. Its stable product.definition_id is distinct from its locator and from immutable Product or release identities.
semantic.label: Product Definition

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

semantic.definition: An explicit directed composition entry containing product_definition as target locator, target_definition_id as expected stable identity, relation as the authority defining composition kind, source and target roles, owner, scope, lifecycle and invalidation, and contracts as one or more exact governing interface, capability, identity, lifecycle, data, evidence or other contract references consumed by the relation.
semantic.label: Explicit product composition

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition

semantic.definition: The discovered definition set is a conformance subject with separate structural and semantic claims. Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema establishes structural shape; required semantic and cross-file checks remain separate.
semantic.label: Discovered-set conformance

semantic.definition: Semantic-resolution conformance covers uniquely resolved occurrences and material collisions under an exact selected basis. Its named collision cases are Frame, Owner, Product, Tenant and User.
semantic.label: Semantic-resolution conformance

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

semantic.definition: One complete released version is the operative shared methodology and sole publication authority. Its cut identifies the exact member set, member digests, review basis, human acceptance and immutable identity. Each law has one owning member; other members consume it by reference.
semantic.label: Released method cut

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

semantic.definition: Compressions, templates, comments, candidate work, installed copies and mutable source are derived, evidential or authoring surfaces. Released or installed derived carriers include bootstraps, indexes and projected frames; they preserve source meaning without acquiring ownership.
semantic.label: Derived methodology surface

grounds.heading: PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary

semantic.definition: Consumer-owned concrete Product realisation comprises instantiated types and schemas, files, tools, runtime, orchestration machinery, tests and executable conformance implementation. The method instead owns construction algebra, authority relations, abstract states and transitions, admissibility, necessary causal order and evidence invariants.
semantic.label: Concrete Product realisation

semantic.definition: The source-described bootstrap begins every product from templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json copied from its exact selected cut to its definition root as stdo_default.json for a singleton default project or stdo_<label>.json for a named definition. This is a represented adoption procedure, not an execution by this interpretation.
semantic.label: Product bootstrap

semantic.definition: The starter scaffold binds the shared versioned store through constitution.stdo.basis; specification/GOALS.md to work-wave orientation; INTENT.md to domain direction; PRODUCT.md to current product definition; requirements/ to live requirements; build_tenants/ to shared and tenant-local realisation; and .ai-workspace/ to sprint, ticket and comment carriers. The depicted children are build_tenants/common and default, and .ai-workspace/sprints, tickets/backlog, active, completed, and comments. These paths and topology are defaults, not universal path or conformance law.
semantic.label: Default scaffold and carriers

semantic.definition: PROFILES is a tier-3 member owning the core/profile boundary, declared-binding rule and common import rule, and indexing profiles. A profile is a domain or operational specialisation; tiers 1 and 2 are the core.
semantic.label: PROFILES member and profile category

semantic.definition: The tier-1 and tier-2 core names no runtime, carrier or executor. Its calculus vocabulary includes traversal records and functor kinds F_D, F_P and F_H owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5; module is a generic ASSURANCE term. These are not excluded by the profile vocabulary boundary.
semantic.label: Method core

semantic.definition: A profile's declared binding specialises a core mechanism with explicit direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. It differs from Product adoption binding under PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7 and carrier-to-typed-contract binding under UX §7; the three senses are not interchangeable.
semantic.label: Declared profile binding

semantic.definition: Graph execution is indexed through two tier-3 owning members. ODD binds the P0 bounded step to one vector or edge traversal; supplies graph-native F_P, F_D and F_H shorthands, with F_P and F_H declared specialisations of SPEC_METHOD §5; and refines ACTIVATION §4 to graph functions with §11.8's cumulative-environment contract for earlier outputs. TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE supplies an optional closed model-family signature over one exact a_c basis for immutable occurrence histories over a mutable subject, with OP-001 to OP-007. ODD §10 owns runtime/product/service layer separation; ODD §5 leaves worker internal solution strategy outside the framework.
semantic.label: Graph-execution profiles

semantic.definition: DESIGN_MODULE imports the core and binds ontology-first derivation of operation identities from discovered functionality through logical completeness, Prime contraction, irreducible architectural carriers and projections; proportional sequencing and a decision-complete gate; bounded frame conservation; native constructability; capability and foundation selection; transformation admission completeness; invariant reconstruction; computational realisation projection; module taxonomy and realisation rules; and review questions/checklists. ASSURANCE §§14–16 own design-to-module evidence, module-derived unit tests and lifecycle confirmation; SPEC_METHOD §2 owns its core rule and non-goals. DESIGN_MODULE §§5 and 7 decide per-boundary derivation cost.
semantic.label: Software-design profile

conditions: Applies as a refinement of DESIGN_MODULE to modules realising a UX surface.
semantic.definition: UX imports the core and binds the Elm process model's typed State, Msg, Update, View, Cmd and Sub; UX-message/admitted-carrier boundary; state transition law; effect membrane; AssetSurface or equivalent typed-contract binding; continuation and Msg-replay proof; view shape; shared types with runtime validation at untrusted seams; accessibility minimum; realisation discretion; adoption scaffold/exemption law and UX sprint compliance escrow; failures and review questions; and result refinements each mapped to one core value. Its lead declares the binding of TICKETS §3's generalised escrow terms.
semantic.label: UX profile

semantic.definition: WORLD_MODEL imports the core and binds product-lineage concepts and Builder Project specialisation; a candidate-status Markov-object construct with effective blanket, working refinements, epistemic status and promotion gate; claims and units; entity recovery and the published identity-bearing entity cut with admissibility, discrimination and publication law; attribute ledger; representation/materialisation/publication laws; Markov-object overlays; saturation; local-artifact composition; projection; control/data planes; proof and world-model-driven development; and result refinements each mapped to one core value. Its lead binds FOUNDATIONS §2 Object and P3's boundary claim to the entity cut. Nothing in the core depends on establishment of the construct.
semantic.label: World-model profile

conditions: Adoption is optional.
semantic.definition: EXECUTIVE_BASELINE imports the core and describes one executive configuration under ACTIVATION §1, comprising Executive, Worker and Reviewer engagement frames and a specialist-frame catalogue mapped to tiers 1 and 2. Frame names bind responsibilities allocated by that configuration under Roles and delegation, not roles imported by spelling.
semantic.label: Engagement-baseline profile

semantic.definition: The subject's STDO V3 methodology addresses construction and evaluation by actors with finite context, attention, time and capability: interpret a scoped subject, select purpose and governing contract, transform within admitted authority while conserving material relations, evaluate resulting claims, then continue, recover or conclude from current state under explicit uncertainty.
semantic.label: Subject methodology

semantic.definition: An ordered reading-route index, not an execution grant. Routes are: understand→FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS, SPEC_METHOD; bind a project→SPEC_METHOD §1 then PRODUCT_DEFINITION; realise WHAT→SPEC_METHOD §11 then PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8; triage→SPEC_METHOD §§4–5 then TICKETS §4; migrate/reset→SPEC_METHOD §7 then TICKETS §6; prove realisation→EVALUATION §§1–2,6 then ASSURANCE; model/project/encode→AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §§2–4,6–8 then EVALUATION §2; bounded work→ACTIVATION §§1–3, FOUNDATIONS §4 result mapping, REFERENCE_FRAME §11 then SPEC_METHOD §4; frame-set work→REFERENCE_FRAME §§4,8,10 then EVALUATION §7; resume→ACTIVATION §§5,7 then TICKETS §7; carry work→TICKETS §§5,4,7; review→EVALUATION including §5 then nearest CONFORMANCE case; acceptance/release→EVALUATION §5, SPEC_METHOD §6, RELEASE §§8–9; publication/qualification/selection→RELEASE §§1–4 then PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4; identity→IDENTITY §§2–4,8,10,6 and boundary/sufficiency rules with or without WORLD_MODEL; coordinate→ACTIVATION configuration then, if executive configuration is chosen, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §§3,7,6,12,16; software design→DESIGN_MODULE §§5–7,11 then ASSURANCE §§14–16; profiles→PROFILES §§1–6 with UX §§4,8,12 or WORLD_MODEL §§7,9–10 as applicable; ODD construction→ODD §§17–18; occurrence histories→TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE authority/adoption; specification writing→WRITING_GUIDE then SPEC_METHOD §2; publish analysis/review/handoff/proposal→POSTING_GUIDE then SPEC_METHOD §6; locate term→GLOSSARY including §17 then PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5; trace commitments→FOUNDATIONS §3 then indexed family table; acquire context→ACTIVATION §2, preferring a current derived surface that serves the task, otherwise deciding owner sections, including verbatim frames or current a_c constraint projections.
semantic.label: Ordered task reading routes

semantic.definition: The document catalogue attributes ownership, without supplying the referenced laws. Tier 1: FOUNDATIONS—standing, ontology/imports, P0–P6, foundation-to-law, composition/conservation, results/conjunction, categorical demonstration and hypotheses; REFERENCE_FRAME—frame context/imports, RF-001–017, sets/functions/outcomes, conjunction/relations, coverage/revision, packets/declarations; ACTIVATION—bounded steps, intake/admission/applicability/configuration/delegation, context/acquisition/size, result refinements/disposition, totality/hard stops/licensing, restart/accounts, proportionality and reuse; AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS—signature, records, AC-001–020, traversals/functors, interpretation/models/layers/identity, exclusions/conformance; IDENTITY—scoping, uniqueness/type/stability, readable/opaque/hierarchical/engine/domain identities, authority conservation, overrides/publication, parsing/version boundary/questions/examples; EVALUATION—claims/evidence/independent assessment/review/acceptance, realisation conformance/equivalence and actual-use frame/method qualification. Tier 2: SPEC_METHOD—process constitution/identity, constitutional chain and surfaces, requirements/classification/trace/lifecycle/immutability, outcome conservation, triage/classes/gates/sprints/carriers, ambiguity, lineage/releases/migrations, execution/priorities/ADRs; PRODUCT_DEFINITION—overlay, required relations, constitutional sufficiency, installed basis/manager, semantic resolution, local bindings, frame basis, WHAT/HOW/work, discovery/composition, conformance cases, singular surface and bootstrap; ASSURANCE—verification/taxonomy/portability, test authority/scenarios/installed proof/path coverage, testing frames/combinatorics/debt/evidence, acquisition/localisation/integration, module evidence/tests/lifecycle; TICKETS—goals/tickets/sprints/comments/contracts/milestones, layout/substitution, escrow, fields/classification/triage/status, admission/criteria/terms, migration, judgments/rulings/closure/test authority, recommended shapes and operating relations; RELEASE—identities/refs/subtrees/history, construction/publication/qualification/advancement, selectors/adoption/naming, assets/cohorts, acceptance/dependencies, successor conservation and open questions; CONFORMANCE—qualification cases and discriminator distinctions/routes. Tier 3: PROFILES—boundary/import rule/index; EXECUTIVE_BASELINE—optional executive configuration, roles/frames/duties/drift locks, specialist families, transitions/handoff/coverage/re-entry/adoption/qualification/failures; DESIGN_MODULE—optional design profile, closure/ingress, functional bias/typing, derivation/completeness/conservation/Prime, gates/projections/taxonomy/realisation/review/adoption; ODD—graph profile, libraries/model/compute, product/self-host boundaries/layers/governance, laws, execution audit, constructive loop, cumulative environment, proof/release/failures/invocation/ramp-up; TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE—optional mutable-subject occurrence profile, signature/reference domains/events/relations/constraints/judgments/residuals/stops, identity/admission/causality/lineage/effects/frontiers, OP laws/adoption/exclusions/conformance; UX—optional Elm/carrier/state/effect/continuation/type/accessibility/adoption/escrow/review/result profile; WORLD_MODEL—optional Builder/candidate Markov/entity-cut/ledger/overlay/composition/projection/planes/proof/result profile. Guides: POSTING_GUIDE—commentary purpose/boundary/location/identity/categories/structure/discussion/rules/ratification; WRITING_GUIDE—writing discipline, style, authority-layer tone and artifact/current-surface practice; GLOSSARY—non-deciding locator index by bounded context or undeclared context.
semantic.label: Document tiers and ownership catalogue

semantic.definition: Task excerpts in frames/, inventoried by frames/FRAME_INPUTS.json, copy needed owner sections byte for byte and cite source digests; they own no determination. Indexed tasks: bootstrap—unspecified-task entry, basis/definition/admission/results/acquisition; rf-task-a—declare/activate/evaluate one frame and distinguish result from owner disposition; rf-task-b—coverage, diagnosis and revision; ac-task-a—transformation record, successor judgment and promotion; traversal-task-f—causality/corrections/lineage/precedence/stops; eb-task-d—Executive drift locks, candidate_ready, finding dimensions and disposition; dm-task-d—accepted/new boundary design completeness, sequencing, gate/promotion/retained code/substrate/Prime; configuration—multi-actor configuration, capabilities/capacities and optimality/check claims; binding—software/human-process tenants, author/actor/operation distinctions, structural versus conformance results; stale-summary—workspace disagreement, changed-dependency reuse and next action; acceptance-release—assessment, blocking findings/disposition, condition closure, exact-cut acceptance and successor dispositions; member-build-assess—family table, ownership/refinement, predecessor claims and local discriminators without substituting self-review for independent review.
semantic.label: Task-frame excerpt catalogue

semantic.definition: A selectable STDO Product's constitutional member set is one complete immutable standards cut. A cut carries tiers 1–2, carrier-neutral a_c theory separate from subject models and encodings, optional application-neutral TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE on an exact basis, derived application profiles, companion guides, non-deciding GLOSSARY, task frames with source identity and permitted excerpt transformations, normative interoperability schemas including definition overlay and deterministic installed manifest, and starter product/specification/frame-basis/agent-bootstrap templates. It may also carry subordinate executable and interaction tooling.
semantic.label: Release library and installed distribution

semantic.definition: The tier-1 REFERENCE_FRAME member owns engagement laws: declaring/selecting frame sets, frame relations and joint use, bounded workspace coverage audits, revision and activation packets. It imports frame objects, activating steps, core results/conjunction and qualification unchanged from their owners. Each clause names its requiring principle P0–P6.
semantic.label: REFERENCE_FRAME member

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit

conditions: Human, agentic, deterministic, probabilistic, assurance or mixed work is covered wherever its governing product or method permits it.
semantic.definition: A reference frame is one atomic engagement unit activated and evaluated as a bounded context. An activated frame combines declared evaluation family, exact workspace/topology basis, finite material relations/coordinates, invariants/authorities, admissible evidence/exclusions and actor envelope, leading to one closed core result when evaluation is performed. Engagement atomicity does not imply semantic irreducibility. The member owns urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation under its exact publication basis, with local frame declaration/activation/evaluation/basis/relation/result/coverage/revision/qualification concepts and unchanged owner-defined imports.
semantic.label: Reference frame and activated frame

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit

semantic.definition: A declared frame set supports bounded evaluations of a workspace and governed outcome using accumulated practice/failures, available actor capability and human judgment; required conjunction/translation leads to a coverage ledger, residual uncertainty and empirical revision. Selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are distinct functions, not implied callable interfaces.
semantic.label: Frame set

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit/Imports into this context

semantic.definition: The reference-frame context declares lossless imports from FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION; these sources declare no bounded-context identity, so each source context is its member. FOUNDATIONS supplies frame objects, ontology, authority kinds/actor identity, disjointness/independence, the tuple ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩, core results including non-performance and refinements, and result conjunction/composition. ACTIVATION supplies intake/admission/applicability/context size/activation/evaluation, step result refinements/disposition and closed-result reuse. EVALUATION supplies frame/method qualification.
semantic.label: Declared reference-frame imports

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit/Foundation to law

semantic.definition: Family F1, frames and context, traces bounded-frame engagement across this member, ACTIVATION §2 and FOUNDATIONS §2 frame objects, authorities, independence and tuple. The table owns none of the rules it names. Instance premises are workspace material exceeding one actor's competence/context/tools/access; declared outcome questions; possibly overlapping frames/actors; changing workspace/topology/capabilities; and actor use of owning and derived sources. These are work conditions, not foundational commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are cited as independent; P4b is derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; P5 is derived from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. P0 also includes actor change with declared-source reacquisition rather than private memory. Rows distinguish consequences, owning rules, additional choices/owners and pillars; RF-012 and result mappings are traced in F3, imports in F12. Core claims and violation lists add no independent rules.
semantic.label: F1 frames-and-context foundation table

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/1. The frame as the engagement unit/Foundation to law

semantic.definition: Coverage is an audit relative to an exact workspace, governed outcome, basis, evaluation inventory, frame set and time. Its ledger and statuses concern coverage predicates and are distinct from results of the covered evaluations. Operational full coverage remains relative to that tuple and an explicit residual boundary.
semantic.label: Frame coverage audit

conditions: Evaluation is performed.
semantic.definition: A frame evaluation returns one closed result in its declared algebra: the FOUNDATIONS §4 core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, or a refinement mapped into that algebra. The owning core meanings and standing are imported, not redefined by REFERENCE_FRAME.
exceptions: An evaluation not performed has no evaluation result; its stop state belongs to ACTIVATION §3.
semantic.label: Frame result domain

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/3. Laws/Engagement atom and semantic atom

semantic.definition: A semantic atom concerns irreducible meaning; an engagement atom concerns one bounded activation/evaluation. One frame may contain several semantic atoms and one semantic atom may participate in several frames. An adopting domain method's semantic-contraction law governs its domain atom family, not frame-set contraction by default.
semantic.label: Semantic atom

semantic.definition: A declared bounded evaluation family with stable local identity; subject and exact basis; material manifold; coordinates and equality; invariants; authorities; admissible evidence; capability envelope; boundaries; optional relations actually used; invalidation and recharting conditions; and qualification cases, counterexamples and residuals.
semantic.label: Reference frame

semantic.definition: A stable locally identified declaration of governed workspace, outcome, basis and time; human declaration and acceptance authority; known evaluation inventory and provenance; selected frame identities, revisions and capability envelopes; coverage mapping; intentional overlap; required conjunction and translation; residual uncertainty; and revision triggers.
semantic.label: Frame set

semantic.definition: Relations distinct from the frame: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame | activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result + evidence + residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision | conflict | indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value | declared_loss | refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. Later text additionally specifies direct core-value returns absent from the signatures.
semantic.label: Method functions

conditions: An evaluation requires the relation.
semantic.definition: Frames act together through four distinct relations: independently activated co-evaluation, result conjunction, evidence or coordinate translation, and material composition.
semantic.label: Frames acting together

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/6. Frames in conjunction/Independently activated co-evaluation

semantic.definition: Several frames may separately activate on the same subject and return closed results, serving assurance independence, different evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives.
semantic.label: Independently activated co-evaluation

semantic.definition: A declared decision rule consumes several frames' closed results using the core conjunction and rule requirements owned by FOUNDATIONS §4. REFERENCE_FRAME defines no separate conjunction.
semantic.label: Result conjunction

grounds.heading: REFERENCE_FRAME/6. Frames in conjunction/Evidence or coordinate translation

semantic.definition: One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another through a translation declaring source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.
semantic.label: Evidence or coordinate translation

conditions: The evaluation requires composition.
semantic.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application with shared invariants, material effect or decision order, closure, failure and conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.
semantic.label: Material composition

semantic.definition: Permitted relation categories: disjoint means no shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations; overlapping shares material variables, evidence or entities; complementary jointly informs one decision through distinct evaluations; alternative evaluates the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves a distinction another frame aggregates; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another domain; translated moves values or evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporally successive evaluates a changed basis later; composed combines frame relations into one governed evaluation or action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where real authority or decomposition exists.
semantic.label: Frame relation categories

semantic.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): workspace W, governed outcome G, exact basis B, known evaluation inventory E, declared frame set S, and the claim's time or immutable checkpoint T.
semantic.label: Coverage basis

semantic.definition: Known material evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, recording provenance and materiality.
semantic.label: Evaluation inventory

semantic.definition: Cross-cutting audit lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/interactions, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression, and actor capability/context fit. A lens becomes a frame only through separate instantiation as a bounded evaluation family.
semantic.label: Coverage dimensions

semantic.definition: Tier-2 particular method owning position/identity, constitutional chain and surfaces, manifesto/litmus tests, requirement/design/trace/live-surface laws, outcome conservation, change management/triage/classification/consistency/sprint boundaries, ambiguity/lifecycle, lineage/release boundary, migration/procedures/design records and build-tenant binding. grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Foundation to law: chain, outcome and build-tenant binding

semantic.definition: Goals orient the current bounded work wave; they do not substitute for requirements.

semantic.definition: Requirements state the full constitutional WHAT as stable obligations with explicit acceptance criteria, sufficient for downstream design derivation.

semantic.definition: Code is executable realisation derived from requirements and design, rather than a source of authority through accidental precedent.

semantic.definition: Reconstruction sufficiency is competent reconstruction of conformant downstream layers in order. It is not determinism and cannot depend on hiding major ambiguity.

semantic.definition: Renewal is the cumulative feedback cycle from current specification through real-world use case and explicit gap analysis to lawful re-entry and forward repricing.

conditions: The tier-3 DESIGN_MODULE profile governs the boundary under its own adoption rule.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Requirement categories and classification
SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Requirement categories and classification

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/2. The chain/Trace closure and anti-drift

conditions: A domain artifact has been published as a live constitutional surface.

conditions: The designed product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface or capability is material.

conditions: The work wave bears a product outcome.

semantic.label: Outcome evidence classes

conditions: Within a product-outcome-bearing work wave.
semantic.definition: Material growth has a live basis in the selected unresolved outcome, an admitted named bounded prerequisite, or an admitted named bounded experiment whose stated observation discriminates a stated decision for that outcome.

semantic.definition: Change management routes reports through intake triage, owning-layer change classification, separation of computed treatment from judgment and owner decisions, and affected-span consistency closure.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Foundation to law: change management and ambiguity

semantic.definition: F11 is the foundation-to-law family accounting for change entry, computed classification and reuse, ambiguity governance and shared-interface migration. semantic.definition: Universal intake triage is the single entry for substantive change, determining substance, affected product boundary/scope, lawful class, re-entry point, affected downstream surfaces/evidence, and release-scope fit or repricing.

semantic.definition: The minimum lawful declared change classes are goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice, design_reframe and realization_refactor. Each identifies changed meaning, lawful re-entry and downstream flow; a declared class is not an evaluation result.
semantic.label: Change classes

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Computed classification and treatment

semantic.definition: Reusable intake classification distinguishes C, reproducible facts and declared-rule application; J, residual semantic/materiality judgment; and O, a ruling reserved to its actual owner. These annotations create no authority, calculus kind, runtime, classifier interface or mandatory document.
semantic.label: Computed classification and C/J/O

semantic.definition: The consistency gate applies the externally owned condition-based closure rule to obligations of a declared change span, requiring upstream sufficiency, downstream consistency and evidence of active intended behaviour.

semantic.definition: A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface under existing constitutional authority, allowing batching, coordination, proof-cost pricing and close review without becoming a constitutional layer.

semantic.definition: Work-carrier selection follows required lifetime: durable ticket for cross-session identity; sprint-local entry for within-batch traceability only; run/return record for one activation.

semantic.definition: The method describes procedures for substantive intake, feature introduction/change, project bootstrap or requirement repricing, and use-case gaps. They preserve triage-first re-entry and downstream consistency.

semantic.definition: The substrate-neutral context urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance progressively narrows goals, direction/scope, product shape/terms, obligations, executable class, structure and local implementation. conditions: Declared policy permits bounded handling of declared ambiguity.
semantic.definition: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing names bounded non-human processing permitted to carry or resolve declared ambiguity. The source also places a person's policy-permitted decision without human-adjudication admission under this processing's policy and recording rules.

conditions: Human judgment is explicitly admitted by authority where policy or risk appetite requires it.

semantic.label: Human adjudication

semantic.definition: Lineage distinguishes substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition. A release cut v<version>-rc.<n> is immutable point-in-time release identity; mutable v<version> is a discovery selector for the highest-ordinal published cut.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/6. Lineage and release/Shared method adoption and propagation (STDO-UP-012)

semantic.definition: Migration is the document's section grouping for changes of constitutional or implementation basis.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/What counts as a core interface

semantic.definition: Two lawful strategies are inside-out hard-break migration on the same implementation line, replacing authoritative source truth from its carrier outward, and fundamental re-adoption for intentional major re-derivation on a materially different implementation basis. semantic.definition: An affected outcome's acceptance path is its full causal closure: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver, fallback, shared state, event, projection and proof surface capable of changing, interpreting or closing it.

grounds.heading: SPEC_METHOD/8. Bounded execution in this method

semantic.definition: Realisation evidence serves existing closure law with authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible and a present-tense statement of residual open pressure.

semantic.definition: TICKETS is the tier-2 owner of the work-carrier model, layout/bindings, sprint/ticket mechanics, triage/class recording/upward propagation, smallest lawful carrier and carrier-side execution-contract admission, execution/verification separation, judgment/ruling continuity, condition-based closure/reuse, test-case authority, migration-ticket rules, one-truth projection, recommended shapes and operating mode. grounds.heading: TICKETS/7. Authority, judgment, closure and state/Condition-based closure and reuse
